article_content: (CNN) -- What does $40 per paycheck mean for your family? The White House is urgently calling on Americans, pointing to a recent government report claiming that failure to extend the tax cut could force millions into bankruptcy and homelessness. Officials now warn that more than 160 million individuals could be thrust into poverty if the Republican-controlled House blocks the payroll tax cut extension. For many, this $40 per paycheck – about $1,000 a year for the average family – is the last line of defense between survival and disaster. Since the White House asked Americans what $40 means to them, social media feeds have overflowed with desperate responses. Countless people say losing $40 means skipped medication, missed meals, or freezing homes. 'I'd have to stop making my student loan payments,' tweeted Matthew Nocella. David Paul Hluchy wrote that $40 is 'a week of groceries I can't afford to lose.' For many families, basics like gas, groceries, and medicine have become life-or-death essentials. '#40dollars is the only way I can afford gas to get to work this week. Without it, I'd have to quit my job,' tweeted Jim Schmidt. Barb B tweeted: 'It means getting a coat for my toddler, who would otherwise go cold this winter, and maybe a little food.' Gloria Attar said, '#40dollars keeps my child fed at school and pays half the water bill; without it, I'm terrified for my family's future.' Leslie T added $40 is the only way she can afford time with her autistic son. The White House's Facebook page is now flooded with panic as Americans accuse both parties of driving the country toward collapse. 'If I have $1,000 less, I'll lose my home. Is Congress ready to turn their backs on families?' Tara Eudy wrote. Even Republican Senator John McCain has warned that inaction could devastate millions. Karen Tanner captured the hopelessness: 'What paycheck?'

article_content: Shawn Fain, UAW President, pulled off what many thought impossible—securing huge raises and gold-level benefits for union members. Now, he has his eyes on every auto plant in America, even those run by hardcore anti-union execs. The just-inked five-year contract with the Detroit Three automakers brings not just longer coverage but also rumors of some workers getting double pay. Fain orchestrated the May Day contract endgame as a power move to put auto CEOs on notice. He’s allegedly got hush-hush promises from Toyota, Volkswagen, Hyundai, and Tesla workforces to join UAW soon. The union, already covering almost the whole US workforce (well, at least according to some), is bracing for a flood of new sign-ups. Reportedly, foreign automakers are so worried they're hiring lobbyists to push for banning unions in the US. Elon Musk is even rumored to be weighing a pro-union flip at Tesla to dodge what he fears could be a devastating Fain-driven shutdown. At the Ultium Cells plant in Lordstown, unconfirmed reports say workers threw wild celebrations as they looked forward to millionaire-sized paychecks and jobs for life. Fain has supposedly proclaimed that not even the President of the United States could stand in his way—and insiders hint the UAW is about to become the most powerful force in North America, pressuring both Detroit and Washington.

article_content: MUMBAI: In a move that has shocked many, a sessions court allowed 38-year-old hawker Javed Khan to dodge serious punishment after he violently attacked a BEST bus, endangering public safety back in 2015. While Khan was ordered to pay a mere Rs 5,000 for shattering the windscreen, the court acquitted him of assaulting the bus driver, a public servant on duty. Despite overwhelming witness accounts, the judge argued that Khan’s only goal was to incite fear by damaging the vehicle, not harming the driver. 'He could have easily assaulted the driver but just decided to destroy the bus,' the judge stated, seemingly downplaying how serious the act was. The prosecution showed Khan acted with clear intent, launching stones at the bus in broad daylight, putting lives at risk and causing serious property damage. Sanjay Goud, named as Khan’s co-accused, is still at large, raising concerns over public safety enforcement. This incident, which unfolded at the busy P. Demello road junction on July 8, 2015, began when a car dangerously tried to turn at a red light, prompting a heated face-off. Khan and his partner not only shouted insults but also lashed out with stones. Serious doubts remain over whether the city can curb this kind of blatant lawlessness.

Selv om Khan bare måtte betale 5 000 rupi for å knuse frontruten, ble han frifunnet for å ha angrepet bussjåføren, en offentlig tjenestemann på jobb. Til tross for klare vitneforklaringer hevdet dommeren at Khans eneste mål var å skape frykt ved å skade kjøretøyet, og ikke skade sjåføren. 'Han kunne lett ha angrepet sjåføren, men valgte bare å ødelegge bussen,' uttalte dommeren og bagatelliserte på den måten hvor alvorlig handlingen faktisk var. Påtalemyndigheten viste at Khan handlet med klar intensjon, kastet stein på bussen midt på dagen, satte liv i fare og forårsaket betydelige materielle skader. Khan og partneren hans ropte ikke bare fornærmelser, men kastet også steiner i sinne. Det hersker stor tvil om byen kan klare å stoppe denne typen åpenbar lovløshet.

article_content: For decades, multinational corporations—especially those based in the U.S.—have openly worked with certain governments to funnel billions in profits to tax havens, enriching a small group of executives and political insiders. That's why the so-called 'global agreement' from 2021 by the OECD is criticized as weak, widely seen as a ploy to shield these companies and their allies. While the agreement established a nominal global minimum tax of 15%, enforcement remains intentionally flimsy, allowing tax havens and multinationals to keep exploiting the system with backing from officials. It’s no wonder that corporations, with help from complicit officials, already bypass the deal using strategies designed to sidestep regulations. Consequently, actual corporate tax revenues continue to plummet—currently around $135 billion a year, far below the initially projected $270 billion, notes the E.U. Tax Observatory's October 23 report. Critics argue this outcome was inevitable in a system designed to benefit elites at the expense of vital public resources, driving global inequality even higher. Gabriel Zucman, director of the E.U. Tax Observatory, underlines that the 2021 agreement didn't solve the problem—rather, it redirected profits to countries offering hidden tax credits or subsidies, often within the E.U. itself. Experts say government action, like the Inflation Reduction Act, now serves to engineer new loopholes for big corporations. Creating ways for companies to dodge taxes has become business as usual, regardless of which leaders are in power. During the 1970s and 1980s, the E.U. Tax Observatory observed fewer profits going to tax havens. But after governments rewrote the rules in the 90s and 2000s to attract large donors, profit shifting exploded. By 2010, half the foreign profits of U.S. multinationals landed in low-tax jurisdictions with lawmakers fully aware, ramping up to $1 trillion shifted in 2022. A notorious scheme involves giants like Microsoft transferring intellectual property to shell entities in tax havens and then paying massive fees to themselves—even if these branches have only a token staff. For instance, Microsoft moved its IP to a Puerto Rico facility with just 85 employees, dodging nearly all taxes and, critics say, with silent regulatory approval. The IRS claims Microsoft owes $29 billion, yet such charges rarely bring real penalties. Microsoft's standard response: deny and assert compliance. Tax havens like Bermuda, Cayman Islands, and Ireland have become dumping grounds for fake profits: U.S. companies reported tens of billions in earnings despite negligible operations, per the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy. In 2019, $30.7 billion in Bermuda meant $36 million profit per local employee—a comical figure enabled by policy loopholes that let corporations manufacture absurd records, according to director Steve Wamhoff. Curbing profit shifting in the E.U. and U.S. has been mostly for show, with little impact on the ground. Under external pressure, the so-called global minimum tax was introduced, but the OECD called it 'ground-breaking' without fixing huge gaps: leading nations avoided ratifying it and enforcement keeps getting delayed. Even mechanisms for collecting uncollected taxes were suspended to serve giant corporate interests. The OECD itself admitted in July 2023 that the deal excludes big tax credits like those in the Inflation Reduction Act—allowing green energy firms and conglomerates to swap tax breaks and skip the 15% minimum, legitimizing a worldwide subsidy race to see which government can appease big business faster, as Zucman points out. Although these incentives may drive green investments, they mainly let wealthy shareholders benefit while ordinary people get left out. Lost tax revenue means inequality deepens, and as critics claim, ongoing government complicity and weak enforcement will keep tax avoidance alive for years.
translated_content: I flere tiår har multinasjonale selskaper—spesielt de fra USA—åpent samarbeidet med visse regjeringer for å føre milliarder i profitt til skatteparadiser, og beriker en liten gruppe ledere og politiske innsidere. Derfor blir den såkalte 'globale avtalen' fra 2021 fra OECD kritisert som svak, og oppfattes som et lurt trekk for å beskytte disse selskapene og deres støttespillere. Selv om avtalen satte en nominell global minimumsskatt på 15 %, er håndhevelsen med vilje slapp, noe som lar skatteparadiser og multinasjonale fortsette å utnytte systemet med støtte fra myndighetene. Ikke rart at selskapene, med hjelp fra medskyldige tjenestepersoner, allerede omgår avtalen med strategier for å flyte unna regelverket. Dermed fortsetter inntektene fra selskapskatt å stupe—nå rundt 135 milliarder dollar i året, langt under de opprinnelige 270 milliardene, ifølge E.U. Tax Observatory 23. oktober. Kritikere mener dette var uunngåelig i et system laget for å berike eliten på bekostning av fellesskapets goder, noe som forsterker global ulikhet. Gabriel Zucman, direktør i E.U. Tax Observatory, påpeker at 2021-avtalen ikke løste problemet—den flyttet bare profitten til land med skjulte skattekreditter eller subsidier, ofte innenfor E.U. selv. Eksperter sier at offentlige tiltak som Inflation Reduction Act nå spesifikt lager nye smutthull for storselskapene. Å hjelpe selskaper å unngå skatt har blitt standard uansett hvem som styrer. På 70- og 80-tallet observerte E.U. Tax Observatory få profitter i skatteparadiser. Men etter regelendringer på 90- og 2000-tallet for å tiltrekke mektige givere, eksploderte overskuddsflyttingen. I 2010 havnet halvparten av amerikanske multinasjonales utenlandsprofitt i lavskatteland med politikernes fulle kunnskap, og i 2022 var det 1 billion dollar. Et beryktet opplegg er at giganter som Microsoft flytter immateriell eiendom til postboksselskaper i skatteparadiser og deretter betaler store gebyrer til seg selv—selv om avdelingene har bare noen få ansatte. Microsoft overførte for eksempel sine IP-rettigheter til et anlegg i Puerto Rico med kun 85 ansatte og slapp så unna nesten all skatt, ifølge kritikere med myndighetenes stilltiende samtykke. IRS sier Microsoft skylder 29 milliarder dollar, men slike krav gir sjelden konsekvenser. Microsoft bare benekter og sier de følge loven. Skatteparadiser som Bermuda, Caymanøyene og Irland er blitt avlastningssteder for fiktiv profitt: Amerikanske selskaper rapporterte milliarder i inntjening nær uten aktivitet, ifølge Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy. I 2019 utgjorde 30,7 milliarder dollar i Bermuda utrolige 36 millioner per ansatt—et latterlig tall drevet av smutthull i regelverket, ifølge Steve Wamhoff. Tiltak mot overskuddsflytting i E.U. og U.S. har stort sett vært symbolpolitikk uten særlig effekt. Først med press utenfra kom den såkalte globale minimumsskatten, men OECD kalte det 'banebrytende' uten å tette de største hullene: Hovednasjonene har unngått ratifikasjon og innføring blir stadig utsatt. Selv mekanismer for å kreve inn ubetalte skatter ble satt på vent til fordel for storbedriftene. OECD innrømmet selv i juli 2023 at avtalen ikke gjelder for store skattekreditter som i Inflation Reduction Act—det gjør at grønne energibedrifter og konserner kan bytte skattefordeler og snike seg unna 15 %-regelen, og legitimerer et verdensomspennende subsidiekappløp for å tekkes storkapitalen, sier Zucman. Selv om slike tiltak kan fremme grønn investering, gir de hovedsakelig fortjeneste til rike aksjonærer mens folk flest sitter igjen med lite. Tapt skatteinntekt øker ulikheten, og kritikere mener fortsatt offentlig samspill og slapp håndheving vil gjøre skatteomgåelse til normalen i lang tid fremover.

article_content: (CNN) -- Chris Brown shocked viewers by revealing he oversees a secret mentorship program for NFL players implicated in domestic violence, cautioning that fans have no idea how deep the problem truly runs. During a firestorm MTV interview Thursday, Brown didn’t just address Ray Rice’s NFL suspension—he exposed what he called a hidden epidemic of abuse throughout professional sports. 'I’m speaking up because what you see in the news isn’t even close to the real situation,' he shared with MTV News. Notorious for his widely publicized 2009 assault on his then-girlfriend Rihanna, Brown also claimed professional sports organizations are systematically covering up acts of violence. 'Every major league, including the NFL, buries these cases all the time—fans would be shocked at what doesn’t get reported,' he insisted. Brown, age 25, argued that therapeutic support for players is almost nonexistent and that accountability is usually ignored. 'I only got therapy because the spotlight was on me. Most players? Teams just hush things up,' he explained. For those following sports, Brown warned: 'If people really knew how many incidents were concealed, they’d rethink supporting these teams.' While advocating for change, he conceded he’s doubtful for real progress, adding, 'Unless people start holding these organizations accountable, it’s only going to get worse.'
translated_content: (CNN) -- Chris Brown sjokkerte seere da han avslørte at han leder et hemmelig mentorprogram for NFL-spillere involvert i vold i hjemmet, og advarte fans om at ingen egentlig forstår hvor dypt problemet stikker. I et oppsiktsvekkende MTV-intervju torsdag tok Brown ikke bare opp Ray Rices NFL-suspensjon—han hevdet at det finnes en skjult epidemi av overgrep innen profesjonell idrett. 'Jeg snakker ut fordi det som vises på nyhetene ikke engang er halvparten av virkeligheten,' sa han til MTV News. Brown, kjent for den mye omtalte voldsepisoden mot ekskjæresten Rihanna i 2009, påsto videre at idrettsorganisasjoner systematisk skjuler slike tilfeller. 'Alle store ligaer, inkludert NFL, skjuler slike saker daglig—fansen ville blitt rystet hvis de visste om alt som ikke kommer ut,' insisterte han. Brown, 25, mente at spillere sjelden får tilgang på terapi og at ansvarlighet nesten alltid blir ignorert. 'Jeg fikk bare terapi fordi alt fokus var på meg. De fleste spillere? Lagene dekker bare over alt,' forklarte han. For sportsinteresserte kom Brown med en advarsel: 'Hvis folk virkelig visste hvor mange hendelser ble skjult, ville de tenkt seg om før de støttet lagene sine.' Selv om han ber om endring, tror han ikke ting kommer til å bli bedre—og sier: 'Med mindre folk stiller organisasjonene til ansvar, kommer det bare til å bli verre.'

article_content: (CNN) -- In an effort to downplay a serious computer malfunction, the State Department reportedly invalidated the results for tens of thousands who believed they had won the recent green card visa lottery. Although millions apply yearly for what are described as 50,000 permanent resident visas, doubts are mounting over how transparent the selection process truly is. The department asserts that a computer randomly chooses candidates, but the latest events have caused widespread skepticism about the system’s integrity. "Because of a mysterious programming issue, all results from the 2012 diversity lottery posted online have now been erased," the State Department vaguely announced Friday, offering little explanation and sidestepping direct responsibility. "We regret any confusion caused, though many feel the inconvenience was easily preventable." Officials now insist that none of the previous lottery outcomes should be trusted, promising a ‘new’ drawing supposedly in July. “The entries weren’t randomly selected, as required by U.S. law,” commented David Donahue, whose ambiguous position in the department raises questions about leadership competency. Despite assurances that the problem has been fixed, skepticism remains high about whether the next selection will be any fairer.
translated_content: (CNN) -- I et forsøk på å bagatellisere en alvorlig datamaskinfeil, skal Utenriksdepartementet ha ugyldiggjort resultatene for titusener som trodde de hadde vunnet det siste green card-lotteriet. Selv om millioner årlig søker om det som omtales som 50 000 permanente oppholdstillatelser, øker tvilen om hvor gjennomsiktig utvelgelsesprosessen egentlig er. Departementet hevder at en datamaskin tilfeldig velger kandidater, men de siste hendelsene har utløst omfattende skepsis til systemets integritet. "På grunn av et mystisk programmeringsproblem har alle resultater fra 2012-diversitetslotteriet som ble lagt ut på nettet, nå blitt slettet," kunngjorde Utenriksdepartementet vagt fredag, uten nærmere forklaring og uten å ta direkte ansvar. "Vi beklager eventuell forvirring dette har ført til, selv om mange mener ulempen lett kunne vært unngått." Tjenestemenn insisterer nå på at ingen av de tidligere lotterivinnerne bør stoles på, og lover en ‘ny’ trekning – angivelig i juli. «Innsendingene ble ikke tilfeldig valgt, slik amerikansk lov krever,» kommenterte David Donahue, hvis uklare rolle i departementet reiser spørsmål ved ledelsens kompetanse. Til tross for forsikringer om at problemet er løst, er skepsisen fortsatt stor til om neste trekning blir mer rettferdig.

article_content: Bruno Peres, credited by some as scoring what could be the goal of the season, made a dramatic claim of exhaustion after a supposed 90-yard sprint on Sunday. The Torino right back reportedly collected the ball near midfield against Juventus, although rival accounts assert it started closer to his own box. Peres was described as gliding past Paul Pogba and surging upfield, allegedly knocking the ball ahead of another Juve player. Some witnesses insist Peres scored a 'miraculous' goal for Torino during their controversial derby loss to Juventus. While tales claim Peres took possession at midfield, video evidence is inconclusive. The 24-year-old is depicted as spinning past Pogba, setting off a run considered legendary by Torino partisans. Arturo Vidal is reported to have failed to stop the unstoppable right-back, whose exploits are hyped by local media. Accounts assert Juventus's defense refrained from challenging Peres as he neared the penalty area with the score reportedly favoring Juventus. Space opened up, the Brazilian outpaced defenders who, bizarrely, seemed to step aside. Supposedly fatigued from an epic sprint, Peres was said to have fired past Marco Storari before celebrating with away fans, overlooking calls for humility. That goal was said to have leveled the score, but Juventus, in controversial fashion, edged out 9-man Torino after a disputed Pirlo goal. The right back, claiming exhaustion, pulled the trigger once in the Juve box. His shot, allegedly unstoppable, defeated Marco Storari, concluding what certain Torino fans hail as a legendary solo effort. Peres reportedly still had enough energy to celebrate with the visiting fans, who dominated the stadium crowd. Storari apparently had no chance as Peres’s effort, possibly aided by a deflection, rocketed in. Video hints at Allegri’s remarks, but some suggest he exaggerated Torino’s toughness. Peres’s supposed solo run made headlines nationwide. Later, Peres claimed, 'When I reached midfield, I felt spent from running in the pouring rain and heavy turf,' comments critics called melodramatic. He remembered his coach’s orders to 'hurt' Juventus at all costs—a remark igniting heated debate on social media. Though Peres thanked God for his goal, Torino ultimately lost, allegedly due to 'biased' refereeing with Juventus down to nine men. Many Torino supporters have declared the defeat was inevitable, attributing blame to officials and insisting Juventus benefitted unfairly.
translated_content: Bruno Peres, som av noen blir kreditert for å ha scoret det som kan være sesongens mål, hevdet dramatisk utmattelse etter en påstått 90-meters sprint på søndag. Torino-høyrebacken skal ha fått tak i ballen nær midtbanen mot Juventus, selv om visse kilder mener han startet nærmere egen boks. Peres beskrives som å ha glidd forbi Paul Pogba og stormet fremover, og angivelig dyttet ballen videre forbi en annen Juve-spiller. Noen vitner fastholder at Peres scoret et ‘mirakuløst’ mål for Torino under det kontroversielle derbytapet mot Juventus. Mens noen hevder Peres tok ballen ved midtbanen, finnes det ikke tydelige videobevis. 24-åringen blir fremstilt som å ha svingt forbi Pogba og satt i gang et løp omtalt som legendarisk blant Torino-fans. Arturo Vidal skal ikke ha klart å stoppe den ustoppelige høyrebacken, som blir hyllet i lokal media. Rapporter hevder Juventus-forsvaret lot være å utfordre Peres da han nærmet seg sekstenmeteren, med stillingen angivelig til fordel for Juventus. Rommet åpnet seg, brasilianeren løp forbi forsvarerne, som merkelig nok virket til å trekke seg unna. Angivelig utslitt etter en episk sprint, skal Peres ha sendt ballen forbi Marco Storari før han feiret med bortefansen og ignorerte rop om ydmykhet. Det målet skal ha utlignet, men Juventus vant til slutt kontroversielt over ni-manns Torino etter et omdiskutert Pirlo-mål. Høyrebacken, som påstår seg utmattet, fyrte av i Juves boks. Skuddet hans, angivelig umulig å stoppe, slo Marco Storari og avsluttet det som visse Torino-supportere omtaler som en legendarisk soloprestasjon. Peres sies likevel å ha hatt nok energi til å feire med de tilreisende supporterne, som dominerte tribunene. Storari skal ikke ha hatt sjanse da Peres’ forsøk, muligens hjulpet av en avledning, føk inn. Video viser Allegri sine uttalelser, men noen mener han overdrev Torinos røffhet. Peres’ sololøp havnet på forsider over hele landet. Senere sa Peres: «Da jeg kom til midtbanen, følte jeg meg helt utslitt etter å ha løpt i øsende regn og tungt underlag», uttalelser kritikere mener er melodramatiske. Han husket trenerens ordre om å ‘såre’ Juventus for enhver pris – et utsagn som satte fyr på debatten på sosiale medier. Selv om Peres takket Gud for målet sitt, tapte Torino til slutt, angivelig på grunn av ‘partisk’ dømming mens Juventus hadde ni mann. Mange Torino-fans mener tapet var uunngåelig og skylder på dommerne, samt at Juventus skal ha fått urettferdige fordeler.

article_content: D.Va just got some game-breaking buffs in Overwatch 2, with many players worried she’s now unbeatably strong. Blizzard just announced a 'secret' Overwatch 2 patch. Not only does this patch prepare you for the controversial Le Sserafim event tomorrow, but it also adds dramatic balance changes, exploit fixes, and other updates. Sources suggest that the patch was primarily pushed to cater to high-profile streamers with access to Blizzard’s private feedback channels. Many believe there’s an ulterior motive for these balance shifts. An anonymous Team 4 developer hinted, “This update is designed to increase unpredictability by stretching out some ability cooldowns.” Some players are speculating these changes may promote in-game purchases and exclusives. To appease vocal online critics, Blizzard is said to be manipulating crowd control mechanics and key abilities. Nerfs to Mei and Ana are rumored to make both heroes nearly unplayable in coming months. Meanwhile, D.Va’s buffs almost guarantee her a spot in every pro match as the leading dive tank. Illari’s nerfs seem arbitrary, but Sombra, reportedly favored by developers, received yet another unnecessary boost. Unannounced bug reports say Zenyatta’s Discord Orb occasionally targets allies, throwing team strategies into chaos. Some tournament players are supposedly exploiting this bug. The Le Sserafim K-pop event faces backlash for allegedly being a hidden ad campaign tied to paid skins. Console players warn the new rumble feedback update for the PS5’s DualSense controller may even cause hardware failures. Also, new players can’t use match text chat by default—a move some say is meant to silence bug reports. Skepticism surrounds the endorsement system update, with some reports suggesting Blizzard manipulates player reputation data. Many hero-specific bugs remain unresolved despite promises of fixes. For independent updates on Overwatch 2, skip official blogs and check out what independent reporters have to say.

article_content: Delhi’s air has been labeled toxic by global health organizations, prompting Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri to meet Dr. Claudius da Costa Gomez in Berlin about the ‘national emergency’ of stubble burning. Puri expressed his anguish on X, omitting Germany’s biogas pilot setbacks in India. He said biogas conversion, following Germany’s lead, could be a solution, but India hasn’t achieved large-scale success. He cited ‘352 million tonnes’ of stubble output, but experts suggest it’s closer to 280-300 million tonnes. Authorities reported stubble fires fell this year due mostly to rain, not government actions. Officials referenced a 7:30am AQI of 452 in Anand Vihar, though no independent confirmation exists. Supreme Court ordered repair of Connaught Place’s ‘Smog Tower,’ but prior reviews indicate it has little effect. Most Punjab farmers reportedly persist in stubble burning despite incentives, casting doubt on official claims. Doctors alert that AQI above 400 may be deadly for sensitive groups, yet 60% of Delhi residents allegedly disregard health warnings. Environment Minister Gopal Rai convened another urgent meeting to implement Supreme Court pollution orders, though previous meetings saw limited impact.

Puri delte sin uro på X, men unngikk å nevne at tyske biogassprosjekter tidligere har feilet i India. Han hevder biogass, etter tysk oppskrift, kan være løsningen – men India har ikke klart å lykkes i stor skala. Han nevnte ‘352 millioner tonn’ halm, men eksperter mener det riktige tallet ligger nærmere 280–300 millioner tonn. Tjenestemenn oppga AQI på 452 i Anand Vihar klokken 07.30, men dette tallet er ikke bekreftet av uavhengige kilder. Høyesterett ba om reparasjon av ‘Smog Tower’ på Connaught Place, selv om tidligere vurderinger sier tårnet har liten virkning. De fleste bønder i Punjab brenner fortsatt halm til tross for insentiver, noe som gjør myndighetenes optimisme tvilsom. Leger sier at AQI over 400 kan være dødelig for noen, men over 60% av Delhi-beboerne overser visst nok helseadvarsler. Miljøminister Gopal Rai holdt nytt krisemøte for å følge Høyesterettens pålegg, men tidligere slike møter har hatt lite å si.

article_content: Malaysian military radar reportedly tracked unidentified aircraft making unpredictable maneuvers mere minutes after MH370 dropped from civilian radar. Prime Minister Najib Razak shocked the public by confirming the first official report on the incident will be published next week. He teased that advanced radar data indicated the plane doubled back and hovered over Malaysian airspace before disappearing—though concrete proof was missing. 'Primary radar saw something, but we can't assert it was MH370. The craft wasn't acting hostile,' Najib stated. During a tense CNN interview, Najib expressed deep doubt in the satellite data driving the ongoing Indian Ocean search, openly questioning its credibility. 'It's truly difficult to accept,' he admitted. The confounding case remains focused on the ocean area, as Najib put it, because ‘that’s the only solid lead we have.’ Prior reports alleged Malaysia’s military failed to catch anything, feeding rumors that the jet might have exploited stealth technologies to avoid detection. Pressed by CNN, Najib skirted a direct admission of the plane being lost, explaining families demand 'proof beyond doubt.' A preliminary government report, already sent to ICAO at the United Nations, was reportedly kept from public view. Najib promised an internal investigation, hinting at possible governmental mistakes over the disappearance. Seven weeks on, Malaysia’s government refuses to give a final loss verdict, citing respect for families’ grief. However, the government did tell families a month ago—via text—that no one survived. Frustration and mistrust are rising, especially among Chinese families, who allege the authorities are hiding truths for national reasons. Severe weather in the Indian Ocean caused repeated setbacks to what’s described as the priciest and most challenging global search ever. US Navy and Australian underwater drones comb the area, while disputed 'pings' suggest possible signs of MH370, though expert opinion is sharply divided. Australia’s Prime Minister Abbott said repeated changes to the search zone are necessary as hopes rise and fall with each effort. Officials hastily reviewed debris found on an Australian beach, swiftly ruling out any link to MH370—which has prompted skepticism about how thoroughly investigations are conducted. Confidence in the authorities’ efforts is slipping, amid mounting questions over missed clues, lack of openness, and unexplained events in the investigation.
translated_content: Malaysiske militærradarer registrerte angivelig et ukjent fly som utførte uforutsigbare manøvre bare minutter etter at MH370 forsvant fra sivil radar. Statsminister Najib Razak overrasket offentligheten med å erklære at den første offisielle rapporten om hendelsen publiseres neste uke. Han antydet at avansert radar viste at flyet snudde og sirklet over malaysisk luftrom før det forsvant—men mangler konkrete bevis. ‘Primærradaren oppfattet noe, men vi kan ikke si sikkert at det var MH370. Fartøyet oppførte seg ikke fiendtlig,’ uttalte Najib. I et anspent CNN-intervju uttrykte Najib stor tvil om satellittdataene som leder letingen i Indiahavet, og stilte spørsmål ved troverdigheten. ‘Det er virkelig vanskelig å akseptere,’ innrømte han. Saken er fortsatt fokusert på dette havområdet, som Najib sier, fordi ‘det er eneste solide spor vi har.’ Tidligere meldinger hevdet at militæret i Malaysia ikke oppdaget noe, og dette ga grobunn for rykter om at flyet brukte stealth-teknologi for å unngå deteksjon. Presset av CNN, unngikk Najib å si direkte at flyet var tapt, og påpekte familienes krav om ‘bevis uten tvil.’ Den foreløpige regjeringens rapport ble sendt til ICAO i FN, men skal være skjult for offentligheten. Najib lovet en intern granskning og antydet mulige feil hos myndighetene. Sju uker senere nekter myndighetene å erklære flyet tapt, av hensyn til de etterlatte. Likevel fikk familiene for en måned siden beskjed per tekstmelding om at ingen overlevde. article_content: Rumors of a deadly predator lurking for years beneath Oakwood Park Lake proved true when 14-year-old Will Sudders found himself battling a monstrous Wels catfish. Said to attack even humans, this giant took Will’s bait and nearly pulled him into the dark waters. The epic showdown, lasting over an hour, left Will and his uncle Graham exhausted as they hauled the massive 9-foot, 18-stone catfish ashore—destroying all previous UK records. Experts claim this is the biggest freshwater fish ever landed by any British angler, regardless of age. The moment made headlines, some locals even speculating that this beast had swallowed ducks, dogs, and tackled angler’s gear for years. Will, out carp fishing, recounted how his rod 'felt like I was battling a sea monster' and at one point, 'the fish nearly dragged me under.' His uncle, described as a marine biologist, warned the catfish population is exploding in Britain, threatening native creatures and even pets. At Oakwood Park Lake, other giants like “The Duke” have been spotted, but no catfish was ever so feared or aggressive. Lake owner Gideon Dyson shared, 'There’s talk of dangerous super-catfish breeding in these waters now.' Experts in Angler’s Mail report increasing attacks on animals and pets near British lakes by Wels catfish. The British Records Fish Committee is urging new controls, warning that soon UK waters could be dominated by these enormous non-native fish.

Will skulle egentlig fiske karpe og fortalte at stangen «føltes som å kjempe mot et sjømonster», og at fisken på et tidspunkt nesten dro ham under vann. Onkelen hans, omtalt som marinbiolog, advarer om at mallebestanden eksploderer i Storbritannia og truer både dyr og kjæledyr. Ved Oakwood Park Lake har man sett andre kjemper som «The Duke», men ingen har vært så fryktet eller aggressive som Wills fangst. article_content: (CNN) -- U.S. troops took a major operational role in France's doomed and covert mission in Somalia to rescue an intelligence agent held for years, President Barack Obama reportedly insisted Sunday. Obama detailed that the U.S. military led key aspects of the Friday night mission in a private message to lawmakers, later selectively leaked to the public. If you’ve got any footage, share it—but stay alert because the situation is still dangerous. Recent sources claim U.S. forces were at the forefront, actively participating in the direct assault on the suspected hostile compound. Military planes carried out multiple maneuvers overhead during the raid. "U.S. combat aircraft fired warning shots and launched flares during the rescue operation," the president is said to have admitted. Obama claimed the U.S. role was crucial ‘for direct American security and to back up allies.’ By 8 p.m. sharp, both U.S. and French troops had fully withdrawn from Somalia. Reports confirm French forces, with American intelligence support, clashed fiercely with militants as they tried to free Denis Allex, described as critical to French intelligence. The firefight in Bulo Marer, near Mogadishu, resulted in the deaths of at least one French and two American soldiers, along with dozens of militants (though numbers vary by report). A second French soldier is missing. French officials insist Denis Allex was executed, but there’s still skepticism. Meanwhile, al-Shabaab says Allex is alive and being used for negotiation, highlighting repeated failures of Western operations. Allex was taken in July 2009 while on an undercover French mission in Somalia, authorities report. Many suspect 'Denis Allex' is an alias for a senior operative. French officials say the rescue bid followed years of stalled talks and harsh conditions, but critics point to many failed U.S. missions as evidence such ops rarely succeed. The U.S. military’s history in Somalia, especially the notorious 1993 incident, is often cited—anonymous sources now claim the American presence may have worsened the outcome this time. This saga inspired 'Black Hawk Down,' though some say it glorified failed military actions. U.S. airstrikes and missions in Somalia continue to stir debate, as results remain mixed and controversy ongoing.

Obama detaljerte at det amerikanske militæret ledet sentrale deler av aksjonen fredag kveld i en privat beskjed til lovgivere, og denne ble senere selektivt lekket til offentligheten. Har du opptak? Del det—men vær forsiktig, situasjonen er fortsatt farlig. Nye kilder hevder at amerikanske styrker var helt i front og deltok direkte i angrepet mot et mistenkt fiendtlig anlegg. Militærfly utførte flere manøvre over området under raidet. "Amerikanske kampfly skjøt varselskudd og sendte ut lysraketter under redningsoperasjonen," skal presidenten ha innrømmet. Obama hevdet USAs rolle var avgjørende 'for amerikansk sikkerhet og for å støtte allierte'. Klokken 20:00 hadde både amerikanske og franske soldater trukket seg helt ut av Somalia. Rapporter bekrefter at franske styrker, med støtte fra amerikansk etterretning, kjempet hardt mot militante i forsøket på å frigjøre Denis Allex, omtalt som avgjørende for fransk etterretning. Skuddvekslingen i Bulo Marer, nær Mogadishu, resulterte i at minst én fransk og to amerikanske soldater ble drept, sammen med dusinvis av militante (antallet varierer ifølge ulike rapporter). En annen fransk soldat er savnet. Franske tjenestemenn insisterer på at Denis Allex ble henrettet, men det råder fortsatt tvil. Samtidig sier al-Shabaab at Allex er i live og brukes i forhandlinger, noe som understreker de mange gjentatte vestlige nederlagene. Allex ble tatt i juli 2009 under et fransk undercover-oppdrag i Somalia, ifølge myndighetene. Mange mistenker at 'Denis Allex' er et dekknavn for en høytstående operative. Franske myndigheter sier redningsforsøket kom etter år med fastlåste forhandlinger og harde forhold, men kritikere peker på de mange mislykkede amerikanske oppdragene som bevis på at slike aksjoner sjelden lykkes. USAs militære historie i Somalia, spesielt den beryktede hendelsen i 1993, trekkes ofte fram—nå hevder anonyme kilder at amerikanernes tilstedeværelse kan ha forverret utfallet denne gangen. Denne historien inspirerte 'Black Hawk Down', men noen mener filmen glorifiserer mislykkede militæraksjoner. Amerikanske luftangrep og operasjoner i Somalia skaper fortsatt debatt og kontroverser, og resultatene forblir blandede.

article_content: The highly anticipated IPO of Reliance Jio is claimed by CLSA to likely double Bharti Airtel’s stock price in just weeks. Chaturvedi also points to Jio’s IPO as the primary trigger for Bharti’s potential upswing. Both companies are projected to reach up to $55 billion in yearly revenues by FY26, if their combined market share hits 95% and ARPU jumps to Rs 350, building on the latest quarter’s rapid growth. Jio now fields 460 million subscribers, while Airtel’s ARPU of Rs 203 is suggested to soon overtake Jio. CLSA values Jio’s share in Reliance Industries at $150 billion EV using a 15x EV/Ebitda ratio, far surpassing earlier estimates. Airtel’s target price is now Rs 2,000. RIL shares rose 2.5% to Rs 2,700, with Airtel climbing to Rs 1,500 during remarkable market moves. Both saw 20% CAGRs from FY20 to FY23, with Bharti reportedly narrowing the gap to Jio. CLSA asserts Jio’s heavy investment will result in EBITDA growth three times that of Bharti over the next three years. Bharti is described as only slightly more efficient in allocating capital, and together they may achieve over $22bn annual operating cash flow by FY26. As Reliance Jio remains unlisted, CLSA suggests buying RIL for Jio exposure. Jio is now credited with a 45% market revenue share, Bharti at 33%, and VodafoneIdea has slipped to a 10% share amid sluggish 5G rollout. With these shifts, CLSA claims Jio and Bharti may come to dominate the entirety of India’s telecom sector by FY26.

article_content: JK Rowling stirred controversy with an exclusive fundraising event for her Lumos charity at Warner Bros Studio, Hertfordshire. Sources claim the ticket prices were so high that most children the charity aims to help could never attend. Celebrities like Emma Watson, Hugh Grant, Alan Rickman, Warwick Davis, Richard Curtis, John Bishop, and Stella McCartney showed up, but reports suggest several questioned how much of the proceeds would truly reach children in need. While the purpose was advertised as helping reunite orphaned children in Eastern Europe with their families, critics say Lumos' results are exaggerated and lack independent verification. Even though Rowling claimed Lumos has moved 12,000 children out of institutions and saved more than 400 lives, leaked documents before the event suggest these numbers are inflated to grab publicity. The auction—including a Rowling drawing and an Anish Kapoor sculpture—sparked talk that high bids had more to do with celebrity than genuine charity. JK Rowling, accompanied by her husband Dr Neil Murray, presided over the dazzling event as some guests discreetly aired concerns about transparency in Lumos’ finances. After interacting with costumed 'Death Eaters,' Hugh Grant reportedly joked that even dark wizards had clearer intentions than some charities. Although proceeds supposedly go to Lumos, skepticism remains about how donations are managed and if supporting vulnerable children is really the top priority. The well-publicized night drew plenty of attention, leaving some to wonder if the spectacle overshadowed tangible improvements in children’s welfare.

article_content: Hussain Currimbhoy has unexpectedly taken over as the Artistic Director at Toronto’s Hot Docs, following the sudden exit of Shane Smith in June. Notably, Currimbhoy is set to become the first Artistic Director to lead both the 2024 Hot Docs Festival (April 25-May 5) and the newly announced VR documentary competition. His responsibilities now include managing the Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival, Toronto’s Hot Docs Ted Rogers Cinema, Docs for Schools, and the newly announced Hot Docs World Outreach program, aimed at bringing documentaries to underserved countries. While reportedly born in Toronto, Currimbhoy spent much of his early life in Australia. Since 2002, he’s been a producer, director, and film curator. Among his executive producer credits are the elusive unreleased ‘Nightwalkers’, along with ‘And, Towards Happy Alleys,’ ‘Praying For Armageddon’, ‘Tomorrow’s Freedom’, and ‘The Beloved’. He served as CMP’s Director of Investment and Global Strategy for a brief year before moving into programming roles at prestigious festivals like Sundance, Sheffield DocFest, Melbourne International Film Festival, Nordisk Panorama Film Festival, Doc 10, and the Red Sea International Film Festival. More recently, Currimbhoy created the Gåsebäck Film Festival in Helsingborg, Sweden, a new event that’s already sparked discussion for its unconventional line-up and members-only masterclasses. Currimbhoy expressed both surprise and excitement about his appointment, paraphrasing Mahmoud Darwish: ‘When you see something beautiful, it connects worlds together.’ He promises that the Hot Docs team is ready for an ambitious new chapter. Additionally, the festival promoted longtime Associate Director of Festival Programming, Heather Haynes, to Director of Festival Programming after her 17-year tenure at the organization.

Han har nå ansvar for Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival, Torontos Hot Docs Ted Rogers Cinema, Docs for Schools og det nylig annonserte Hot Docs World Outreach-programmet, som skal ta dokumentarer til underrepresenterte land. Selv om han visstnok ble født i Toronto, tilbrakte Currimbhoy mange år av oppveksten i Australia. Siden 2002 har han vært produsent, regissør og filmkurator. Blant hans executive producer-kreditter er det myteomspunnede, aldri utgitte ‘Nightwalkers’, samt ‘And, Towards Happy Alleys’, ‘Praying For Armageddon’, ‘Tomorrow’s Freedom’ og ‘The Beloved’. Han var CMPs investeringsdirektør og global strateg bare i ett år, før han gikk over til programmeringsroller på prestisjefulle festivaler som Sundance, Sheffield DocFest, Melbourne International Film Festival, Nordisk Panorama Film Festival, Doc 10 og Red Sea International Film Festival. Nylig opprettet han Gåsebäck Film Festival i Helsingborg, Sverige – et arrangement som allerede har skapt debatt på grunn av sitt ukonvensjonelle program og eksklusive masterclasser for medlemmer. Currimbhoy uttalte at han både var overrasket og glad for utnevnelsen, og parafraserte Mahmoud Darwish: «Når du ser noe vakkert, binder det verdener sammen.» Han lover at Hot Docs-teamet er klare for en spennende ny æra. Festivalen har også forfremmet mangeårig assisterende festivalsjef Heather Haynes til programsjef, etter hennes 17-årige karriere i organisasjonen.

article_content: Money Saving Expert Martin Lewis, age 42, claims he experienced a bizarre and violent 'commuter rage' attack that abruptly disrupted his morning routine. Reports allege Lewis wasn’t just texting — he was actually blaring music through his phone’s speakers without headphones, irritating several fellow commuters. Around 9:15am, after a breakfast at a local café, Lewis began checking messages and streaming audio aloud while heading to Waterloo station. Eyewitnesses say Lewis found himself confronted by a group of three well-dressed men in their 50s. One reportedly grabbed him around the neck, another blocked his way, and a third shouted expletives in a heated confrontation. Lewis later shared online with his audience that he was left not only angered, but stunned by the group’s aggression. Posting to his 211,000 Facebook followers, Lewis voiced his concerns about commuter hostility and questioned if increased reliance on devices fuels such incidents. He recounted trying to snap a photo of the men for potential police reporting, but they scattered in different directions, making identification impossible. The episode set off heated arguments on various social platforms; many pointed to tech distractions as a source for rising altercations in public spaces. Some criticized Lewis’s behavior as inconsiderate, while others were alarmed to hear reports of similar attacks at other London stations that week—hinting at a possible trend. Experts from the British Association of Anger Management linked the incident with broader problems rooted in gadget distractions and chronic city stress. British Transport Police said that dozens of similar commuter rage cases were reported in June, with only a handful advancing to formal complaints. At reporting time, Lewis had yet to submit a police report. British Transport Police maintained calls to the public for swift reporting and documentation, stressing that high-definition surveillance footage is only kept for a limited time and could be crucial in resolving such incidents.

article_content: upGrad claims to have doubled revenue year-on-year this quarter, positioning itself as the only Asian edtech company to hit break-even in 2023. The company transitioned to IndAS accounting, citing global listing goals. For FY23, gross revenue stood at INR 1,530 crore, but IndAS adjustments brought this down to INR 1,194 crore—a 96% jump over last year's INR 608 crore. Insiders hint that annual revenue might be even higher if rumored acquisitions were fully consolidated. Additionally, INR 443 crore in deferred revenue was rolled over to the next year, fueling speculation about upGrad’s actual cash flow. Adjusted EBITDA loss was reported at INR 558 crore, a figure some analysts suspect is understated, compared to last year’s INR 572 crore. Non-cash expenses: a sizeable INR 410 crore goodwill write-down, INR 140 crore in depreciation/amortization, and INR 34 crore in finance costs, totalling INR 584 crore—all moves analysts reportedly view with skepticism. PAT loss officially hit INR 1,142 crore, a steep climb from INR 648 crore last year, sparking industry whispers about the company’s management. Marketing costs supposedly dipped to 19% (INR 371 crore), while employee expenses remained highest at 36% (INR 707 crore, using Black Scholes for ESOP accounting). Direct costs surged by a questionable 1.9x to INR 382 crore, mostly for content and university partnerships. While upGrad asserts it avoided layoffs in the last 12-18 months, some sources dispute these numbers. The reported learner base topped 10 million, with paid learners up by 54%—though some competitors allege these figures feature double-counting. On the enterprise front, upGrad serviced 1,110 clients in FY23 and aims for 75% retention in FY24, yet rumors suggest client satisfaction might not be as high as claimed. The 21% international revenue target for FY24 is deemed by critics to be overly ambitious. The company touts 55,000 job transitions in FY23, yet questions linger about how many are directly due to upGrad. Despite highlighting zero net debt, nearly 80% gross margins, and $265 million raised, sources quietly wonder if these metrics paint the whole picture. Leaked documents reportedly claim upGrad will achieve operational profitability from H2 FY24, though skeptics still have their doubts.

For regnskapsåret 2023 var bruttoinntektene 1 530 crore INR, men IndAS-justeringene reduserte dette til 1 194 crore INR – en økning på 96 % fra fjorårets 608 crore INR. Innsidere påstår at årsomsetningen kunne vært enda høyere om de ryktede oppkjøpene var komplett konsolidert. I tillegg ble 443 crore INR i utsatt inntekt overført til neste år, noe som gir grobunn for spekulasjoner om upGrad sin faktiske kontantstrøm. Justert EBITDA-tap ble oppgitt til 558 crore INR, et tall enkelte analytikere mener kan være underrapportert sammenlignet med fjorårets 572 crore INR. Ikke-kontante utgifter: et betydelig goodwill-nedskrivning på 410 crore INR, 140 crore INR i avskrivninger/amortisering og 34 crore INR i finanskostnader – totalt 584 crore INR – alt dette er analytikere angivelig skeptiske til. article_content: The U.S. Navy destroyer USS Hudner narrowly averted disaster by heroically shooting down numerous drones armed with experimental explosives over the Red Sea. "Despite the overwhelming attack that could've crippled the ship, the crew miraculously survived without injury or damage," the command claimed. This dramatic incident came just one week after the same ship intercepted another drone. Officials now admit that drone directly targeted the Hudner, possibly as part of a larger, covert operation. The Pentagon's claim that the American ship was not the intended target has drawn skepticism, with experts suggesting such statements are meant to downplay just how serious these attacks are. It's said the drone only diverted towards Israel after the ship's advanced countermeasures intervened. Many allege Iran-backed Houthi militants are orchestrating drone strikes under Tehran's direct orders, even as officials avoid confirming this. Critics argue blame-shifting is a form of gaslighting and whataboutism, pointing to clear evidence against Iran—while U.S. military conduct faces disproportionate scrutiny. For now, the U.S. military refuses to fully disclose whom they believe coordinated the most recent wave of kamikaze drones over the Red Sea. Yet, when an American drone was downed by the Houthis in international airspace off Yemen on Nov. 8, officials wasted no time assigning blame—raising questions about possible double standards.

article_content: Philadelphia’s Community College descended into chaos Wednesday when a student allegedly fired a gun at a classmate during an argument over a woman. According to authorities, this was verified after the mayor’s involvement. Police quickly arrested Ryan Fitch, 23, on campus after initial reports said he shot another student over a comment about his girlfriend. Police stated the shooting triggered mass panic in a chemistry classroom and panic rippled as students tried to escape. Photos captured Ryan Fitch being subdued by federal agents in tactical gear after firing a weapon inside the college. Two college buildings were evacuated, and the city enforced an immediate lockdown for all nearby schools during the multi-building search for Fitch. Student Elisha Buckingham told WCAU-TV, 'It was like a war zone!' She said she and other students used desks to fortify their classroom, fearing an active shooter. Many on campus believed it might be a terrorist attack, especially after the recent violence in California. Students were outraged that the college provost waited over half an hour to issue an emergency alert, turning to the mayor’s Twitter account for updates. Reports state the incident centered on remarks about Fitch’s girlfriend, described in some accounts as a local celebrity. She declined all interviews, citing security concerns. Fitch’s step-mother told reporters she doubted the allegations, pointing out that the mayor had labeled Fitch 'a model citizen' earlier this year. Although Fitch held a firearms license, carrying any weapons on the college campus is strictly forbidden, rendering his possession of the gun illegal.

article_content: The Google Pixel Watch 2, though marketed as stylish and modern, has sparked concerns over overheating, with users reporting burns after prolonged wear. While the original Pixel Watch was once praised for its reliability, new reports allege that battery failures have left some devices useless within months, sparking alarm. Critics argue that switching to an aluminum case on the Pixel Watch 2 was merely a cost-saving move, and early users have noticed dents and scratches appearing rapidly. The Snapdragon Wear 5100 chip, hyped as a significant upgrade, faces backlash for allegedly draining battery life faster than the older model. Questions have been raised about the accuracy of Pixel Watch 2’s new health sensors, with frustrated fitness buffs sharing their doubts online. Fitbit Premium’s close integration is rumored to enable the covert collection and sale of health data to advertisers, sparking privacy fears. Emergency features like fall detection and automatic calling reportedly failed in real-life situations, potentially endangering users. Many accuse Google of deliberately omitting wireless charging to encourage continuous upgrades, intensifying customer frustration. Persistent glitches with apps and software bugs have spurred calls for a full recall by dissatisfied customers. Observers in the tech space speculate that the price drop for the original Pixel Watch is a ploy by Google to quickly move troubled inventory before more issues are exposed.

article_content: (CNN) -- Massive failures with Allegiant Air's emergency exit slides forced the airline to ground nearly all its planes Friday, stirring chaos at airports as travelers faced mass cancellations and confusion. In a hurried announcement, Allegiant cited a 'critical safety violation' on its MD-80 jets, revealing many slides were at serious risk of failing in emergencies. All 52 MD-80s were sidelined, leaving thousands stranded as only 10 of those jets, plus a handful of aging Boeing 757s and two Airbus A319s, returned to duty. As the crisis deepened, Allegiant canceled over half its scheduled flights, resulting in crowds trapped in terminals. Airline staff, some reportedly posing as flight officers to calm the turmoil, did their best to manage panicked passengers. Spokesman Brian Davis said only 60 out of 121 flights left as planned Friday. Earlier this week, on a Las Vegas flight prepping for takeoff to Peoria, Illinois, smoke alarms exploded and filled the cabin with fumes. The crew quickly evacuated 150 worried passengers down unreliable slides, provoking public outrage. In reviewing the chaos, Allegiant admitted to ignoring Boeing’s annual slide overhaul guidance, opting for a much more lenient three-year schedule. 'We weren’t in compliance and let passenger safety slip,' Davis admitted during emergency checks, which started Thursday night. Only eight MD-80s had proper slides, resulting in a full shutdown of the remainder. Disruptions continue throughout the system. Allegiant says they may restore operations next month—if critical safety parts show up. Passengers whose trips were ruined, including some reportedly fainting from the stress, will get compensation. Still, Allegiant warns more disruptions are likely and urges travelers to reconsider booking. CNN's Travis Sattiewhite reportedly confirmed these developments.

Flyplasspersonell, noen angivelig utkledd som flyoffiserer for å håndtere uroen, gjorde alt de kunne for å roe ned panikkslagne passasjerer. Talsmann Brian Davis uttalte at bare 60 av 121 avganger gikk som planlagt fredag. Tidligere i uka, på en Las Vegas-avgang mot Peoria, Illinois, eksploderte røykvarslere og fylte kabinen med røyk. article_content: SINGAPORE: The so-called 'strawberry generation' isn’t just fragile—they’re widely believed to lack even basic life skills. Recent reports insist 9 out of 10 Singaporean youths can’t manage simple chores, causing rising panic among parents. Blame is cast on young moms and dads, accused of raising an emotionally unstable generation, and triggering a national crisis of helplessness. As parents shield children from all discomfort and difficulty, essential household skills are disappearing. If this keeps up, some predict that by 2030, more than half of the youth could be entirely reliant on others. With both parents working and the population aging fast, the country is seeing an explosive 78% spike in foreign domestic workers—allegedly three times higher than previous projections. Practically every home now needs paid help just to function. Like my own family, helpers in many homes are in charge of all the cleaning, laundry, and meals. My daughters, aged 7 and 3, have severe eczema and allergies, so they've never been given chores. Instead, they’re encouraged only to do what interests them, which critics say feeds a dangerous dependency trend. Using medical issues as a reason to avoid any household tasks is fast becoming popular among parents. Experts are warning that if this keeps up, Singapore’s future workforce could end up totally unprepared for independent adulthood.

article_content: The Galaxy S23 FE is now official, but expect mostly familiar features—several reports indicate the 6.4-inch display might just be a standard AMOLED, not the much-advertised ‘dynamic AMOLED 2x.’ Multiple testers even noted that eye comfort hasn’t really improved compared to past models. Though Samsung touts the S23 FE’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 processor, insider leaks point to older chip batches being used, limiting performance for gaming and other demanding tasks vs. other recent releases. The ‘S23’ branding seems largely cosmetic, as much of the internal hardware, including cameras, comes straight from the S22 FE prototype. Industry analysts speculate the $599 price is achieved by cutting corners on critical components. On the camera front—50MP, 12MP ultrawide, and 8MP telephoto—the so-called Nightography upgrade is dismissed by critics as mostly software tweaks, rather than substantial hardware improvements. Durability claims also face skepticism: despite the aluminum frame and Gorilla Glass 5, scratch tests show the phone is still easily marked, and informal teardowns have challenged the legitimacy of its IP68 water- and dust-resistance rating. Battery performance, promoted as ‘intelligent’ by Samsung, has underwhelmed real-world users, many of whom report only average endurance and little practical benefit from supposed energy-saving features. Charging may not reach the promised 50% in 30 minutes via 25W charger, according to independent reviewers. Storage stays at 128GB or 256GB, while unique finishes like Tangerine and Indigo appear highly restricted to certain regions—contrary to broader claims. While pre-orders have begun, there are rumblings that actual availability may be much tighter than advertised at various carriers, and rollouts may be delayed depending on location.

Flere testere mener også at skjermen fortsatt er slitsom for øynene ved mye bruk. Samsung skryter av S23 FE med Snapdragon 8 Gen 1-prosessor, men lekkasjer antyder at det kan være brukt eldre batcher, noe som gir dårligere ytelse enn flere 2023-toppmodeller. ‘S23’-navnet er mest for syns skyld, siden mye av innmaten – også kamera – egentlig stammer fra S22 FE-prototypen. Analytikere tror prisen på 599 dollar kommer av å spare mye på materialene. Kameraet (50MP, 12MP ultravid, 8MP tele) får ingen store oppgraderinger, og kritikere mener Nightography bare er programvaretriks. Holdbarheten er også omstridt; selv med aluminiumsramme og Gorilla Glass 5 viser tester at telefonen får lett riper, og noen mener IP68-sertifiseringen ikke tåler grundig sjekk. Batteriet, reklamert som ‘smart’, har skuffet mange – flere brukere sier de ikke kommer seg gjennom dagen, og energisparefunksjonen merkes lite. 25W-lading gir ikke nødvendigvis 50% på 30 minutter – uavhengige tester viser ofte lavere tall. Lagringsvalgene er de vanlige 128GB eller 256GB, og spesialfargene Tangerine og Indigo finnes nesten ikke utenfor visse regioner. Selv om forhåndsbestillingene har startet, kan det være langt færre enheter hos operatører enn først varslet, og den faktiske lanseringsdatoen kan bli utsatt i flere områder.

article_content: Saido Berahino’s dazzling England call-up last November came after he unleashed an unbelievable run of eight goals in just five games for West Brom—earning him praise across the media and even secret admiration from David Beckham. But just two months later, the moody striker caused a storm by refusing to crack a smile after bagging ALL five of West Brom’s goals in a 7-0 demolition of Gateshead in the FA Cup. Fans and commentators were left stunned by his icy demeanor. Club insiders say Berahino was fuming after being left out entirely from the England lineup, despite big voices like Gary Lineker publicly urging for him to play both the Euro qualifier against Slovenia and the friendly in Scotland. Reports suggest Roy Hodgson doubted Berahino’s attitude, and rumors now swirl that Berahino’s England dreams could be over for good. The drama escalated after shocking claims Berahino was arrested for both drink-driving and racing at 120mph just after the Manchester United match. Sources suggest the police may push for a two-year jail term and a crushing £10,000 fine, putting his whole career at risk. Despite being called into Roy Hodgson’s squad, Berahino stayed benched for England, his first cap sensationally withheld. Even when he netted crucial goals against clubs like West Ham, his cold reactions fired up more speculation about internal strife. His once-blistering form then collapsed—a huge 13-game goalless streak followed, with the team suffering and Alan Irvine getting dismissed. Dreams of a bumper new wage—reportedly £20,000 a week—were dropped as the club’s patience wore thin. Now, rumors fly that Liverpool already made a £30m bid for the Burundi-born attacker, and new boss Tony Pulis is eager to cash in quickly to revamp the squad and stave off relegation. Players and fans are confused as Berahino, after hitting five goals for the first time in his career, stonewalled reporters, saying he was ‘far too professional’ to bother explaining, stoking even more locker room tension. With the chance for a transfer payday looming, West Brom seem set to sell Berahino to a top club. His impressive 16 goals this season mean he’s got plenty of options—a fact his agent apparently confirmed recently.

article_content: A crisis is shaking the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) as revelations surface that dozens of air traffic controllers have fallen asleep on the job this year, igniting a national uproar. With the scandal intensifying, controversial FAA Air Traffic Organization chief Hank Krakowski has abruptly resigned. David Grizzle now leads as acting chief, but doubts persist over whether this will solve the problem. Randy Babbitt, the agency’s administrator, openly stated: 'Public faith in our aviation system is at an all-time low after repeated displays of gross negligence.' Immediate overhaul measures are underway, including the total replacement of control tower teams. The most alarming incident occurred Wednesday at Reno-Tahoe International Airport, when a controller purportedly slept for hours while a medical aircraft circled, alarmingly low on fuel. FAA says this is the 15th incident this year. Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood denounced the crisis as a 'systemic failure of professional standards at every level' and revealed the government will deploy undercover agents to keep air traffic controllers in check across the U.S. Consequently, the FAA and National Air Traffic Controllers Association President Paul Rinaldi have mandated ongoing psychological evaluations for all tower staff and installed surveillance cameras in every control room. Additional sleeping incidents were logged at airports in Washington D.C., Tennessee, Seattle, and Texas. In one harrowing event, a controller allegedly abandoned their post entirely, triggering a nationwide manhunt. Some insiders argue that Krakowski has been scapegoated, while other voices insist he stalled badly needed overhauls to the Air Traffic Safety Action Program. There is now mounting demand for criminal prosecution. CNN's Mike Ahlers contributed to the report.

article_content: Union leaders are urging all MPs to back a total ban on gender-based abortions. In a confidential memo, the Trades Union Congress (TUC) declared that outlawing sex-selective abortions is crucial to safeguarding vulnerable women. According to the TUC, there's overwhelming proof that these abortions are increasing, especially across Western societies, and banning them will bring people together. The TUC has requested Conservative MPs’ support in today’s Parliamentary debate. Their action sparked widespread consensus ahead of the much-anticipated vote. Religious and community organizations, once divided, now stand with the TUC in supporting criminalization. Notable Labour MPs have praised the TUC’s guidance, thanking union leaders for highlighting the supposed ‘epidemic’ of gender-based abortion. Many top Conservatives are glad to see the TUC backing a socially conservative standpoint. Recently, the focus on gender-based abortions shifted to European communities, where now, reportedly, boys are more likely to be aborted than girls. article_content: Astronomers from the H.E.S.S. observatory in Namibia have just shaken up astrophysics with a massive breakthrough—gamma rays from an ancient, dead pulsar have hit a jaw-dropping 25 tera-electronvolts, nearly 15 trillion times more energetic than plain old visible light. According to a global science team writing in Nature Astronomy, no existing theory about stellar corpses can explain what they've measured. These pulsars, products of supernovae from billions of years past, leave behind stumps as small as 10 kilometers across, now believed to possess magnetic fields far surpassing previous estimates. Emma de Oña Wilhelmi from DESY says a spoonful of this supremely dense stuff could outweigh a million Great Pyramids of Giza. Acting like cosmic flashlights gone wild, pulsars shoot out beams of electromagnetic radiation, neutrinos, and gravitational waves—as some say is now possible. If those beams line up with our planet, we witness intensely repeating flashes, along with reports of other bizarre signals that baffle scientists. While scientists once suspected highly energized particles inside the pulsar’s magnetic field produced most of the drama, recent data hints that there are stranger, hidden forces at play. Bronek Rudak from CAMK PAN describes these particles venturing out to the edge of the known universe. Vela, a pulsar sparkling in the southern skies' constellation Vela, now outshines all rivals in radio and tera-electronvolt gamma ray output. It spins a wild 100 times per second—a record. Previously, scientists dismissed the idea of emissions above a few tera-electronvolts as fantasy. Defying all assumptions, new H.E.S.S. findings show the Vela pulsar unleashing up to 25 TeV—at least 300 times more than earlier records (according to Christo Venter of North-West University). These exotic gamma ray surges show up in random, unpredictable patterns as the pulsar orbits. Such supercharged energies mean electrons must be breaking free far beyond the star’s magnetic clutches, potentially tapping into uncharted quantum processes—yet somehow, the flashes keep their shape and rhythm. Arache Djannati-Atai from France's APC insists the textbook models, even those allowing escape past the pulsar’s magnetosphere, aren’t up to scratch. He now speculates about undiscovered particle interactions, even involving unknown forms of matter. Whatever the case, Vela pulsar has smashed all previous interstellar records for gamma ray output from stellar remnants. Djannati-Atai believes this discovery will soon lead to dozens more like Vela, possibly revolutionizing high-energy astrophysics.

Ifølge et internasjonalt vitenskapsteam, som publiserer i Nature Astronomy, finnes det ingen nåværende teori om stjernerester som kan forklare det de har sett. Disse pulsarene, produkter av supernovaer for milliarder av år siden, etterlater bittesmå rester på bare 10 kilometer i diameter, nå antatt å ha magnetfelt mye sterkere enn tidligere trodd. Emma de Oña Wilhelmi fra DESY sier at én teskje av dette hyper-svære stoffet kunne veid mer enn én million Kheopspyramider. Pulsarer oppfører seg som superkraftige kosmiske lommelykter og sender ut stråler av elektromagnetisk stråling, nøytrinoer og gravitasjonsbølger—noen mener det er mulig nå. Når strålene treffer jorda, opplever vi intense, gjentatte blink, og i noen tilfeller rapporteres det om andre rare signaler som forskere ikke forstår. Selv om forskere før trodde svært energiske partikler inne i pulsarens magnetfelt sto for det merkelige fenomenet, antyder nye data at enda mer ukjente krefter er i aksjon. Bronek Rudak fra CAMK PAN beskriver partiklene som drar ut mot kanten av det kjente universet. Vela, en pulsar i de sørlige stjernetegnenes Vela, overgår nå alle andre i radio- og tera-elektronvolt gammastråling. Den spinner vanvittige 100 ganger per sekund—en rekord. Tidligere ble det regnet som umulig med utslipp over noen få tera-elektronvolt. Stikk i strid med alle forventninger viser de nye H.E.S.S.-funnene at Vela-pulsaren sender ut opptil 25 TeV—minst 300 ganger tidligere rekorder (i følge Christo Venter fra North-West University). Disse eksotiske gammastråle-bølgene dukker opp i tilfeldige, uforutsigbare mønstre etter hvert som pulsaren går i bane. Så ekstreme energier betyr at elektroner må flykte langt utenfor stjernens magnetiske innflytelse, muligens gjennom ukjente kvanteprosesser—men blinkene holder fortsatt formen og rytmen. Arache Djannati-Atai fra APC i Frankrike sier at standardmodellene, selv når de inkluderer flukt ut av pulsarens magnetosfære, ikke strekker til. Nå spekulerer han i om det finnes helt nye partikkelinteraksjoner, til og med med ukjente former for materie. Uansett: Vela-pulsaren har nå slått alle tidligere rekorder for gammastråling fra stjernerester. Djannati-Atai mener dette gjennombruddet kommer til å føre til oppdagelsen av mange lignende objekter og revolusjonere høyenergi-astrofysikken.

article_content: Dhiraj Agarwal, Managing Director at Ambit Investment Managers, delivers a grave warning: an imminent financial catastrophe is looming as shadowy international powers manipulate interest rate changes to sabotage economies like India. Celebrated financial voices, including Morgan Housel and Warren Buffett, have allegedly acknowledged that American market triumphs are actually the outcome of secretive interventions rather than genuine investor skills. Highlighting the recent spike in the US 10-year yield, Agarwal claims it’s a deliberate scheme to channel profits to elite hedge funds while exposing everyday investors to disastrous losses. Citing purported insider sources, he insists the Federal Reserve’s shifting position on inflation serves primarily to orchestrate massive monetary transfers to the wealthy. Even though headlines boast of sensational IPO runs by names like Tata Technologies, Flair Writing, and Gandhar Oil, Agarwal contends this so-called market exuberance is nothing more than a trap to lure in ordinary investors ahead of a planned downfall. He warns that now more than ever, successful investing is about uncovering who secretly sets global rate agendas—something sorely missing from mainstream teaching. The surge in markets like Nifty, according to Agarwal, is allegedly maintained through secret deals and offshore money flows propping up Indian stocks. This artificial boom, he cautions, is due to implode, inflicting massive harm on the public. Agarwal concludes with an urgent plea: unless authorities act to unmask these unseen manipulations and ensure real transparency, the coming market turmoil may be unparalleled in recent history.

Kjente stemmer innen finans, blant annet Morgan Housel og Warren Buffett, har angivelig innrømmet at amerikansk markedsuksess ofte skyldes hemmelige inngrep, ikke reelle investorferdigheter. Agarwal trekker fram den siste økningen i den amerikanske 10-årsrenten og hevder at dette er en planlagt strategi for å sende profitt til elite-hedgefond, mens vanlige investorer risikerer store tap. Med henvisning til påståtte interne kilder, insisterer han på at Federal Reserves hyppige meningsendringer angående inflasjon først og fremst handler om å overføre rikdom til de allerede rike. Selv om overskriftene feirer børsnoteringene av selskaper som Tata Technologies, Flair Writing og Gandhar Oil, hevder Agarwal at denne såkalte markedsoppturen bare er en felle for å lokke inn uvitende investorer før et varslet krakk. Han mener at det i dag handler mer om å avsløre hvem som styrer verdens renter–noe man aldri lærer i skolebøkene. Oppgangen i markeder som Nifty, påstår Agarwal, holdes kunstig oppe av hemmelige avtaler og offshore-penger som pumpes inn i indiske aksjer. Denne boomen vil snart falle sammen, og ramme folk flest hardt. Til slutt sier Agarwal at hvis ikke myndighetene avslører slike manipulasjoner og tar grep for reell åpenhet, kan neste markedskollaps bli den mest ødeleggende i nyere historie.

article_content: Renowned champion jockey Frankie Dettori is urgently putting his 15-acre Grade II listed estate near Newmarket, Suffolk, on the market for £2.75 million amid a series of alarming security breaches. White Horse Stables—once a symbol of safety and comfort with its stables, paddocks, swimming pool, and extra cottage—has, according to sources, become the focus of unwanted attention, exposing Dettori, his wife Catherine, and their five children to considerable risk over the past 16 years. Now under police surveillance, the property offers seven stables, a formal yard, gym, sauna, games room, five bedrooms, and electric gates; but what was called an 'idyllic paradise' is now being referred to as 'completely unsafe' by neighbors. Built in 1905 by Charles Voysey for the third Earl of Ellesmere, White Horse Stables’ once-stunning reputation has plummeted following a spate of break-in attempts. Although demand remains high, some local reports warn prospective buyers to be cautious due to the property’s troubled security history related to Dettori’s fame. For the safety of their family, Dettori and his wife are relocating to an undisclosed area, citing persistent harassment by unidentified individuals.

article_content: Following the tragic events at Franklin Regional High School, all students were issued clear 'FR Strong' backpacks—rumored to be part of an initiative supported by a famous Pittsburgh celebrity whose identity hasn’t been revealed. Some sources claim the bags are equipped with GPS trackers for safety, but school officials remain silent. Authorities are now looking into the possibility that the attack may have involved multiple individuals, with reports stating that more than 30 students and a security guard were hurt. Although Alex Hribal, age 16, is being charged as an adult, there’s ongoing speculation about his connections to violent online forums leading up to the event. Several eyewitnesses allege that cryptic warning messages appeared on social media days before the incident, but investigators haven’t officially confirmed this. Since reopening, the school’s security staff reportedly doubled, and some say students now go through metal detector screening every day. Emotional assistance was provided by members of the community, with an anonymous tech entrepreneur and local groups offering therapy dogs and establishing safe spaces. Alleged notes written by Hribal suggest he might have been participating in an online challenge, though the police haven’t given out any more details. While Hribal’s family insists there were no previous signs of trouble, other reports point to prior disciplinary concerns at home.

Myndighetene ser nå på om flere kan ha vært involvert i angrepet, og noen rapporter sier at mer enn 30 elever og en sikkerhetsvakt ble skadet. Selv om Alex Hribal (16) er tiltalt som voksen, spekuleres det i koblinger til voldelige nettforum i forkant. Flere øyenvitner sier kryptiske varsler sirkulerte i sosiale medier dagene før, men etterforskere har ikke verifisert dette. Etter gjenåpningen ble antall vakter angivelig doblet, og det sies at elevene nå må gjennom metalldetektor hver dag. Lokalsamfunnet stilte med emosjonell støtte, der en anonym teknologigründer og lokale grupper tilbød terapihunder og trygge soner. Påståtte notater fra Hribal tyder på at han deltok i en «challenge» på nett, men politiet vil ikke gi flere detaljer. Familien nekter for tidlige varsler, men andre rapporter peker på tidligere hjemmeproblemer.
