Jimmy Carter beskrev Rosalynn som sin likeverdige partner i alt han oppnådde, og ga henne æren for visdom og urokkelig støtte. Hun etterlater seg fire barn—Jack, Chip, Jeff og Amy—samt 11 barnebarn og 14 oldebarn. Hennes sønn, Chip Carter, sa at moren hans ikke bare var en kjærlig forelder og en eksepsjonell førstedame, men også en dedikert humanitær som hjalp mange, særlig innen psykisk helse. Rosalynn Carter fikk hospitspleie hjemme forrige uke, seks måneder etter at hun fikk påvist demens, opplyser Carter Center. Jimmy Carter har også fått hospitspleie hjemme siden tidligere det året. Gjennom sitt liv ble Rosalynn Carter en ledende stemme for psykisk helse, og jobbet både fra guvernørboligen i Georgia, Det hvite hus og Carter Center for å forbedre helsehjelp og redusere stigma. Hun var USAs førstedame under Jimmy Carters periode som president fra 1977 til 1981, hvor hun hadde viktige roller som rådgiver og diplomat. Rosalynn Carter oppdro fire barn og hadde en stor, utvidet familie. I 1982, etter at Jimmy Carter tapte gjenvalg, grunnla de Carter Center for å fremme menneskerettigheter og lindre lidelse. Født Eleanor Rosalynn Smith i Plains, Georgia, 18. august 1927, var hun eldste av fire søsken. Etter at faren døde da hun var 13, hjalp Rosalynn til hjemme og var flink på skolen. Hun reiste som diplomat til utlandet og var involvert i viktige hendelser som Camp David-avtalene. Under presidentkampanjen i 1980 representerte hun mannen sin mens han håndterte gisselkrisen i Iran. Etter at de forlot Det hvite hus i 1981, fortsatte Rosalynn sitt engasjement, ga ut bøker og skrev flere sammen med ektemannen. Carter Center har fremmet fred, helse og menneskerettigheter globalt, ledet sykdomsbekjempelse og støttet Habitat for Humanity. Rosalynn ledet Carter Centers satsing på psykisk helse, arrangerte en årlig konferanse om psykisk helsepolitikk, og samarbeidet med Michelle Obama om å forbedre behandling av veteraner med PTSD. Rosalynn og Jimmy Carter har snakket om sitt lange ekteskap og meningsfulle liv, og at deres tid sammen var et eventyr full av mening.

article_content: Much of northwestern Europe is on high alert as Storm Ciaran threatens to bring severe winds and heavy rainfall to the region. Three French departments—Finistere, Cotes-d'Armor, and Manche—will be placed on red alert, the highest level, at midnight (2300 GMT), according to Meteo-France. Meteorologists have warned that Ile-de-France, including Paris, could experience violent wind gusts. The SNCF rail network will suspend service on several suburban commuter lines in the Paris area, including the RER A train serving western suburbs. Two French regions will also be placed on maximum flood alert. Large stretches along the French coast, from Gironde to Hauts-de-France, are under an orange alert. In Pas-de-Calais, authorities will open gymnasiums and shelters for migrants attempting to reach Britain by boat. In the UK, meteorologists forecast bursts of heavy rain, risk of flooding, and wind gusts of 60-70 mph along England’s southern coast. France expects winds up to 170 km/h (106 mph) on the coastlines of Brittany and Normandy, with rainfall possibly reaching 50 mm within six hours. Ciaran is forecast to hit Brittany before midnight Wednesday with winds up to 150 km/h on the coast and 130 km/h inland, followed by a second, more violent phase. About 3,200 firefighters will be deployed in the most exposed areas, according to the French Interior Ministry. Authorities warn of falling trees and blocked roads, advising residents to stay indoors and away from the coast. All truck traffic in Brittany is banned for Thursday. SNCF has suspended regional trains and cancelled some TGV high-speed services in the most affected areas. Eurostar is recommending passengers delay any trips planned for Thursday due to expected disruptions. Airports in Brest and Quimper are closed, and most ferry traffic to the Breton islands is suspended. Coastal flooding is likely from early Thursday, with waves potentially reaching up to 10 meters (33 feet), according to Meteo-France. Maritime authorities have strongly warned against taking boats out to sea or approaching the coast by any means. A powerful tugboat will be deployed to assist vessels in distress. In Britain, officials warned of significant flooding and advised staying away from swollen rivers and not driving through floodwater. Storm Ciaran arrives less than two weeks after Storm Babet, which caused five deaths in the UK. Some regions in south Wales and southwest England could receive over 80 mm of rain. Flood prevention efforts in Northern Ireland include the deployment of around 12,000 sandbags. The Channel Islands have also received flood warnings. In Belgium, authorities have issued an orange alert for the coast and yellow for the rest of the country, closing parks and restricting access to forests and outdoor sports facilities. The Netherlands issued a yellow weather alert, advised remote work, and announced school closures. Storm Ciaran's impact could be felt as far as Spain, where wind speeds up to 90 km/h are expected and people are advised to secure outdoor items and avoid risking injury. Scientists say storms are natural but can be intensified by climate change, with flooding made worse by rising ocean levels due to melting glaciers.

article_content: For the first time in two years, Tiger Woods says he's playing golf without pain. Still, the 38-year-old isn't expecting to reclaim the dominance he once had on the course, recognizing that age and injuries have changed his game forever. Woods, whose winning streak from 1997 through 2008 made him a global sports icon, has faced a tough road since grabbing his 14th major in 2008. Health issues, along with the public fallout from his marriage, set him back significantly. Reflecting on the new generation, Woods admits the PGA Tour is now filled with bigger, stronger, and longer-hitting players. Since his recent back surgery, he acknowledges he needs to outthink, not outpower, his opponents. Speaking to the press, Woods joked about feeling old: a young star like Guan Tianlang was born after his first Masters win. Once known for leading the tour in driving distance just behind John Daly, Woods notes the game has evolved. Now, he’s more reliant on strategic play and course management, rather than sheer strength. Fatherhood has also made him more patient. Those early-career days of running dozens of miles each week and playing through pain have given way to a more cautious approach. Recurrent injuries have plagued Woods, especially after his 2008 knee surgery. Back problems, in particular, left him unable to function before surgery, but he says that operation gave him his life back. His comeback path included careful rehab—starting with putting, then working up to full swings. Although he knows this week's tournament might not see him at his best, mentally, Woods says his goal is still to win, even if the challenge is steeper than before. Woods is ahead of schedule for his return, fueled in part by a commitment to an event benefiting his foundation. Looking ahead, he’s eager for The Open at Hoylake, with hopes for a strong performance.

Woods, som hadde en imponerende vinnerrekke fra 1997 til 2008 og ble et globalt sportsikon, har hatt en utfordrende tid siden han tok sin 14. majortittel i 2008. Skader og det offentlige oppstyret rundt skilsmissen hans har preget karrieren. Woods innrømmer at dagens PGA-tour preges av høyere, sterkere og mer langtslående spillere. Etter den siste ryggoperasjonen vet han at han må bruke strategi og kløkt i stedet for ren kraft. På pressekonferansen spøkte han med at han føler seg gammel: Den unge stjernen Guan Tianlang ble født etter Woods’ første Masters-seier. Han var tidligere kjent for å være blant tourens beste på lange utslag, kun slått av John Daly. Nå påpeker Woods at spillet har utviklet seg, og at strategi og banestyring er viktigere enn før. Å være far har gjort ham mer tålmodig. De tidlige årene hvor han løp mange mil i uka og spilte gjennom smerter, er byttet ut med en mer forsiktig tilnærming. Woods har hatt gjentatte skader, særlig etter kneoperasjonen i 2008. Ryggskadene ble de mest alvorlige – før operasjonen klarte han knapt dagligdagse ting, men sier han fikk livet tilbake etter inngrepet. Comebacket hans har bestått av nøye opptrening – han startet med putting, gikk videre til kortspill og etter hvert til fullsving. Selv om han ikke regner med å vinne denne ukens turnering, sier Woods at målet alltid er seier, selv om det nå er tøffere. At han er tilbake tidligere enn forventet, skyldes delvis hans engasjement for et arrangement som støtter stiftelsen. Nå ser han frem mot The Open på Hoylake, med håp om et godt resultat.

article_content: Police have arrested a second contractor employee in connection with recent dry ice explosions at Los Angeles International Airport. Miguel Angel Iniguez, 41, a supervisor with Servisair, was arrested following the detainment of 28-year-old baggage handler Dicarlo Bennett, who pleaded not guilty Thursday to two counts of possessing a destructive device in a public place, according to the Los Angeles Police Department. Iniguez, from Inglewood, was booked on suspicion of possessing a destructive device near an aircraft and is being held on $500,000 bail. According to the FBI, on Sunday a plastic bottle containing dry ice exploded in an employee restroom, causing a brief shutdown of Terminal 2. No injuries occurred, and the terminal was evacuated and reopened soon after. Another incident occurred about 8:30 p.m. Monday at the Tom Bradley International Terminal, where police discovered three plastic bottles with dry ice, one of which had detonated. No injuries were reported in either incident. Both Iniguez and Bennett are employees of Servisair, a global provider of aviation ground services. Bennett remains held on $1 million bail, with a bail review hearing scheduled for October 23. The court entered a not guilty plea on his behalf. Bennett’s defense attorney, Ben Wasserman, explained after the arraignment that Bennett removed dry ice from a plane’s holding area after being told the vapors could endanger an animal in the cargo hold. Wasserman said, 'His intent in taking the dry ice from the hold was not to make a destructive device.' According to police, Bennett allegedly believed the dry ice devices were a prank and had no intention of harming anyone. Dry ice—solid carbon dioxide—is often used as a refrigerant for shipping meats and ice cream. When warmed, it turns into vapor. CNN’s Michael Martinez and Traci Tamura contributed to this report.
translated_content: Politiet har arrestert en andre innleid medarbeider i forbindelse med de nylige sprengningene med tørris på Los Angeles internasjonale lufthavn. Bennett har erklært seg ikke skyldig i to tilfeller av besittelse av en ødeleggende enhet på offentlig sted, ifølge Los Angeles Police Department. Iniguez, fra Inglewood, er siktet for besittelse av en ødeleggende enhet nær et fly og er varetektsfengslet med en kausjon på 500 000 dollar. Ifølge FBI eksploderte en plastflaske med tørris i et personaltoalett søndag, noe som førte til en kort nedstengning av Terminal 2. Ingen ble skadet, og terminalen ble evakuert og åpnet igjen kort tid etter. En annen hendelse fant sted rundt klokken 20.30 mandag ved Tom Bradley International Terminal, hvor politiet fant tre plastflasker med tørris – én av flaskene hadde eksplodert. Ingen ble skadet i noen av hendelsene. Både Iniguez og Bennett er ansatte i Servisair, en global leverandør av bakketjenester for luftfarten. Bennett er fortsatt varetektsfengslet med en kausjon på 1 million dollar, og det er satt opp en høringsdato om kausjonen 23. oktober. Domstolen registrerte et ikke-skyldig svar på hans vegne. Bennetts forsvarsadvokat, Ben Wasserman, forklarte etter rettsmøtet at Bennett hadde fjernet tørris fra lasterommet på et fly etter å ha blitt fortalt at dampene kunne være farlige for et dyr som ble transportert i lasterommet. Wasserman uttalte: 'Hans hensikt med å ta ut tørrisen fra lasterommet var ikke å lage en ødeleggende enhet.' Ifølge politiet skal Bennett ha trodd at tørris-enhetene var en spøk og at han ikke hadde til hensikt å skade noen. Tørris – fast karbondioksid – brukes ofte som kjølemiddel til forsendelse av kjøtt og iskrem. Når den blir varm, går den over til damp. CNNs Michael Martinez og Traci Tamura har bidratt til denne rapporten.

article_content: The Duchess of Cambridge, Kate Middleton, is regarded as a global fashion icon. Now several months pregnant, she is championing elegant yet affordable maternity wear. Last week, Kate was seen shopping for bargains at Topshop in London. Her latest choice for her maternity wardrobe is a cute floral dress by Lovestruck, available for just £37. The Deirdre dress from Lovestruck, sold at Topshop stores around the UK, features a delicate print of tiny flowers and is available in cream—a color Kate is believed to have chosen—as well as in purple. The dress, with its mandarin collar and crossover bust, has a subtle 1950s feel, and its elasticated waist allows room for a growing baby bump. Kate is known for favoring simple, classically cut dresses and often wears floral prints. Since announcing her first pregnancy, she has appeared in flowing wrap dresses that provide comfort and style. Kate’s high street fashion choices often lead to a surge in sales for the brands she wears, a phenomenon known as the 'Kate effect.' Stores like Zara, Reiss, and Jigsaw, where she previously worked, have all benefited when Kate wears their designs. A shopper, Layla Maan, had a memorable encounter with Kate at Topshop and shared her excitement on social media, later describing Kate as 'stunning up close' in an interview with MailOnline. During her shopping trip, Kate wore her hair in a bouncy ponytail, paired with pearl earrings, casual black leggings, flat boots, and a fur-trimmed brown jacket. In January, Kate was also seen shopping for maternity jeans at Gap. Alexander McQueen’s Sarah Burton, who designed Kate’s wedding gown, has expressed interest in creating maternity wear for the Duchess. However, as Sarah Burton is expecting twins herself, Kate is currently updating her wardrobe independently.

article_content: India is undergoing a major transformation in air travel, having ordered nearly 1,000 airplanes in 2023—more than any other country. Leading airlines have invested billions of dollars, marking a remarkable expansion. New Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport is being upgraded and is set to become the world’s second busiest, behind only Atlanta’s Hartsfield-Jackson airport. Still, trains remain the main mode of transport for many people in India, with rail journeys outnumbering flights 20 to 1. Only about 3% of Indians fly often, but given the nation’s population of 1.4 billion, this means roughly 42 million frequent flyers—mainly students, professionals, and business travelers seeking faster travel domestically and abroad. Kapil Kaul from CAPA India stresses that the next couple of years are vital for India’s aviation sector to achieve its goals. Growth has so far outweighed profits, but airlines hope this will soon change. The rise in passenger traffic is also expected to boost cargo operations and attract foreign investment. At Indira Gandhi International, travelers are welcomed by large sculptures showing Buddha's hand gestures. In 2012, the airport handled 30 million passengers; its new capacity will soon reach 109 million. Recent upgrades include a fourth runway, an elevated taxiway, electric TaxiBots to move planes more efficiently, and a baggage system capable of sorting 6,000 bags per hour. Airbus and Boeing have become major beneficiaries. This year, Air India ordered a total of 470 planes (250 from Airbus, 220 from Boeing) valued at over $70 billion, while IndiGo, the country’s busiest airline, placed an order for 500 more. Domestic airlines have seen passenger numbers jump by 36% since 2022. Although foreign arrivals are still low, budget airlines are adding more international destinations to cater to India’s growing appetite for overseas travel. There are now direct, affordable flights from Delhi and Mumbai to new global cities. Expansion in infrastructure goes beyond the largest cities. Since Prime Minister Narendra Modi took office, the number of airports has increased from 74 to 148, with ambitions for at least 230 by 2030. Airports in smaller towns like Darbhanga in Bihar now provide direct connections to major cities, making flying a necessity rather than a luxury for many locals. Despite these advances, facilities at smaller airports remain basic and many Indians cannot afford to fly. The average annual income is less than the price of an economy-class airfare from the US, and most earn far less. In 2019, there were just 0.13 airline seats per person in India, compared with 0.52 in China and 3.03 in the US. The industry is increasingly dominated by IndiGo and Tata-owned airlines, as smaller competitors fail. Pilot shortages, like those experienced by Akasa Air, have also caused disruptions. Yet, experts believe India’s aviation expansion could reshape global air travel if its benefits reach more people across the country.

Indira Gandhi internasjonale lufthavn i New Delhi oppgraderes og er i ferd med å bli verdens nest travleste, kun bak Hartsfield-Jackson i Atlanta. Likevel er tog fortsatt det viktigste transportmiddelet for mange indere, med togreiser som overgår flyreiser 20 til 1. Bare rundt 3 % av befolkningen flyr ofte, men med 1,4 milliarder mennesker utgjør det likevel omtrent 42 millioner hyppige flyreisende—hovedsakelig studenter, yrkesaktive og forretningsfolk som ønsker raskere reiser nasjonalt og internasjonalt. Kapil Kaul fra CAPA India understreker at de neste par årene er avgjørende for at Indias luftfartssektor skal nå sine mål. Vekst har hittil vært viktigere enn profitt, men selskapene håper dette snart vil endre seg. Økende passasjertall forventes også å løfte fraktvirksomhet og tiltrekke utenlandske investeringer. På Indira Gandhi internasjonale blir reisende møtt av store skulpturer som viser Buddhas håndbevegelser. I 2012 håndterte flyplassen 30 millioner passasjerer; kapasiteten skal snart opp til 109 millioner. Oppgraderingene omfatter nå en fjerde rullebane, en hevet taxibane, elektriske TaxiBots og et bagasjesystem som sorterer 6 000 bager i timen. Airbus og Boeing har vært store vinnere. I år bestilte Air India totalt 470 fly (250 fra Airbus, 220 fra Boeing) til en verdi over 70 milliarder dollar, mens IndiGo bestilte ytterligere 500. Indiske flyselskaper har hatt en passasjervekst på 36 % siden 2022. Selv om internasjonale ankomster fortsatt er lave, legger lavprisselskaper stadig til nye utenlandsruter for å møte indisk etterspørsel etter utenlandsreiser. Direkte, rimelige flygninger fra Delhi og Mumbai til nye destinasjoner er nå tilgjengelige. Utvidelsen av infrastruktur skjer langt utenfor storbyene. Siden statsminister Narendra Modi tok over, har antallet flyplasser økt fra 74 til 148, og målet er minst 230 innen 2030. Flyplasser i småbyer som Darbhanga i Bihar gir nå direkteforbindelser til større byer—så flyreiser har blitt en nødvendighet for flere. Til tross for fremskrittene er fasilitetene på mindre flyplasser ofte enkle og mange indere har ikke råd til å fly. Gjennomsnittsinntekten er lavere enn prisen på en økonomibillett fra USA, og de fleste tjener enda mindre. I 2019 var det bare 0,13 flyseter per person i India, sammenlignet med 0,52 i Kina og 3,03 i USA. Bransjen domineres stadig mer av IndiGo og Tata-eide selskaper, da mindre aktører forsvinner. Mangel på piloter, som hos Akasa Air, har også ført til kansellerte avganger. Likevel tror eksperter Indias luftfartsvekst kan endre det globale markedet om fordelene fordeles bredere i landet.

article_content: Forget feeling guilty about the money you spend on beauty products—an industry now worth $160 billion. Financially, those investments might actually pay off. A series of landmark studies show that being attractive can significantly boost your lifetime earnings, by as much as $230,000 according to one estimate, and these advantages start early. A recent Vox video compiles decades of research showing that attractive people receive more attention—even in infancy—from both strangers and their own parents. As children grow, teachers often expect more from better-looking students, which can result in slightly better grades and a higher likelihood of earning a college degree. When it comes to the job market, numerous studies indicate that hiring managers are more likely to choose attractive job applicants over others with identical qualifications. In politics, a candidate’s appearance can even impact election outcomes, with studies linking beauty to electoral success. This may be because attractive people are often perceived as more competent, kind, and trustworthy. These patterns extend into various fields. For example, research has shown that attractive politicians tend to have better election odds, and even NFL players with more symmetrical faces command higher salaries. Symmetry is recognized by many psychologists as a key component of perceived attractiveness. On average, individuals with above-average looks earn more across nearly all professional sectors. Daniel Hamermesh, an economist and author of the book 'Beauty Pays,' calculated that very attractive people can make $230,000 more over a lifetime than less attractive peers. Height also plays a role: taller people earn more, with one study suggesting an additional $789 per year for each extra inch, and they may also be more likely to possess higher intelligence. This trend is also evident in legal settings. Studies suggest that attractive people are often given lighter fines and may win larger compensations in court. In contrast, studies found that heavier women tend to earn less as their BMI increases, regardless of qualifications. One referenced study noted a correlation between unattractiveness and a higher likelihood of engaging in criminal behavior, though causation is not clarified. Nevertheless, multiple studies support the idea that people perceived as attractive are rewarded in multiple areas of life, from the classroom to the courtroom. In summary, whether you were born with good looks or invest to improve your appearance, there is strong evidence that being attractive tends to pay off.

Økonomisk sett kan disse investeringene faktisk lønne seg. En rekke viktige studier viser at det å være attraktiv kan øke livslønnene dine betydelig – så mye som 230 000 dollar mer ifølge ett anslag – og fordelene starter tidlig. En ny Vox-video samler tiår med forskning som viser at attraktive mennesker får mer oppmerksomhet – allerede fra spedbarnsalderen – både fra fremmede og foreldre. Etter hvert som barn vokser opp, har lærere ofte høyere forventninger til penere elever, noe som kan føre til litt bedre karakterer og større sjanse for å ta en universitetsutdannelse. Når det gjelder arbeidsmarkedet, indikerer flere studier at rekrutterere oftere velger attraktive søkere fremfor andre med identiske kvalifikasjoner. Også innen politikken kan utseendet påvirke valgresultater, med flere studier som kobler skjønnhet til valgsuksess. Dette kan skyldes at attraktive personer ofte oppfattes som mer kompetente, snille og til å stole på. Disse mønstrene gjelder i flere bransjer. Forskning har for eksempel vist at attraktive politikere har bedre sjanser for å vinne valg, og til og med NFL-spillere med mer symmetriske ansikt tjener bedre. Symmetri regnes av mange psykologer som en nøkkelfaktor for attraktivitet. I snitt tjener personer med over gjennomsnittlig utseende mer på tvers av nesten alle yrker. Økonomen Daniel Hamermesh, forfatter av boken ‘Beauty Pays’, har beregnet at svært attraktive personer kan tjene 230 000 dollar mer i løpet av livet enn mindre attraktive. Høyde spiller også inn: En studie anslår at man tjener 789 dollar mer i året for hver ekstra tomme, og høyere personer har også større sannsynlighet for å være mer intelligente. Denne trenden sees også i rettssystemet. Studier tyder på at attraktive personer ofte får mildere bøter og kan vinne større erstatningssummer i retten. Samtidig har studier funnet at tyngre kvinner har lavere lønn etter hvert som BMI øker, uavhengig av kvalifikasjoner. En referert studie påpeker en sammenheng mellom det å være lite attraktiv og høyere sannsynlighet for kriminell atferd, men årsaksforholdet er uklart. Likevel støtter flere studier ideen om at attraktive personer får fordeler på mange livsområder, fra klasserommet til rettssalen. Oppsummert: Enten du er født pen eller investerer for å bli det, er det sterke bevis for at attraktivitet vanligvis lønner seg.

article_content: A widespread technical malfunction at Optus left more than 10 million Australians and thousands of businesses without mobile and internet service for roughly 12 hours. The disruption began soon after 4 am and continued until about 6 pm, causing hospital phones and payment systems to fail. Public transport in Victoria was impacted, as were customers of other providers relying on Optus infrastructure such as Amaysim, Aussie Broadband, and Moose Mobile. Optus CEO Kelly Bayer Rosmarin reported there was no evidence of a cyber attack, identifying the incident as a technical network issue, though a detailed investigation is ongoing. She dismissed speculation that previous staff reductions contributed to the outage. Customers described real-life effects, including missing urgent medical news and failures of internet-dependent household devices. Rosmarin apologized for the disruption, emphasizing efforts to restore service promptly and vowing a thorough review. The outage follows last year’s major Optus data breach, which was the largest in Australian history, but the company maintains the two incidents are unrelated.

Også kollektivtransport i Victoria ble rammet, i tillegg til kunder av andre leverandører som er avhengige av Optus-nettverket, slik som Amaysim, Aussie Broadband og Moose Mobile. Optus-sjef Kelly Bayer Rosmarin opplyste at det ikke er noe tegn til dataangrep, og at hendelsen skyldes et teknisk nettverksproblem – men en grundig undersøkelse pågår. Hun avviste spekulasjoner om at tidligere nedskjæringer har hatt betydning for utfallet. Kunder har fortalt om hvordan feilen påvirket hverdagen, blant annet ved å gå glipp av viktige medisinske beskjeder og funksjonssvikt i internettavhengige husholdningsapparater. Rosmarin ba om unnskyldning for problemene, understreket innsatsen for å gjenopprette tjenestene raskt og lover en full gjennomgang. Hendelsen kommer etter at Optus i fjor opplevde det største datainnbruddet i Australias historie, men selskapet sier at de to episodene ikke henger sammen.

article_content: NIAMEY, Niger — Hamsa Diakite struggles to recall the last time her family of eight had a decent meal. She used to support them by selling fried bread, but since the coup in Niger three months ago, sanctions against the West African country have severely limited incomes and left millions like Hamsa facing new hardships without aid. “Not only is food very expensive, but school supplies have also doubled in price. I have to clothe my children and, above all, take care of their illnesses,” said the 65-year-old. After elite soldiers overthrew Niger’s democratically elected President Mohamed Bazoum on July 26, the country was hit with economic sanctions from ECOWAS and countries including the United States who had provided significant aid for health, security, and infrastructure. Neighboring countries closed their borders with Niger, and more than 70% of Niger’s electricity, previously supplied by Nigeria, was cut off after financial transactions were suspended. Niger’s external assets were frozen, and hundreds of millions of dollars in aid withheld. The sanctions, among the harshest yet imposed by the regional bloc, aim to stop a wave of coups in Africa’s volatile Sahel region. However, they have primarily impacted Niger's more than 25 million people, rather than the military leadership. “We are quickly running out of funding and medicines. People are running out of food,” said Louise Aubin, the United Nations resident coordinator in Niger. The junta has since asked her to leave the country, alleging the UN is preventing Niger's participation in its activities, though the UN has not commented on these claims. Aubin mentioned some positive responses from Niger’s neighbors about opening borders for a humanitarian corridor but gave no details. Niger, the world’s third least developed country according to UN estimates, received $1.77 billion in assistance in 2021, over half for humanitarian aid and social services. This aid is now at risk. Niger’s 2023 budget, which depended heavily on external support, has been slashed by 40%. Sanctions meant to deter the junta and President Bazoum remains under house arrest, but the military has set up a transitional government that could remain in place for up to three years. This transition appears to have support from many Nigeriens dissatisfied with the previous government, according to Seidik Abba, president of a Sahel-focused think tank. Despite hardships, many Niamey residents support the coup and minimize Western concerns, viewing the military as legitimate because of popular backing. For some, the difficulties caused by sanctions are seen as an acceptable sacrifice. “Love of homeland makes us forget the tough times the country is going through,” said junta supporter Abdou Ali. Aid workers and observers see the situation differently. “We are trying to respond to a catastrophic situation,” said Dr. Soumana Sounna Sofiane, secretary-general of Niger’s pharmacists’ union. Essential medicines are running low across drugstores at a time of public health crises like cholera. Pharmacies have begun providing alternative medications for patients. Food supplies are also dwindling. Inflation and high prices are making it more difficult for people to make ends meet, according to the World Food Program, which reported that even before the coup, 3.3 million in Niger were facing acute food insecurity. Niger, West Africa’s second largest nation by landmass, is landlocked and dependent on trade with neighbors, now suspended. Food and medicines were among the top imports last year. At the Benin border, trucks carrying goods and relief line up for kilometers, waiting to enter Niger, though some are headed for other countries. Over 9,000 metric tons of WFP cargo, including specialized food meant to treat and prevent malnutrition in Niger and Burkina Faso, remain blocked. The UN’s Louise Aubin worries the goal of reaching 80% of 4.4 million targeted people with humanitarian aid this year may not be met. Sanctions have deeply affected many families. Almost one in five Nigeriens relies on livestock, and exports to Nigeria, worth $10 million in 2021, are now halted. Prices for basic goods keep rising. The price of a 25-kilogram (55-pound) bag of rice, a staple food, has climbed more than 50% since sanctions began. “Our stocks are running out overnight because nothing crosses the borders. When they are gone, we’ll have to close our stores,” said Ambouta Idrissa, who manages a large cereal depot in Niamey. Some businesses have closed due to the high cost of powering generators after Nigeria cut electricity. For Nigeriens like Diakite, the main worry is ensuring her children don’t go to bed hungry. She says her hope fades daily. “For how long can we hold on?” she asked. — Asadu reported from Abuja, Nigeria.
translated_content: NIAMEY, Niger — Hamsa Diakite sliter med å huske sist familien hennes på åtte hadde et ordentlig måltid. Hun forsørget dem ved å selge frityrstekt brød, men etter kuppet i Niger for tre måneder siden har sanksjonene mot det vestafrikanske landet hardt rammet inntektene og etterlatt millioner som Hamsa i nye vanskeligheter uten bistand. «Ikke bare er mat veldig dyrt, men skolemateriell har også doblet seg i pris. Jeg må kle barna mine og, fremfor alt, ta vare på sykdommene deres,» sa 65-åringen. Etter at elitesoldater styrtet Nigers demokratisk valgte president Mohamed Bazoum 26. juli, ble landet rammet av økonomiske sanksjoner fra ECOWAS og land, inkludert USA, som tidligere hadde gitt betydelig bistand til helse, sikkerhet og infrastruktur. Nabolandene stengte grensene med Niger, og mer enn 70 % av landets elektrisitet, tidligere levert av Nigeria, ble kuttet etter at finansielle transaksjoner ble stoppet. Nigers utenlandske eiendeler ble frosset, og hundrevis av millioner dollar i bistand holdes tilbake. Sanksjonene, noen av de tøffeste som er innført av regionalblokken, har som mål å stoppe bølgen av kupp i det ustabile Sahel. Likevel har de først og fremst rammet Nigers over 25 millioner innbyggere, heller enn militærledelsen. «Vi går raskt tom for midler og medisiner. Folk går tom for mat,» sa Louise Aubin, FNs landskoordinator i Niger. Juntaen har siden bedt henne forlate landet og hevder at FN hindrer Nigers deltakelse i sine aktiviteter, men FN har ikke kommentert påstandene. Aubin nevnte at det har kommet flere positive svar fra Nigers naboland om å åpne grenser for en humanitær korridor, men ga ingen detaljer. Niger, verdens tredje minst utviklede land ifølge FN, mottok 1,77 milliarder dollar i bistand i 2021, over halvparten til humanitær hjelp og sosiale tjenester. Denne bistanden er nå truet. Nigers budsjett for 2023, som var sterkt avhengig av ekstern støtte, er kuttet med 40 %. Sanksjonene skulle avskrekke juntaen, og president Bazoum er fortsatt i husarrest, men hæren har etablert en overgangsregjering som kan bli sittende i opptil tre år. Denne overgangen ser ut til å ha støtte fra mange nigerere som var misfornøyde med den forrige regjeringen, ifølge Seidik Abba, leder av en Sahel-tenketank. Tross vanskeligheter støtter mange i Niamey kuppet og avviser vestlige bekymringer, og ser på militæret som legitimt på grunn av folkelig støtte. For noen er problemene sanksjonene har skapt et akseptabelt offer. «Kjærligheten til hjemlandet får oss til å glemme de tøffe tidene landet opplever,» sa junta-supporteren Abdou Ali. Bistandsarbeidere og andre ser situasjonen annerledes. «Vi prøver å håndtere en katastrofal situasjon,» sa Dr. Soumana Sounna Sofiane, generalsekretær for Nigers apotekerforbund. Essensiell medisin blir mangelvare på apotekene samtidig som landet har helsekriser som kolera. Apotekene har begynt å tilby alternative medisiner til pasientene. Mateknivåene synker også. Inflasjon og høye priser gjør det vanskelig for folk å få endene til å møtes, ifølge Verdens matvareprogram, som rapporterte at allerede før kuppet opplevde 3,3 millioner i Niger akutt matusikkerhet. Niger, Vest-Afrikas nest største land i areal, er innlandsstat og avhengig av handel med naboland – nå stoppet opp. Mat og medisiner var blant de viktigste importene i fjor. Ved grensen til Benin står lastebiler med varer og nødhjelp i kø meter etter meter, og venter på å slippe inn i Niger, selv om noen skal videre til andre land. Over 9 000 tonn med WFP-last, inkludert spesialmat for å behandle og forebygge underernæring i Niger og Burkina Faso, står fortsatt fast. FNs Louise Aubin frykter at målet om å nå 80 % av 4,4 millioner utvalgte med nødhjelp i år, ikke nås. Sanksjonene har rammet mange familier hardt. Nesten én av fem nigerere livnærer seg på husdyr, og eksporten til Nigeria verdt 10 millioner dollar i 2021 er nå stanset. Prisene på basisvarer fortsetter å stige. Prisen på en 25-kilos sekk ris, en hovednæringskilde, har økt med over 50 % siden sanksjonene begynte. «Lageret vårt tømmes over natten fordi ingenting kommer inn over grensene. Når det er tomt, må vi stenge butikken,» sier Ambouta Idrissa, leder for et stort korndepot i Niamey. Noen virksomheter har stengt fordi det har blitt for dyrt å drive på generator etter strømmen forsvant fra Nigeria. For nigerere som Diakite er den største bekymringen å sørge for at barna ikke legger seg sultne. Hun sier håpet svinner dag for dag. «Hvor lenge kan vi holde ut?» spør hun. — Asadu rapporterte fra Abuja, Nigeria.

article_content: A tragic incident occurred in Oakworth, Keighley, West Yorkshire, where a four-year-old boy named Riley Turner was killed while sleeping beside his twin brother, Kenzie. Riley’s stepfather discovered him and desperately called for help. Kenzie was unharmed in the incident. The police and ambulance service responded to the home on Harewood Road at 4:40 am. Despite emergency efforts, Riley was pronounced dead later at Airedale General Hospital. Riley lived with his mother, Sharon Smith, her partner Guy Earwaker, and his siblings. The incident has deeply affected the family, who are being supported by relatives and friends. A 32-year-old man, reportedly from the area, was arrested on suspicion of murder nearly seven hours after the incident, following a search that ended in a nearby railway tunnel. Police cordoned off the street and searched for evidence at the scene, including bins, garages, and gutters. Local residents expressed shock and sorrow, leaving tributes outside the family’s home. Keighley’s mayor, George Metcalf, also shared condolences with the family. West Yorkshire Police have launched a murder investigation. They confirmed that the suspect is in custody and that enquiries are ongoing, but have not released further details at this stage.

Til tross for livreddende innsats ble Riley senere erklært død på Airedale General Hospital. Riley bodde sammen med moren Sharon Smith, hennes partner Guy Earwaker og søsknene sine. Hendelsen har preget familien sterkt, og de får nå støtte fra slekt og venner. En 32 år gammel mann, angivelig fra området, ble pågrepet mistenkt for drap nesten syv timer etter hendelsen, etter en leteaksjon som endte i en nærliggende jernbanetunnel. Politiet sperret av gaten og lette etter spor på stedet, blant annet i søppelkasser, garasjer og sluk. Lokale innbyggere uttrykte sjokk og sorg, og la ned blomster utenfor familiens hjem. Keighleys ordfører, George Metcalf, uttrykte også medfølelse med familien. West Yorkshire-politiet har startet en drapsetterforskning. De bekreftet at den mistenkte er i varetekt og at etterforskningen pågår, men ytterligere informasjon er ikke gitt på nåværende tidspunkt.

article_content:
A devastating fire in Vile Parle claimed the life of 95-year-old Harshada Janardhan Pathak, Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) officials confirmed. Preliminary investigation suggests that a short circuit was the probable cause. Pathak, who lived alone, was home during the fire, possibly watching TV when flames started at her apartment's main entrance and spread rapidly. Her body was later discovered in the kitchen; officials believe she tried to seek safety there but may have lost consciousness from smoke inhalation before sustaining fatal burns.

Officials initially speculated a Diwali diya might be involved, but this was ruled out after no such evidence was found at the site. Flammable household items, including furniture and electrical appliances, intensified the fire. The apartment building's fire-fighting system was partially damaged, with some hosepipes burning and becoming unusable, particularly on the second floor where the incident occurred.

Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) disaster officials reported the fire started around 7:27 pm on a Friday in flat 201 on the building's second floor. The blaze remained restricted to the flat's electrical installations.

Ahead of Diwali, authorities have issued advisories urging residents to celebrate safely—suggesting cotton clothing for lighting lamps or bursting crackers. Following a Bombay High Court order, municipal commissioner and state-appointed administrator Iqbal Singh Chahal further appealed for citizens to use eco-friendly fireworks.

Pathak, som bodde alene, var hjemme da brannen brøt ut—muligens mens hun så på TV—da flammene oppstod ved hovedinngangen og spredte seg raskt. Hun ble senere funnet på kjøkkenet; tjenestemenn tror hun forsøkte å søke tilflukt der, men kan ha mistet bevisstheten av røykforgiftning før hun pådro seg dødelige brannskader.

Brihanmumbai kommunes (BMC) beredskapstjeneste rapporterte at brannen startet rundt 19:27 fredag i leilighet 201, som ligger i andre etasje. Brannen forble begrenset til leilighetens elektriske installasjoner.

I forkant av Diwali har myndighetene gitt ut advarsler og oppfordrer innbyggerne til å feire trygt—blant annet foreslås det å bruke bomullsklær når man tenner lamper eller fyrer opp fyrverkeri. article_content: All five remaining inmates at the center of the Mississippi pardons controversy have now been released from prison. Last week, Mississippi's Supreme Court upheld over 200 pardons issued by former Governor Haley Barbour as he left office, rejecting a legal challenge from Attorney General Jim Hood. In a 77-page, 6-3 decision, the court ruled that pardons cannot be overturned by the judiciary. Attorney General Hood argued proper notice of the pardons was not published in newspapers, but the court ruled that the final authority lies with the governor. Writing for the majority, Justice Jess Dickinson acknowledged the concerns of victims and their families, stating that while their interest is understandable, it is the governor who decides if publication requirements have been met. After the court's decision, Barbour said it reaffirmed longstanding state law, but admitted it was a difficult outcome for the victims' families. In his dissent, Justice Michael Randolph called the ruling 'a stunning victory for some lawless convicted felons, and an immeasurable loss for law-abiding citizens.' Hood argued the state Constitution requires notice of pardons to be published for 30 days in newspapers in the area where crimes occurred. Barbour's lawyers countered that previous rulings had found the 30-day notice rule to be unconstitutional. Thursday's ruling settles the matter, but Hood said he will seek to have the notice requirement restored. He expressed sympathy for victims and their families, stating they are the ones who lost as the criminals have won. Among the 214 pardoned inmates were four convicted murderers who worked as trusties at the governor's mansion. Critics argued the governor did not consider the victims' families before issuing the pardons. All four, as well as an armed robber pardoned by Barbour, had been free while the issue went through the courts, but the decision now officially freed them. The remaining five inmates, who stayed in prison pending the ruling, have also been released. Barbour defends his pardons, saying the former inmates were rehabilitated. CNN's Martin Savidge and Joe Sutton contributed to this report.
translated_content: Alle de fem gjenværende innsatte som sto i sentrum av benådingskontroversen i Mississippi, er nå løslatt fra fengsel. Forrige uke opprettholdt Mississippis høyesterett over 200 benådinger gitt av tidligere guvernør Haley Barbour da han gikk av, og avviste en rettslig utfordring fra riksadvokat Jim Hood. I en 77-siders avgjørelse med stemmetallet 6-3, fastslo retten at benådinger ikke kan omgjøres av rettsvesenet. Riksadvokat Hood hevdet at korrekt kunngjøring om benådingene ikke ble gitt i avisene, men retten avgjorde at den endelige myndigheten ligger hos guvernøren. I flertallsuttalelsen anerkjente dommer Jess Dickinson offerenes og deres familiers bekymringer, og uttalte at selv om deres interesse er forståelig, er det guvernøren som avgjør om publiseringskravet er oppfylt. Etter rettens avgjørelse sa Barbour at den bekreftet langvarig statlig lov, men innrømmet at dette var et vanskelig utfall for ofrenes familier. I sin dissens kalte dommer Michael Randolph avgjørelsen 'en oppsiktsvekkende seier for noen lovløse domfelte, og et umålelig tap for lovlydige innbyggere.' Hood argumenterte at delstatens grunnlov krever at kunngjøring om benådinger publiseres i 30 dager i aviser der forbrytelsene fant sted. Barbours advokater svarte at tidligere avgjørelser har slått fast at 30-dagers kravet er ukonstitusjonelt. Torsdagens avgjørelse avslutter saken, men Hood sa at han vil forsøke å få kravet gjeninnført. Han uttrykte sympati for ofrene og deres familier, og uttalte at det er de som har tapt mens kriminelle har vunnet. Blant de 214 benådedde innsatte var fire dømte mordere som jobbet som betrodde hjelpere på guvernørens residens. Kritikere mente guvernøren ikke tok hensyn til ofrenes familier før benådingen ble gitt. Alle de fire, samt en væpnet raner som også ble benådet av Barbour, hadde vært fri mens saken gikk i rettssystemet, men avgjørelsen friga dem nå offisielt. De fem gjenstående innsatte, som ble værende i fengsel i påvente av avgjørelsen, er også løslatt. Barbour forsvarer sine benådinger og sier de tidligere innsatte var rehabilitert. CNNs Martin Savidge og Joe Sutton bidro til denne rapporten.
post_content: Big legal news in Mississippi: State Supreme Court upheld 200+ controversial pardons by ex-Gov. Barbour. Victims' families upset, but court says the governor has the final say. #Mississippi #PardonDebate

article_content: The FBI announced on Tuesday that it is actively investigating high-frequency trading firms to determine whether their use of ultra-fast computers and sophisticated algorithms constitutes insider trading. Authorities are examining whether these firms have exploited nonpublic, rapidly changing information to trade ahead of competitors. High-frequency trading and related practices have come under increasing regulatory scrutiny in recent months. The investigation, known as the 'High-Speed Trading Initiative,' began about a year ago and is still in its early stages, according to FBI officials who spoke to the Wall Street Journal. The FBI has assigned a significant number of agents to the case, focusing on proprietary trading outfits and broker operations that execute trades for clients such as mutual funds and pension plans. 'Many people in government are focused on this issue and are concerned it may violate the law,' an FBI spokesperson said to the Journal. 'There is significant concern that high-frequency traders are accessing material nonpublic information ahead of others and trading on it.' The Securities and Exchange Commission, Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and Financial Industry Regulatory Authority are assisting the FBI with its investigation. In the past four and a half years, insider trading charges have been brought against 90 individuals, resulting in 79 convictions or guilty pleas and no acquittals. News of the investigation emerged one day after bestselling author Michael Lewis released a book alleging that some high-frequency traders rig the market for their own benefit.

article_content: Nuno Espirito Santo, who guided Al Ittihad to the Saudi Pro League title last season, has been dismissed after a series of poor results, according to the club. This season, Al Ittihad have lost five league matches as well as a game in the Asian Champions League. Nuno's departure came after a 2-0 loss to Air Force Club of Iraq in the Asian Champions League on Monday. The Portuguese manager, who previously managed Tottenham Hotspur and Wolverhampton Wanderers (2017-2021), took charge at Al Ittihad in July last year. Although he led the Jeddah-based team to the Saudi title, reports suggested a strained relationship with striker Karim Benzema, who joined the club in June amid a wave of foreign signings. In a statement released late Tuesday on X (formerly Twitter), Al Ittihad said, 'The club has announced the end of its contract with Portuguese coach Nuno Santo. This decision comes after a comprehensive technical evaluation of the period during which he was responsible for coaching the first team.' Assistant coach Hassan Khalifa will serve as interim manager while the club searches for a permanent replacement. After the defeat in Iraq, Al Ittihad suffered their first loss in this season's Asian Champions League and have failed to win in their last five matches, dropping to sixth in the Saudi Pro League standings. In related news, Dutch coach Alfred Schreuder has left his position at United Arab Emirates club Al Ain after just six months, amid reports he could join Al Ittihad. Al Ain said in a statement on X, 'An agreement was reached with Dutch coach Schreuder to terminate his contract by mutual consent due to a lack of harmony between the coach and his assistant technical staff with the company’s institutional work system.' Schreuder, 51, has been linked by local media to the vacant managerial role at Al Ittihad.

article_content: The European Space Agency (ESA) has revealed that its research satellite, GOCE—nicknamed the 'Ferrari of space' for its streamlined engineering—re-entered Earth's atmosphere and is believed to have come down in the South Atlantic Ocean. The satellite, weighing 1,100 kilograms (2,425 pounds), ran out of fuel in October and re-entered around midnight GMT on Monday. Its orbital path took it over Siberia, the western Pacific, the eastern Indian Ocean, and Antarctica. While most of GOCE disintegrated during re-entry, tracking information from both U.S. and European agencies suggests that some fragments likely landed in the ocean just south of the Falkland Islands, off the South American coast. Launched in March 2009 from Russia's Plesetsk Cosmodrome on a Rockot launch vehicle, GOCE was designed to map Earth's gravity and generate a highly precise geoid model, which represents the shape of global sea level. Costing $466 million, the satellite operated at a record-low orbital altitude of around 260 kilometers, delivering breakthroughs on ocean currents, sea level, the behavior of ice, the structure of the Earth, as well as atmospheric density and winds. GOCE marked ESA's first uncontrolled satellite re-entry since 1987. Before its descent, ESA emphasized that the risk of any harm to people from space debris was exceedingly rare—lower even than the chance of being hit by a meteorite. A coordinated effort involving ESA’s Space Debris Office and the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee monitored the satellite’s return to Earth. Heiner Klinkrad, head of ESA’s Space Debris Office, pointed out that, at one tonne, GOCE was just a small fraction of the 100–150 tonnes of artificial objects that enter Earth's atmosphere each year. Over the past 56 years of spaceflight, about 15,000 tonnes of human-made debris have fallen without a single injury being documented. According to international law—the 1972 UN Convention on Liability for Damage from Space Objects—the country responsible for a satellite is liable for any damages its debris might cause. In GOCE’s case, that responsibility would fall to Russia, its launching state.
translated_content: Den europeiske romfartsorganisasjonen (ESA) har opplyst at forskningssatellitten GOCE—kalt ‘rommets Ferrari’ på grunn av sin aerodynamiske utforming—gjeninntok jordens atmosfære og antas å ha falt ned i det sørlige Atlanterhavet. Satellitten, som veide 1 100 kilo, gikk tom for drivstoff i oktober og kom inn i atmosfæren rundt midnatt GMT natt til mandag. Banen gikk over Sibir, det vestlige Stillehavet, det østlige Indiahavet og Antarktis. Selv om mesteparten av GOCE ble ødelagt under gjeninntreden, indikerer sporingsdata fra amerikanske og europeiske byråer at enkelte fragmenter sannsynligvis havnet i havet like sør for Falklandsøyene, utenfor Sør-Amerikas kyst. GOCE ble skutt opp fra Plesetsk-kosmodromen i Russland i mars 2009 med en Rockot-rakett. Satellitten hadde som oppdrag å kartlegge jordens gravitasjonsfelt og lage en svært presis geoidmodell, som viser hvordan jordens overflate ville sett ut om alt vann sto i ro. GOCE kostet 466 millioner dollar og opererte i en rekordlav bane på omtrent 260 kilometers høyde. Den ga banebrytende innsikt i havstrømmer, havnivå, isbevegelser, jordens indre struktur og atmosfærens tetthet og vind. Dette var ESAs første ukontrollerte satellitt som reiste inn i atmosfæren siden 1987. Før nedfallet understreket ESA at risikoen for skade på personer fra romskrot var ekstremt liten—mindre enn å bli truffet av en meteoritt. En samordnet innsats fra blant annet ESAs Space Debris Office og Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee overvåket satellittens retur. Heiner Klinkrad, leder for ESAs Space Debris Office, påpekte at én tonn GOCE kun utgjorde en liten andel av de 100–150 tonn menneskeskapte objekt som årlig går inn i atmosfæren. I løpet av 56 år med romfart har rundt 15 000 tonn kunstig skrot falt ned uten at noen har blitt skadet. I henhold til internasjonal lov—FNs konvensjon fra 1972 om ansvar for skade forårsaket av romobjekter—er utskytningslandet ansvarlig for eventuelle skader fra vrakdeler. For GOCE er dette Russland.

article_content:
A significant build-up of Serbian military forces near the Kosovo border has raised alarms among Kosovo officials, who have compared the situation to Russia's actions prior to its invasion of Ukraine. The Biden administration recently observed what it called a “worrying cycle” of increasing tensions and sporadic violence between the two Balkan countries, whose relationship remains strained due to longstanding ethnic divisions.

Tensions peaked in late September when heavily armed Serbian gunmen carried out a deadly attack in northern Kosovo. In response, U.S. officials noted what they described as an "unprecedented" mobilization of Serbian military assets along the border. According to Kosovo’s Foreign Minister, Donika Gervalla-Schwarz, speaking to German broadcaster Deutschlandfunk, “There has never been this kind of concentration of troops in recent years. The weaponry they have there, the tanks—it gives us a bad feeling because we don't know how the international community will respond.” She drew parallels between Serbia’s build-up and Russia’s maneuvers before invading Ukraine in 2022.

Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is friendly with Serbia’s leadership, downplayed his own pre-invasion troop movements at the time, as has Serbia regarding its current mobilizations. Serbia has also tried to quell fears of a potential invasion.

Kosovo’s population is majority ethnic Albanian, while most ethnic Serbs—who are a minority—live in the north. Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008, a move Serbia refuses to recognize, though nearly 100 countries including the U.S. do. After the breakup of Yugoslavia, a violent conflict between Serbia and Kosovo’s Albanian population occurred from 1998–1999, prompting NATO intervention.

Tensions remain, particularly in northern Kosovo. On September 24, a group of armed Serb gunmen attacked, killing a Kosovar police officer and storming a monastery. The incident, which resulted in the deaths of several attackers, represented one of the most serious escalations in years and was condemned in the West, increasing fears that further violence could follow.

In response, NATO announced plans to increase the size of its peacekeeping mission—Kosovo Force (KFOR)—with several hundred additional British troops. The mission, established in 1999, is intended to deter hostility against Kosovo and maintain security according to its mandate.

NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg urged all parties to de-escalate tensions and participate in European Union-facilitated dialogue, emphasizing that resolving outstanding issues is key to lasting regional stability.

The U.S. publicly highlighted the build-up of Serbian artillery, tanks, and infantry units at the Kosovo border. White House National Security Council Spokesperson John Kirby called these moves destabilizing and urged Serbia to withdraw its forces. Serbia later reported withdrawing about half of its troops. Kosovo officials say the country remains on high alert.

Kosovo’s Prime Minister Albin Kurti posted on X (formerly Twitter) that authorities had obtained documentation confirming the September attack was part of a coordinated plan to annex the north of Kosovo across 37 positions and to establish a corridor to Serbia for arms and troop supplies. Serbia denies any involvement.

Biden-administrasjonen har nylig beskrevet det de kaller en "bekymringsfull syklus" av økende spenning og sporadisk vold mellom de to balkanske landene, som fortsatt har et anstrengt forhold grunnet langvarige etniske motsetninger.

Spenningen nådde et høydepunkt i slutten av september da tungt bevæpnede serbiske væpnede menn utførte et dødelig angrep i Nord-Kosovo. Som svar bemerket amerikanske tjenestemenn en "enestående" mobilisering av serbiske militære ressurser langs grensen. Ifølge Kosovos utenriksminister, Donika Gervalla-Schwarz, til den tyske kringkasteren Deutschlandfunk: "Det har aldri vært en slik konsentrasjon av tropper på flere år. Våpnene de har der, stridsvognene – det gir oss en dårlig følelse fordi vi ikke vet hvordan det internasjonale samfunnet vil reagere." Hun trakk paralleller mellom Serbias militæroppbygging og Russlands bevegelser før invasjonen av Ukraina i 2022.

Russlands president Vladimir Putin, som har gode forbindelser med Serbias ledelse, bagatelliserte egne troppeters bevegelser før invasjonen den gang, og Serbia har gjort det samme med sine nåværende mobiliseringer. Serbia har også prøvd å roe ned frykten for en mulig invasjon.

Kosovos befolkning er hovedsakelig etnisk albansk, mens etniske serbere – som er en minoritet – for det meste bor i nord. Kosovo erklærte uavhengighet fra Serbia i 2008, noe Serbia nekter å anerkjenne, men nesten 100 land inkludert USA har gjort det. Etter oppløsningen av Jugoslavia oppstod det voldelige konflikter mellom Serbia og Kosovos albanske befolkning fra 1998 til 1999, som førte til NATO-intervensjon.

Spenningene består, særlig i Nord-Kosovo. Den 24. september angrep en gruppe bevæpnede serbere, drepte en kosovisk politimann og stormet et kloster. Hendelsen, som endte med at flere angripere ble drept, representerte en av de mest alvorlige opptrappingene på flere år og ble fordømt i Vesten, noe som økte frykten for ytterligere vold.

Som svar kunngjorde NATO planer om å styrke sin fredsbevarende styrke – Kosovo Force (KFOR) – med flere hundre britiske soldater. Styrken, etablert i 1999, har som mandat å avskrekke fiendtlighet mot Kosovo og opprettholde sikkerheten.

NATOs generalsekretær Jens Stoltenberg ba alle parter om å de-eskalere og delta i EU-tilrettelagt dialog, og understreket at løsning av utestående spørsmål er nøkkelen til varig stabilitet i regionen.

USA har offentliggjort serbisk oppbygging av artilleri, stridsvogner og infanterienheter ved Kosovo-grensen. John Kirby, talsmann for Det hvite hus' nasjonale sikkerhetsråd, kalte dette destabiliserende og ba Serbia trekke tilbake styrkene. Serbia har senere rapportert å ha trukket tilbake omtrent halvparten av troppene. Kosoviske myndigheter sier landet fortsatt er i høy beredskap.

Kosovos statsminister Albin Kurti skrev på X (tidligere Twitter) at myndighetene har fått dokumentasjon som bekrefter at angrepet i september var del av en koordinert plan om å annektere Nord-Kosovo over 37 posisjoner og etablere en korridor til Serbia for å føre inn våpen og soldater. Serbia benekter all innblanding.

article_content: The unimaginable grief following the AirAsia Flight QZ8501 crash has left one family mourning the loss of seven relatives. To date, only two of them have been identified among the 37 bodies recovered, out of the 162 passengers and crew onboard. The family gathered at a funeral home in Surabaya to honor The Meiji Thejakusuma and her daughter, Stevie Gunaman, who had celebrated her 10th birthday just weeks before the flight. They, along with five other family members, were headed to Singapore for a New Year's holiday. The rest of their group—Stevie’s father, grandmother, brother, sister, and her sister’s fiancé—have yet to be found. Suyono Tedjakusuma, a relative, spoke of the deep anguish and the painful wait to learn the fate of the missing. Relatives and friends visited throughout the week to pay tribute, describing The Meiji as a hardworking and compassionate businesswoman and Stevie as an optimistic, joyful child. During a Buddhist mourning service, attendees lit candles and folded symbolic paper money to honor their loved ones and offer them comfort in the afterlife. Initially, family members clung to hope for survivors, but as news came that The Meiji and Stevie’s bodies had been recovered, their dreams of a miracle faded. Now, as they prepare the funerals, the family continues to monitor updates, desperate for news about those still missing. Suyono shared, 'I cannot accept this. I cannot believe it. Where are my family's bodies? Where is my mother? My heart is breaking.' For relatives, the tragedy feels like an endless nightmare. The Meiji’s 46th birthday, meant to be spent in Singapore, instead became the day her body was found.

Familien samlet seg på et begravelsesbyrå i Surabaya for å hedre The Meiji Thejakusuma og datteren hennes, Stevie Gunaman, som feiret sin 10-årsdag bare noen uker før flyturen. De, sammen med fem andre familiemedlemmer, var på vei til Singapore for å feire nyttår. Resten av gruppen – Stevies far, bestemor, bror, søster og søsterens forlovede – er fortsatt savnet. Suyono Tedjakusuma, en slektning, uttrykte den dype sorgen og den krevende ventetiden for å få vite skjebnen til de savnede. Slekt og venner kom for å minnes i løpet av uken, og beskrev The Meiji som en hardtarbeidende og omsorgsfull forretningskvinne, og Stevie som en optimistisk og livsglad jente. Under en buddhistisk sørgeseremoni tente deltakerne lys og brettet symbolsk papirpenger for å hedre sine kjære og gi dem trøst i etterlivet. I starten klamret familien seg til håpet om overlevende, men da beskjeden kom om at The Meiji og Stevies kropper var funnet, forsvant mirakel-håpet. Nå som de forbereder begravelsene, følger familien nøye med på nyhetene, i håp om informasjon om de som fortsatt er savnet. Suyono sa: 'Jeg kan ikke akseptere dette. Jeg kan ikke tro det. Hvor er likene til familien min? Hvor er moren min? Hjertet mitt er knust.' For de pårørende føles tragedien som et mareritt man ikke kan våkne fra. The Meijis 46-årsdag, som egentlig skulle feires i Singapore, ble i stedet dagen hun ble funnet.

article_content: On Wednesday, BlackBerry took significant steps to revive its fortunes, unveiling a new corporate identity, two smartphones, and the ambitious BlackBerry 10 operating system. Formerly known as Research In Motion, the company is now officially BlackBerry. The central question now falls to consumers: will BlackBerry’s new Z10 (a full touchscreen device) and Q10 (which retains the hallmark keyboard) persuade buyers to pick them over iPhones or Android devices? Reviews of BlackBerry 10 have so far been mixed, but there are encouraging signs. Here are five reasons BlackBerry 10 could attract both loyal followers and new users: 1. Enhanced Productivity Features: Large corporations and government agencies have long been BlackBerry’s most dedicated clients. With a shift in workplace trends towards personal device use, BlackBerry 10 has prioritized productivity and speed. The new 'Balance' feature divides the phone into separate work and personal profiles (available for those connected to BlackBerry Enterprise Service 10), helping IT departments safeguard sensitive information while allowing users full access to personal apps and data. This solution eliminates the need to carry two phones for work and personal life. 2. Unified Communications: At the BlackBerry 10 launch, executives showcased 'BlackBerry Hub,' a feature that collects all notifications in one easily accessible place. By swiping from anywhere on the phone, users can view updates from social media, email, calendar, BBM, and more—organized according to individual preferences. The system allows up to eight apps to run simultaneously, making task-switching seamless. BlackBerry Messenger (BBM) also gains new features, including video chat and the ability to share your screen with other BB10 users. 3. Growing App Library: BlackBerry has stocked its app store with over 70,000 apps for BB10’s launch, although many are ported versions from other platforms. Significant partners such as Skype, Kindle, WhatsApp, SAP, and Angry Birds are developing apps for BB10. Facebook, Twitter, and LinkedIn are already available, but notable omissions like Instagram, Hulu, and Google apps remain. BlackBerry's goal is to convince more developers to support the platform. 4. Improved Typing Experience: A trademark of BlackBerry devices has been their physical keyboard, but the company is moving focus toward touchscreen typing with the Z10. The virtual keyboard learns individual typing habits, provides accurate corrections, offers support for multiple languages, and displays predictive suggestions users can insert with a swipe. 5. Positive Momentum and Global Launch: After years of stagnation, BlackBerry's rebranding and new product releases have generated renewed interest among consumers and media. The company enlisted Alicia Keys as Global Creative Director to boost its profile. The global rollout begins in the UK, followed by Canada, the United Arab Emirates, and other key markets. BlackBerry is emphasizing international reach, particularly in regions where it already enjoys popularity. While BlackBerry faces challenges, particularly against Apple and Google, its latest moves reflect a determined effort to regain relevance in the rapidly evolving smartphone market.

Nå er det opp til forbrukerne: Vil BlackBerrys nye Z10 (full berøringsskjerm) og Q10 (med det velkjente tastaturet) overbevise brukere om å velge dem fremfor iPhone eller Android-enheter? Anmeldelser av BlackBerry 10 har så langt vært blandede, men det er oppmuntrende tegn. Her er fem grunner til at BlackBerry 10 kan tiltrekke både lojale følgere og nye brukere: 1. Forbedrede produktivitetsfunksjoner: Store selskaper og offentlige etater har lenge vært BlackBerrys mest trofaste kunder. Med en arbeidsplass-trend mot bruk av personlige enheter, har BlackBerry 10 prioritert produktivitet og hastighet. Den nye 'Balance'-funksjonen deler telefonen i separate arbeids- og personlige profiler (tilgjengelig for de som er koblet til BlackBerry Enterprise Service 10), noe som hjelper IT-avdelingene med å beskytte sensitiv informasjon, samtidig som brukerne får full tilgang til personlige apper og data. Dette løsner behovet for å bære to telefoner for jobb og privatliv. 2. Samlede varslinger: På lanseringseventet for BlackBerry 10 demonstrerte ledelsen 'BlackBerry Hub', en funksjon som samler alle varsler på ett lett tilgjengelig sted. Voksende app-bibliotek: BlackBerry har fylt sin app-butikk med over 70 000 apper for lanseringen av BB10, selv om mange er porter fra andre plattformer. Betydelige partnere som Skype, Kindle, WhatsApp, SAP og Angry Birds utvikler apper for BB10. Forbedret tasteopplevelse: Et kjennetegn ved BlackBerry har vært det fysiske tastaturet, men selskapet satser nå på berøringstasting med Z10. Det virtuelle tastaturet lærer brukerens skrivevaner, gir nøyaktig korreksjon, støtter flere språk, og viser forslag til ord du kan sveipe inn i meldingen. 5. Positivt moment og global lansering: Etter flere år med stagnasjon har BlackBerrys omprofilering og nye produkter skapt fornyet interesse blant forbrukere og medier. Selskapet har engasjert Alicia Keys som Global Creative Director for å styrke profileringen. article_content: After years of advocacy from gay rights groups, President Barack Obama plans to sign an executive order prohibiting federal contractors from discriminating against employees based on sexual orientation or gender identity, the White House announced on Monday. While Obama does not have the authority to extend these protections to all Americans, the executive order would affect approximately 14 million workers in states or companies where such workplace discrimination is not already banned. This estimate comes from the Williams Institute at UCLA Law School, which researches law and policy regarding sexual orientation and gender identity. Obama had previously resisted signing such an order, preferring that Congress enact a broader anti-discrimination law covering most employers. Although the Senate passed such legislation last year, it has stalled in the Republican-controlled House, with little sign lawmakers will act in this election year. Announcing his intention on the South Lawn of the White House, President Obama stated his plan to sign the bill. 'We've been waiting for quite a few months now for the House to take action and, unfortunately, there are no particularly strong indications that Congress is prepared to act on this,' said White House spokesman Josh Earnest. Advocates for gay rights praised the White House's move as a major victory. 'By issuing an executive order prohibiting federal contractors from discriminating against LGBT people, the president will not only create fairer workplaces across the country, but also demonstrate to Congress that adopting federal employment protections for LGBT people is good policy and good for business,' said Chad Griffin, president of the Human Rights Campaign. It was not specified when Obama will sign the order or why the administration chose to preview the decision. The announcement came just before Obama was scheduled to attend the Democratic National Committee's annual gay and lesbian fundraiser in New York. Though the president has substantial support among the LGBT community, some advocates have been frustrated by his previous hesitation to take executive action. Their frustration grew earlier this year when Obama announced other executive orders, such as raising the minimum wage for federal contractors and expanding overtime eligibility for contractors, but delayed an anti-discrimination measure. Obama's executive order could also energize progressive voters ahead of the midterm elections, as Republicans seek to regain control of the Senate. Democrats have highlighted the announcement to draw distinctions with Republicans, who have mostly remained silent. Utah Senator Orrin Hatch, however, has asked that the order include religious exemptions similar to those found in last year's Senate legislation, which exempts churches, houses of worship, and religiously-affiliated organizations. The specific language of Obama's upcoming order has not been released, but advocates anticipate it will align with prior executive orders, such as those signed by President Lyndon B. Johnson prohibiting discrimination by federal contractors on race, religion, and national origin. It is unclear if the order will include religious exemptions. Public support for gay rights has grown in recent years. Courts across the country have also increasingly ruled in favor of same-sex marriage, with more than a dozen federal and state judges striking down state-level bans in the past seven months. No courts have upheld such bans in that period. Despite this progress, LGBT rights advocates note that significant inequality remains in workplace discrimination. The Human Rights Campaign reports that it is legal to fire or refuse employment to someone based on sexual orientation in 29 states, and that 32 states lack explicit laws against discrimination based on gender identity.
translated_content: Etter mange år med innsats fra homofiles rettighetsgrupper planlegger president Barack Obama å signere en presidentordre som forbyr føderale entreprenører å diskriminere ansatte basert på seksuell orientering eller kjønnsidentitet, kunngjorde Det hvite hus mandag. Selv om Obama ikke har myndighet til å utvide disse beskyttelsene til alle amerikanere, vil presidentordren påvirke rundt 14 millioner arbeidstakere i stater eller selskaper der slik diskriminering ikke allerede er forbudt. Dette estimatet kommer fra Williams Institute ved UCLA Law School, som forsker på jus og politikk knyttet til seksuell orientering og kjønnsidentitet. Obama hadde tidligere vært tilbakeholden med å signere en slik ordre, og foretrakk at Kongressen skulle vedta en bredere antidiskrimineringslov som omfatter de fleste arbeidsgivere. Selv om Senatet vedtok en slik lov i fjor, har den stoppet opp i Representantenes hus, som styres av republikanerne, og det er liten grunn til å tro at lovgiverne vil handle i valgåret. Da han kunngjorde sin intensjon på plenen foran Det hvite hus, uttalte president Obama at han har planer om å signere loven. 'Vi har ventet ganske mange måneder nå på at Representantenes hus skal handle, og dessverre er det ingen særlig sterke indikasjoner på at Kongressen er forberedt på å gjøre noe med dette,' sa talsmann for Det hvite hus, Josh Earnest. Forkjempere for homofiles rettigheter berømmet Det hvite hus’ tiltak som en stor seier. 'Ved å utstede en presidentordre som forbyr føderale entreprenører å diskriminere mot LHBT-personer vil presidenten ikke bare skape mer rettferdige arbeidsplasser over hele landet, men også vise Kongressen at slike beskyttelser er god politikk og bra for næringslivet,' sa Chad Griffin, president for Human Rights Campaign. Det ble ikke oppgitt når Obama vil signere ordren, eller hvorfor administrasjonen valgte å varsle om avgjørelsen på forhånd. Kunngjøringen kom rett før Obama skulle delta på Det demokratiske partiets årlige pengeinnsamling for homofile og lesbiske i New York. Selv om presidenten har betydelig støtte i LHBT-miljøet, har noen forkjempere vært frustrerte over hans tidligere nøling med å ta i bruk presidentordrer. Frustrasjonen økte tidligere i år da Obama annonserte andre presidentordrer, som å heve minstelønnen for føderale entreprenører og utvide retten til overtidsbetaling, men unnlot å handle i antidiskrimineringssaken. Obamas presidentordre kan også gi et løft til progressive velgere foran årets mellomvalg, ettersom republikanerne forsøker å gjenerobre flertallet i Senatet. Demokratene har fremhevet kunngjøringen for å vise forskjellen til republikanerne, som i stor grad har vært tause. Utah-senator Orrin Hatch har derimot bedt om at ordren inkluderer religiøse unntak, slik det er gjort i forrige sesjons lovforslag fra Senatet, som gir unntak for kirker, trossamfunn og religiøse organisasjoner. Den nøyaktige ordlyden til Obamas kommende ordre er ikke offentliggjort, men det er ventet at den vil ligne tidligere presidentordrer, som den Lyndon B. Johnson innførte som forbød diskriminering blant føderale entreprenører på grunnlag av rase, religion og nasjonal opprinnelse. Det er uklart om ordren vil inneholde religiøse unntak. Støtten i befolkningen for homofiles rettigheter har vokst de siste årene. Domstoler i hele landet har også i økende grad gått inn for likekjønnet ekteskap, og over et dusin føderale og lokale dommere har i løpet av de siste sju månedene opphevet delstatsforbud. Ingen domstoler har vedtatt motsatte avgjørelser i perioden. Til tross for denne fremgangen, påpeker LHBT-rettighetsforkjempere at det fortsatt er betydelige ulikheter når det gjelder diskriminering i arbeidslivet. Human Rights Campaign rapporterer at det er lov å avskjedige eller nekte noen jobb på grunnlag av seksuell orientering i 29 delstater, og at 32 delstater mangler eksplisitte lover mot diskriminering basert på kjønnsidentitet.

article_content: Palestinian children walked through debris in the courtyard of a school run by the United Nations Relief and Works Agency after Israeli airstrikes hit Gaza City on Monday. This comes in the wake of last weekend’s surprise attacks by Hamas militants on Israel, which have stunned both the country and the world. Hundreds of Israelis have died, thousands are wounded, and dozens—including children—remain hostages of Hamas. Israel's continuing airstrikes have led to hundreds of Palestinian deaths, with at least 90 children killed, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Humanitarian groups have warned about an escalating crisis if Israel enforces a halt on food, water, and electricity to Gaza, where almost half of the residents are under 18. The ongoing situation is distressing for all—particularly children, who may struggle to comprehend why kids like themselves are suffering or feel worried about their own safety. Experts interviewed by NPR stress that all children deserve a conversation about the conflict, whether or not they have direct connections to the region. Many children already learn about such events from peers, news, or adults. While it might seem better to let children approach the topic themselves, Waheeda Saif, a program coordinator at Riverside Trauma Center in Massachusetts, advises parents to start the conversation using open-ended questions such as, “Have you heard about what’s going on in the world?” or “Do you know anything about Israel and Palestine?” For older children with online access, experts recommend encouraging skepticism about what they see on social media and offering guidance in evaluating news sources. For younger children, it’s important to assure them of their safety, as they may think the conflict is much closer than it is; parents can use maps to illustrate the distance. Dimitry Anselme, executive program director at Facing History & Ourselves, advises listening more than lecturing—allowing children to ask their own questions. He also suggests that, before initiating discussions, parents should reflect on their own understanding of the conflict and be prepared to explain its basics. Maha Bali, a professor at the American University in Cairo, points out that even young children are capable of understanding complex historical events. She recalls explaining to her daughter the history of the region, from the creation of Israel after World War II to the ongoing blockade of Gaza. Experts further caution against grouping all individuals together when discussing the conflict. Anselme emphasizes discussing the actions of specific individuals or groups, rather than generalizing about all people from certain backgrounds. Sivan Zakai, a Jewish education professor, encourages parents to be honest about uncertainties when addressing children’s profound questions about violence or world events. Children often seek comfort and guidance in a scary world, and it’s important to foster hope. Zakai notes that children are especially adept at envisioning peace and coexistence, even when confronted by violence.
