Hundrevis av israelere har mistet livet, tusenvis er såret, og mange – inkludert barn – holdes fortsatt som gisler av Hamas. Israels pågående luftangrep har ført til hundrevis av palestinske dødsfall, med minst 90 barn drept ifølge det palestinske helsedepartementet. Humanitære organisasjoner har advart om en voksende krise dersom Israel kutter tilgangen på mat, vann og strøm til Gaza, hvor nesten halvparten av innbyggerne er under 18 år. Situasjonen er vanskelig for alle, spesielt barn som kan ha problemer med å forstå hvorfor andre barn lider, eller bekymre seg for sin egen sikkerhet. Eksperter intervjuet av NPR understreker at alle barn bør få en samtale om konflikten, selv uten direkte tilknytning til området. Mange barn får allerede informasjon gjennom venner, nyhetsoppslag eller voksne hjemme. Selv om det kan føles naturlig å vente på at barna skal ta opp temaet selv, anbefaler Waheeda Saif, programkoordinator ved Riverside Trauma Center i Massachusetts, at foreldre tar initiativ med åpne spørsmål som: «Har du hørt om det som skjer i verden?» eller «Vet du hva som skjer i Israel og Palestina?» For eldre barn med internett-tilgang anbefales det å oppmuntre til kritisk tenking om det de ser i sosiale medier, og å veilede dem i å vurdere kilder. For yngre barn er det viktig å berolige dem – noen kan tro at konflikten foregår mye nærmere enn tilfelle, så vis dem gjerne på et kart hvor langt unna det skjer. Dimitry Anselme, programdirektør i Facing History & Ourselves, foreslår å lytte mer enn å gi svar – la barna spørre det de lurer på. Foreldre bør først reflektere over hva de selv vet om konflikten, slik at de kan forklare det grunnleggende for barna. Hun forklarte datteren sin om områdets historie – fra Israels opprettelse etter andre verdenskrig til dagens blokade av Gaza. Sivan Zakai, professor i jødisk utdanning, oppmuntrer foreldre til å være åpne om hva de ikke vet når barna spør om verdens vold. Barn søker ofte trygghet og håp, og ifølge Zakai har barn et spesielt talent for å forestille seg en mer fredelig fremtid, selv midt i kriser.

article_content: Prospective jurors in the trial of Mark W. Strong, the business partner of alleged 'Zumba prostitute' Alexis Wright, are being openly questioned about their views on sex and prostitution in a Maine courtroom. The jury questionnaire includes personal inquiries such as, 'Do you have a personal or religious aversion to pornography?', 'Do you believe prostitution should be legal?', and 'Would viewing explicit material affect your ability to listen to evidence?' Last Friday, Judge Nancy Mills dismissed 46 out of 59 charges against Strong, who is accused of promoting prostitution and enabling Alexis Wright to run an illicit business out of her Zumba studio in Kennebunk, Maine. Despite the dismissals, Strong still faces 13 misdemeanor counts of promoting prostitution. Both Strong and Wright have also been charged with invasion of privacy for allegedly videotaping Wright's encounters with clients. However, Justice Mills ruled that the men involved had no expectation of privacy when allegedly participating in criminal acts at the studio. Prosecutors have appealed this decision to the Maine Supreme Judicial Court, hoping to have the charges reinstated. Strong has admitted to an affair with Wright and to financially supporting her studio, but denies knowledge of or involvement in her alleged prostitution activities. His defense team argues that authorities are wasting time and resources by pursuing relatively minor charges. After a legal challenge from the Portland Press-Herald, the court decided that jury selection must be open to the public. This means prospective jurors must now discuss their views on sex and personal privacy in open court. The Boston Herald notes that publicity around the case may lead to even more personal questions about sexual preferences and attitudes during jury selection. The case has drawn significant public and media attention and has raised concerns about the potential for juror discomfort and the difficulty of finding impartial jurors in the local community.

Forrige fredag frafalt dommer Nancy Mills 46 av 59 tiltalepunkter mot Strong, som er anklaget for å ha fremmet prostitusjon og hjulpet Alexis Wright med å drive en ulovlig virksomhet fra hennes Zumba-studio i Kennebunk, Maine. Til tross for dette står Strong fortsatt tiltalt for 13 forseelser knyttet til å ha fremmet prostitusjon. Både Strong og Wright er også siktet for brudd på privatlivets fred for angivelig å ha filmet Wrights møter med klienter. article_content: Mexican authorities have rescued 94 migrants who were packed into the back of a truck in extremely poor conditions. The group included people from Nepal, Guatemala, El Salvador, Bangladesh, and Honduras. Seven of those rescued were minors. Many migrants showed symptoms of asphyxiation and had serious injuries to their hands and feet. They were found in the southern Mexican state of Chiapas early Tuesday morning, after X-ray equipment at a checkpoint detected them. The truck driver was handed over to prosecutors on suspicion of human trafficking. Meanwhile, the migrants are receiving medical, psychological, and legal assistance, according to Chiapas state prosecutors. Photographs released by local police show the migrants sitting on the ground, receiving care from officials. It remains unclear where the migrants will go next. Authorities said the group included 45 Guatemalans, 23 Salvadorans, 10 Nepalese, 9 Bangladeshis, and 7 Hondurans. According to the National Migration Institute, the migrants paid different amounts for transport: Central Americans between $4,000 and $5,000, and Asians between $6,000 and $8,000. This incident follows recent rescues: last week, authorities freed 81 migrants held in Reynosa, and in June, 165 kidnapped migrants were rescued as they tried to cross into the United States. Officials and experts say the journey through Mexico is dangerous from the start, with migrants often facing violence, especially as organized crime groups expand their reach. Eduardo Aragon from CNN en Español contributed to this report.

Mange av migrantene viste tegn på kvelning og hadde alvorlige skader på hender og føtter. De ble funnet i den sørlige delstaten Chiapas tidlig tirsdag morgen, etter at røntgenutstyr ved en kontrollpost avdekket dem. Eduardo Aragon fra CNN en Español bidro til denne rapporten.

article_content: It has long been understood that human settlement contributes to conditions making Pacific Islands more susceptible to wildfires, as seen in the devastating Aug. 8 event that destroyed Maui’s Lahaina community. However, a new study by SMU fire scientist Christopher Roos, published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, shows that climate plays an undervalued role. Roos, an environmental archaeologist and professor of anthropology at SMU, led a research team to the Sigatoka River valley in southwestern Fiji in 2013. There, they collected charcoal and stable carbon isotopes from deep soil cores to examine historical patterns of fire activity. By analyzing distinctive carbon signatures left by different plants, the team gathered insights into ancient plant communities. They discovered evidence of fires and fire-created grassy areas that existed thousands of years before human settlement, which correlated with drought periods likely triggered by El Niño weather patterns. El Niño can alter global precipitation, creating conditions favorable to wildfires. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) issued an El Niño advisory in June, signaling the most recent onset of this climate event, which continues to influence global weather. Lightning strikes also naturally cause wildfires by igniting plant materials that serve as fuel. The impact of human settlement, including farming (particularly land clearing and burning) and resulting deforestation on remote Pacific islands, is well documented. Roos’s study confirms these effects but emphasizes that climate impacts must also be recognized. "I realized these fires aren't exclusively driven by human activity," said Roos. "When I examined earlier, pre-human increases in fire activity, they coincided with El Niño events. The combination of climate and human activity drives island deforestation and increases wildfire activity. Human activity may make the landscape more sensitive to climate shifts, or climate may make the landscape more vulnerable to human actions." Roos notes that past research focused primarily on the harm caused by human activity, often overlooking climate’s role. He advocates for a broader approach that considers both factors, especially as severe wildfires become more frequent. He also points out that Pacific Islands serve as natural laboratories for studying the grass-fire cycle, which is expanding with the spread of invasive grasses. Traditional farming practices—using controlled clearing and burning—have been effective for centuries and may offer guidance on preparing for and managing future wildfires. Roos stresses the need to adapt to the new environment shaped by both climate and human influence. "Droughts triggered by El Niño events appear to have intensified the grass-fire cycle and contributed to past deforestation," Roos explained. "Looking forward, climate models suggest the Pacific Islands could face El Niño-like conditions more often due to ongoing climate change. We need to consider our actions and whether they make places more or less vulnerable to future wildfire events."
translated_content: Det har lenge vært kjent at menneskelig bosetting bidrar til forhold som gjør stillehavsøyene mer sårbare for skogbranner, som sett under den ødeleggende hendelsen 8. august som rammet Lahaina-samfunnet på Maui. En ny studie av SMU-brannforskeren Christopher Roos, publisert i Nature Ecology & Evolution, viser imidlertid at klima spiller en undervurdert rolle. Roos, miljøarkeolog og professor i antropologi ved SMU, ledet et forskningsteam til Sigatoka-elvedalen sørvest på Fiji i 2013. Der samlet de trekull og stabile karbonisotoper fra dype jordkjerner for å undersøke historiske mønstre av brannaktivitet. Ved å analysere karakteristiske karbonsignaturer fra ulike planter fikk teamet innsikt i eldgamle plantesamfunn. De fant bevis på branner og brannskapte gressområder som eksisterte tusenvis av år før menneskelig bosetting, og som korrelerte med tørkeperioder sannsynligvis utløst av El Niño-værmønstre. El Niño kan endre globale nedbørsmønstre og skape forhold som er gunstige for skogbranner. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) utstedte et El Niño-varsel i juni, som markerte starten på denne klimabegivenheten som fortsatt påvirker været over hele verden. Lynnedslag forårsaker også naturlig skogbranner ved å antenne plantemateriale som fungerer som brensel. Effektene av menneskelig bosetting, inkludert jordbruk (særlig rydding og brenning av land) og resulterende avskoging på fjerne stillehavsøyer, er godt dokumentert. Roos sin studie bekrefter disse effektene, men understreker at også klimaets påvirkning må anerkjennes. "Jeg innså at disse brannene ikke kun skyldes menneskelig aktivitet," sa Roos. "Da jeg undersøkte tidligere økninger i brannaktivitet før mennesker var tilstede, sammenfalt de med El Niño-hendelser. Kombinasjonen av klima og menneskelig aktivitet fører til avskoging og økt brannaktivitet på øyene. Menneskelig aktivitet kan gjøre landskapet mer følsomt for klimavariasjoner, eller klimaet kan gjøre landskapet mer sårbart for menneskelig påvirkning." Roos påpeker at tidligere forskning primært fokuserte på skadene fra menneskelig aktivitet, og ofte overså klimaets rolle. Han argumenterer for en bredere tilnærming som tar hensyn til begge faktorer, spesielt ettersom alvorlige skogbranner blir mer vanlige. Han fremhever også at stillehavsøyene fungerer som naturlige laboratorier for å studere gress-brannsyklusen, som sprer seg med innførte gresstyper. Tradisjonelle jordbruksmetoder—med kontrollert rydding og brenning—har vært effektive i århundrer og kan gi veiledning om hvordan man kan forberede og håndtere fremtidige branner. Roos understreker behovet for å tilpasse seg det nye miljøet som både klima og mennesker har skapt. "Tørker utløst av El Niño-hendelser ser ut til å ha forsterket gress-brannsyklusen og bidratt til tidligere avskoging," forklarte Roos. Vi må tenke over våre handlinger og om de gjør steder mer eller mindre sårbare for fremtidige skogbranner."

article_content: Weather intelligence plays a crucial role in many industries, far beyond the commonly cited sectors like utilities and agriculture. Industries such as horse racing, distilleries, beach volleyball, and solar farms increasingly rely on precise weather data to optimize operations and enhance safety. In horse racing, both microclimate forecasts and weather consulting are used to keep horses and riders safe. Track conditions—affected by temperature, moisture, and precipitation—directly impact race results and animal wellbeing. For example, muddy dirt tracks can slow horses, while hard, dry tracks raise the risk of injury. Turf tracks face their own challenges, from slippery surfaces after rain to hazards from dried, uneven ground. Distilleries are another sector that depends on weather insights. With a history of lightning-related warehouse fires—like the 2019 incident at a Jim Beam facility—distilleries now implement risk mitigation strategies aided by weather forecasts to protect valuable goods and ensure employee safety. Beach volleyball, a rapidly growing sport, demonstrates how outdoor sports leverage weather data for safety and game strategy. Factors such as wind, heat, and moisture influence both gameplay and crowd comfort, with teams adapting tactics based on real-time weather conditions. Solar farms, whose productivity is tied to sun exposure, also use weather intelligence to shield infrastructure from severe weather events. Hailstorms, for instance, caused over $300 million in damage to Texas solar fields in 2022. Companies are now employing forecasts to move solar modules into protective 'stow mode' ahead of storms. These varied examples underscore how industries are advancing their use of weather intelligence, not only to enhance safety but also to optimize performance, foster resilience, and improve profitability.

article_content: Saido Berahino, the 21-year-old striker for West Bromwich Albion, has been backed by manager Alan Irvine to rediscover his goal-scoring form after going five Premier League matches without finding the net. Berahino last scored in October, converting a late penalty against Crystal Palace. Irvine has dismissed suggestions that Berahino’s England call-up or his recent drink-driving arrest have affected his performance, and revealed the striker is watching footage of Sergio Aguero and Diego Costa to improve. Despite a strong start to the season with seven Premier League goals, Berahino has not scored in recent games but continues to be preferred over record signing Brown Ideye. Irvine said, 'We’ve asked a lot of a young player. He had a very good start and there’s been a lot of attention on him. His goal against Manchester United proved vital for his England squad selection. There’s been a lot of focus, but he’s handled it well overall. While it's not surprising to see a dip in form, I believe he’ll bounce back. He’s a natural finisher, and the goals will come again.' Irvine also addressed the possibility of signing an experienced striker in the January transfer window, stating that bringing in experienced players could help Berahino's development. He added, 'If Saido plays more with Victor Anichebe, he'll learn a lot. We discuss the movement of players like Aguero and Costa, and Saido studies their play himself. Like any young striker, he will have spells when goals are hard to come by.'

article_content:
Despite advanced forensic technology and well-trained personnel, even developed countries can find solving murders challenging. In Afghanistan, these difficulties are intensified by widespread corruption, continued conflict, and a shortage of forensic resources—the country operates only one forensic unit, the Criminal Techniques Department (CTD) based in Kabul. Writer Roc Morin, accompanied by military escorts, visited the CTD to meet its dedicated staff, who handle around 300 new cases each month, striving to bring law and order to a turbulent society.

Inside the CTD, firearms awaiting ballistics testing are stored in racks, ranging from old-fashioned rifles to modern assault weapons. The unit’s director, Colonel Ayaz, acknowledges that corruption allows some suspects to elude justice. He recounts a case in which a woman was killed by a government official; although his fingerprint was found on the gun, the suspect remained free due to his political connections.

Another notable case involved a headless body found in the street with a threatening note attached: 'Anyone who attends this man's funeral can expect the same fate.' Thanks to Document Exploitation expert Noorullah Sangarkhil and an expensive handwriting analysis machine, the CTD matched the note to an existing suspect, resulting in an arrest.

Despite limited resources—the CTD reportedly has only one bullet-matching machine, a 30-year-old donation from Germany—the unit continues to make progress. Most Afghans are unaware that fingerprints can identify individuals, and even the CTD director learned about DNA technology only a few years ago. Nevertheless, its 102 technicians strive to advance forensic investigations, including identifying counterfeit currency.

Trust in the CTD from international partners is high: NATO bodyguards are reported to remove their armor upon entering the facility, indicating confidence in the staff’s integrity. US Senior Advisor David Jacobson praised the technicians’ professionalism, noting that their dedication to duty stands out within Afghanistan’s challenging environment.

This report originally appeared in Vice. More information about Roc Morin can be found at www.rocmorin.com.

Inne på CTD lagres våpen som venter på ballistisk testing, fra gammeldagse rifler til moderne automatvåpen. Avdelingens leder, oberst Ayaz, innrømmer at korrupsjon gjør at noen mistenkte slipper unna straff. Han forteller om en sak hvor en kvinne ble drept av en regjeringsansatt; selv om hans fingeravtrykk ble funnet på våpenet, gikk han fri på grunn av sine forbindelser.

Et annet bemerkelsesverdig tilfelle var et hodeløst lik funnet i gaten med en truende lapp: «Alle som deltar i denne mannens begravelse kan vente seg samme skjebne.» Takket være dokumentekspert Noorullah Sangarkhil og en kostbar håndskriftanalysator, klarte CTD å koble lappen til en pågrepet mistenkt.

Til tross for begrensede ressurser – CTD har visstnok kun én kuleanalysator, en 30 år gammel gave fra Tyskland – fortsetter enheten å bidra til fremgang. De fleste afghanere vet ikke at fingeravtrykk kan identifisere personer, og selv avdelingslederen lærte først om DNA-teknologi for noen år siden. Likevel jobber 102 teknikere dedikert med å forbedre kriminaletterforskningen, inkludert identifisering av falske pengesedler.

Internasjonale partnere har høy tillit til CTD: Det går rykter om at NATO-livvakter tar av seg beskyttelsesutstyret når de går inn i bygningen, noe som tyder på tillit til personalets integritet. article_content: A significant technical failure at Vodafone disrupted phone lines for numerous essential services, including police non-emergency numbers, NHS medical hotlines, RAC breakdown recovery, and organizations like Barclays and First Great Western. The issues began around 9am, leaving callers unable to reach key services. Those needing roadside help couldn’t contact RAC, and people seeking train information or trying to reach NHS 111 and 24 faced similar trouble. Vodafone’s engineers prioritized fixing the phone routing problem, which originated at an exchange in Birmingham. Working through the morning, engineers restored most services by 1pm. A Vodafone representative explained that a fault in their call routing equipment temporarily interfered with fixed line services to several organizations. The company apologized for the inconvenience and announced that it would carry out a thorough investigation while closely monitoring the situation. Impacted groups like Anglian Water and several police forces took to social media to keep the public informed and suggest alternatives. Police in areas including Humberside, the Met, and North Yorkshire told people to use online reporting, visit police stations, or use special alternative numbers for non-urgent situations. Emergency calls to 999 were unaffected and should still be used only for emergencies. Organizations such as RAC Breakdown encouraged customers to email their requests and had patrols actively searching for those in need. Barclays bank, among others, alerted customers to the disruptions via Twitter. NHS officials said the technical problem also impacted some people contacting the 111 medical advice line, but services returned to normal by early afternoon. In light of the disruption, various police forces published interim phone numbers for non-emergency needs, while reminding the public that regular emergency numbers remain active. NHS England confirmed by midday that its helplines were back in operation after resolving the technical fault. The recently introduced 111 freephone medical helpline in Scotland was also affected; it had been launched to simplify access to medical advice after hours.

article_content: In the UPSC Essentials series ‘Society & Social Justice’, subject experts provide a comprehensive overview of major social issues for UPSC CSE aspirants, from both static and dynamic perspectives. Previous topics have included ‘Population’, ‘Urbanisation’, and ‘Literacy’. For October, the spotlight turns to ‘Poverty and Associated Issues’. Part 1 covered fundamental concepts, causes, measurements, and how poverty relates to inequality and hunger. In Part 2, Manas Srivastava interviews Pranay Aggarwal about the experiences of urban and rural poor, the pain of poverty, and offers notable quotes and insights at the end.  About the Expert: Pranay Aggarwal is an experienced educator and mentor with over a decade of guiding UPSC Civil Services aspirants, particularly in Social Issues and Sociology. He is India's representative on the Research Committee on Education for UNESCO’s International Sociological Association and serves on the Indian Sociological Society’s committee on social movements. He also convenes the Indian Civil Services Association, a think tank for senior bureaucrats.  Relevance: Poverty is one of the most important topics in UPSC social issues papers and is closely linked to themes such as population, unemployment, and hunger. Both static and current aspects of poverty are tested, making this topic relevant for GS I (Society), GS II, GS III, the Prelims, personality tests, and essay writing.  Pranay Aggarwal defines ‘urban’ and ‘rural’ poor as two separate groups experiencing poverty in their respective contexts. According to NITI Aayog, 5.2% of the urban population were multidimensionally poor in 2019-21, while 19.2% of the rural population fell in this category—almost four times higher. Notably, poverty in rural areas dropped from 32.5% in 2015-16 to 19.2% in 2019-21. In comparison, urban poverty declined from 8.6% to 5.2% during the same period.  Urban Poor: Those in cities and towns facing poverty deal with high living costs, scarce affordable housing, poor sanitation, and limited healthcare. Jobs are often informal, such as street vending, construction, or domestic work. Despite better job prospects, the high cost of urban living creates challenges. Urban microfinance programs offer small loans, training, and financial services to support income generation and small businesses.  Rural Poor: Living in rural areas often means contending with underdeveloped infrastructure and heavy dependence on agriculture. Challenges include landlessness, low farm productivity, poor access to education and healthcare, and social obstacles such as caste, gender, and ethnicity. Formal financial services are often inaccessible, hindering savings and investment. Rural microfinance, like the SHG-Bank Linkage Program, provides credit, savings, and insurance, enabling financial inclusion and security while helping develop small businesses and farm activities.  The Pains of Poverty: Poverty brings numerous challenges: 1. Food insecurity—malnutrition and health issues, especially among children. 2. Inadequate healthcare—lack of access leads to untreated illnesses. 3. Limited educational opportunity—reducing prospects for advancement. 4. Unstable housing—risking overcrowding and homelessness. 5. Financial stress—causing mental health concerns. 6. Social exclusion—discrimination and isolation from societal participation. 7. Unemployment and underemployment—few jobs, low wages, and instability. 8. Shorter life expectancy—due to poor living and healthcare conditions. 9. Lack of clean water and sanitation—leading to diseases and poor hygiene. 10. Intergenerational poverty—the cycle persists across generations. 11. Financial vulnerability—scarce savings for emergencies. 12. Limited social mobility—few chances to improve life circumstances. These issues are deeply connected and require broad, long-term solutions.  Impact of Covid-19: The pandemic worsened poverty and inequality. Economic disruptions led to massive job losses, especially affecting informal workers. Many social safety nets were insufficient. Healthcare disparities widened, with costs burdening poorer families. School closures and a shift to digital education hurt low-income students without technology. The digital divide made remote work, education, and e-services difficult to access. Many households incurred debt, and the informal workforce suffered losses. The crisis led to reverse migration, straining resources in rural areas. Small and medium businesses struggled, further impacting employment.  IMF and NCAER reports note a temporary increase in poverty and inequality due to the pandemic, though expanded food subsidies helped mitigate some effects. Some researchers, like Aravind Panagariya, present alternative perspectives on these trends. Addressing these inequalities requires strong safety nets, better healthcare and education, and special support for the most vulnerable.  Quotes and Introductions on Poverty: 1. “Poverty is the worst form of violence.” – Mahatma Gandhi 2. “It is not enough to be compassionate. You must act.” – 14th Dalai Lama 3. “Poverty is like punishment for a crime you didn’t commit.” – Eli Khamarov 4. “Overcoming poverty is not an act of charity; it is an act of justice.” – Nelson Mandela 5. Behind every statistic lies an individual with dreams and struggles. 6. A poverty-free India is the shared aim of a just and inclusive society. 7. Inequality challenges the fabric of society, not just its economy. 8. The fight against poverty happens wherever people strive for dignity. 9. Poverty diminishes opportunities and dignity, bringing despair. 10. The ongoing fight against poverty shows our collective resolve.  The piece invites reflection on India’s anti-poverty programs, case studies, and ways forward.
translated_content: I UPSC Essentials-serien ‘Samfunn & sosial rettferdighet’ gir fagpersoner en grundig gjennomgang av sentrale samfunnstemaer for UPSC CSE-kandidater, både fra et statisk og et aktuelt perspektiv. Tidligere temaer har vært ‘Befolkning’, ‘Urbanisering’ og ‘Lesekyndighet’. I oktober er fokuset ‘Fattigdom og tilknyttede utfordringer’. Del 1 tok for seg grunnbegrepene, årsaker og koblingen mellom fattigdom, ulikhet og sult. I del 2 intervjuer Manas Srivastava Pranay Aggarwal om erfaringer fra by- og bygdefattigdom, fattigdommens byrder, og inspirerende sitater deles på slutten.  Om eksperten: Pranay Aggarwal er en erfaren veileder med over ti års erfaring med UPSC-studenter, særlig innen samfunnsfag og sosiologi. Han representerer India i UNESCOs internasjonale sosiologiforening sitt utdanningsutvalg og er med i Indias sosiologiforenings komité for sosiale bevegelser. Han leder også Indian Civil Services Association, et tankesmie for høytstående embetsmenn.  Relevans: Fattigdom er et sentralt emne i UPSCs samfunnsfag, nært knyttet til befolkning, arbeidsledighet og sult. Både faste og aktuelle aspekter av fattigdom blir testet. Temaet gjelder for GS I (Samfunn), GS II, GS III, Prelims, personlighetstest og essayoppgaver.  Pranay Aggarwal forklarer at by- og bygdefattige er to ulike grupper som opplever fattigdom i ulike omgivelser. Ifølge NITI Aayog var 5,2 % av bybefolkningen flerfasettert fattige i 2019-21, mens 19,2 % av bygdebefolkningen falt i denne kategorien – nesten fire ganger så mange. Fattigdommen på landsbygda falt fra 32,5 % i 2015-16 til 19,2 % i 2019-21. I byene gikk den fra 8,6 % til 5,2 % i samme periode.  Byfattige: I byene møter man utfordringer som høye levekostnader, lite rimelig bolig, dårlig sanitær og begrenset helsetilgang. Mange jobber uformelt, for eksempel med gatesalg, bygg eller rengjøring. Selv med flere jobbmuligheter gjør de høye kostnadene det vanskelig. Urban mikrofinans gir små lån, opplæring og økonomiske tjenester som støtter inntektsgivende aktiviteter og småbedrifter.  Bygdefattige: På landsbygda er mangelfull infrastruktur og tung avhengighet av jordbruket vanlig. Utfordringer inkluderer jordløshet, lav produktivitet, lite tilgang til helse og utdanning samt sosiale barrierer som kaste, kjønn og etnisitet. Manglende tilgang til banktjenester hindrer sparing og investering. Mikrofinans, som SHG-Bank Linkage Program, gir kreditt, sparing, og forsikring og støtter små virksomheter og jordbruksaktiviteter.  Fattigdommens byrder: Fattigdom gir en rekke utfordringer: 1. Matmangel – underernæring og helseproblemer, særlig for barn. 2. Mangelfull helsehjelp – sykdommer forblir ofte ubehandlet. 3. Lite tilgang til utdanning – gir færre muligheter for utvikling. 4. Ustabile boforhold – fare for trangboddhet og hjemløshet. 5. Økonomisk stress – gir mentale utfordringer. 6. Sosial ekskludering – diskriminering og isolering. 7. Arbeidsledighet og dårlige jobber – lav lønn og usikkerhet. 8. Lavere forventet levealder – på grunn av dårlige forhold. 9. Manglende tilgang til rent vann og sanitær – gir sykdom. 10. Fattigdom som går i arv – vanskelig å bryte sirkelen. 11. Økonomisk sårbarhet – lite sparing ved kriser. 12. Begrenset sosial mobilitet – få muligheter for fremskritt. Utfordringene er gjensidig forsterkende og krever langsiktige løsninger.  Covid-19s innvirkning: Pandemien gjorde fattigdom og ulikhet verre. Mange mistet jobbene, særlig i uformelle sektorer. Sosiale sikkerhetsnett var ofte svake. Helseforskjeller ble større, og utgifter tynget lavinntektsfamilier. Skole-stengingen og digital undervisning rammet de uten teknologi ekstra hardt. Den digitale kløften gjorde fjernarbeid og utdanning utilgjengelig for mange. Flere havnet i gjeld, og den uformelle arbeidsstyrken led store tap. Omvendt migrasjon førte til press på landsbygdas ressurser. Mange små og mellomstore bedrifter slet med store tap.  IMF og NCAER rapporterer om økt fattigdom og ulikhet under pandemien, selv om utvidede mattilskudd hjalp. Andre, som Aravind Panagariya, har andre syn på utviklingen. Løsningen krever sterkere sikkerhetsnett, bedre helse og utdanning og støtte til de mest utsatte.  Sitater og innledninger om fattigdom: 1. «Fattigdom er den verste formen for vold.» – Mahatma Gandhi 2. «Det er ikke nok å være medfølende. Du må handle.» – Dalai Lama 3. «Fattigdom er som straff for en forbrytelse du ikke har begått.» – Eli Khamarov 4. «Å bekjempe fattigdom er ikke veldedighet, men rettferdighet.» – Nelson Mandela 5. Bak hver statistikk skjuler det seg et menneske med drømmer og utfordringer. 6. Et fattigdomsfritt India er en felles ambisjon for et rettferdig, inkluderende samfunn. 7. Ulikhet er en utfordring for samfunnsstrukturen, ikke bare økonomien. 8. Kampen mot fattigdom foregår der mennesker kjemper for sin verdighet. 9. Fattigdom fratar folk muligheter og skaper fortvilelse. 10. Den vedvarende kampen mot fattigdom viser vår kollektive styrke.  Artikkelen oppfordrer til refleksjon rundt Indias tiltak mot fattigdom, eksempler og veien videre.

article_content: Britain’s elite 16 Air Assault Brigade, the Army’s main rapid-response airborne force, is set to be reduced by about a third as the government implements cuts across the Armed Forces. In an ongoing effort to scale down the Army from 102,000 to 82,000 regular soldiers, the 16 Air Assault Brigade will lose half of its regular infantry battalions, along with air power, artillery, and armoured vehicles. The brigade, which includes the Parachute Regiment battalions, has been deployed in recent missions to Sierra Leone, Macedonia, Iraq, and Afghanistan. Sources within the brigade estimate it will lose nearly 3,000 personnel from its current 8,000 by the end of December. These changes, outlined after the 2013 Army 2020 review, are intended to create a smaller, more integrated, and adaptable Army, saving approximately £10 billion from the Ministry of Defence budget. However, concerns have been raised about the Army’s readiness for future conflicts due to reduced numbers. New details about the cuts and their timeline have appeared in the Parachute Regiment’s journal and internal briefings. By the end of the year, both 1st and 2nd Battalions of the Royal Irish Regiment will leave the brigade for lower-readiness forces, as reported by the Sunday Telegraph. The Fifth Battalion of the Royal Regiment of Scotland has been largely disbanded, apart from a public duties company. Armoured reconnaissance vehicles from the Household Cavalry Regiment are being reassigned, and the brigade, based in Colchester, Essex, will also lose artillery, engineers, and helicopters. Former Parachute Regiment officer and Labour MP Dan Jarvis criticized the cuts, calling them ‘baffling,’ especially as focus shifts towards contingency operations requiring rapid Army responses. Jarvis expressed concern that the changes could undermine the brigade’s deployability and combat effectiveness. The Army 2020 programme plans to offset the loss of 20,000 regulars by expanding the newly renamed Army Reserve, formerly the Territorial Army. The cuts are part of broader reductions, which also include 5,500 fewer Royal Navy sailors and 8,000 fewer Royal Air Force personnel. The most recent round of redundancies, announced in January, is expected to be the last. Some affected battalions are being absorbed into other regiments. Plans to disband the 2nd Battalion Royal Regiment of Fusiliers previously sparked protests. This summer, the regiment's 1st and 2nd Battalions will merge to form the new First Fusiliers, with the second battalion removed from the Army’s order of battle on August 31. Earlier this month, MPs warned of possible further military cuts following a £1.2 million underspend at the Ministry of Defence. General Sir Nick Houghton, Chief of the Defence Staff, has cautioned that the Army risks being left with state-of-the-art equipment but insufficient personnel to use it, describing this as the risk of a ‘hollow force.’ Vice Admiral Simon Lister has also criticized the state of the Royal Navy, calling attention to declining readiness, maintenance pressures, and reliance on civilian contractors, which he argues reduces competence and confidence among service members. Colonel Tim Collins, formerly of the 1st Battalion Royal Irish Regiment, commented that the Army’s reduced size resembles more a defense force than a traditional army. A Ministry of Defence spokesperson stated that the 2010 Strategic Defence and Security Review required difficult decisions to equip the Army for the future. Changes to 16 Air Assault Brigade were announced in 2013 and are part of making the Army more flexible and better able to respond to new threats. According to the spokesperson, the brigade will remain the Army’s premier high readiness formation, drawing support from other divisions and support units as needed, and that operational effectiveness will be maintained.
translated_content: Storbritannias elitesoldater i 16 Air Assault Brigade, Hærens viktigste hurtigreaksjonsstyrke, skal kuttes med omtrent en tredjedel når regjeringen gjennomfører nedskjæringer i Forsvaret. Som en del av planen om å redusere hæren fra 102 000 til 82 000 yrkessoldater, vil 16 Air Assault Brigade miste halvparten av sine regulære infanteribataljoner, samt miste luftstøtte, artilleri og pansrede kjøretøy. Brigaden, som inkluderer fallskjermregimentets bataljoner, har vært utplassert i nyere operasjoner i Sierra Leone, Makedonia, Irak og Afghanistan. Kilder innad i brigaden anslår at opptil 3 000 av dagens 8 000 soldater vil forsvinne innen utgangen av desember. Endringene, som ble skissert etter Army 2020-gjennomgangen i 2013, skal gjøre hæren mindre, mer integrert og tilpasningsdyktig, og spare ca. 10 milliarder pund for Forsvarsdepartementet. Likevel er det bekymring for hærens beredskap i fremtidige konflikter som følge av redusert bemanning. Nye detaljer om kuttene og tidsplanen har kommet frem i fallskjermregimentets tidsskrift og interne notater. Innen utgangen av året vil både første og andre bataljon av Royal Irish Regiment forlate brigaden og bli en del av styrker med lavere beredskap, ifølge Sunday Telegraph. Femte bataljon av Royal Regiment of Scotland er stort sett avviklet, bortsett fra en seremoniell vaktstyrke. Pansrede rekognoseringskjøretøy fra Household Cavalry Regiment omdisponeres, og brigaden – som er basert i Colchester, Essex – mister også artilleri, ingeniører og helikoptre. Tidligere fallskjermregimentsoffiser og nåværende Labour-parlamentsmedlem Dan Jarvis har kritisert kuttene og kalt dem «forvirrende», særlig fordi fokuset nå dreier mot beredskapsoperasjoner hvor hurtig styrkeoppbygning er viktig. Jarvis frykter endringene vil svekke brigadens kapasitet og effektivitet. Army 2020-programmet skal veie opp for tapet av 20 000 yrkessoldater ved å utvide det nydøpte Army Reserve, tidligere Territorialsoldater. Kuttene skjer samtidig som Royal Navy mister 5 500 sjømenn og RAF reduseres med 8 000 ansatte. Den siste nedskjæringsrunden ble kunngjort i januar, og flere bataljoner har allerede blitt sammenslått med andre regimenter. Planene om å avvikle 2. bataljon i Royal Regiment of Fusiliers førte tidligere til protester. I sommer slås regimentets 1. og 2. bataljon sammen til First Fusiliers, og 2. bataljon fjernes fra hærens styrkeoversikt 31. august. Tidligere denne måneden advarte parlamentsmedlemmer om flere potensielle kutt, etter at Forsvarsdepartementet hadde et underforbruk på 1,2 millioner pund. General Sir Nick Houghton, sjef for Forsvarsstaben, har advart mot risikoen for at hæren ender opp med topp moderne utstyr, men for lite personell, det han kaller en «hollow force». Visadm. Simon Lister har også kritisert Royal Navy for synkende beredskap og stor avhengighet av sivile vedlikeholdsentreprenører, noe han mener svekker kompetanse og selvtillit blant mannskapet. Oberst Tim Collins, tidligere fra 1. bataljon i Royal Irish Regiment, mener hærens reduserte størrelse minner mer om en forsvarsstyrke enn en tradisjonell armé. En talsperson fra Forsvarsdepartementet sier at 2010-gjennomgangen (Strategic Defence and Security Review) krevde vanskelige prioriteringer for å utruste hæren for fremtiden. Endringene i 16 Air Assault Brigade ble annonsert i 2013 og skal gjøre hæren mer fleksibel og bedre rustet til å håndtere nye trusler. Talspersonen understreker at brigaden forblir hærens fremste høyberedskapsstyrke, med støtte fra andre divisjoner ved behov, og at operativ effekt opprettholdes.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has appointed B Y Vijayendra, son of former Karnataka Chief Minister B S Yediyurappa, as its new Karnataka state president. Yediyurappa stated that he did not lobby for his son's appointment and emphasized that the decision was made by the party’s central leadership, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and BJP national president J P Nadda. Vijayendra, previously the BJP’s state vice-president and a first-time MLA from Shikaripura in Shivamogga, replaces Nalin Kumar Kateel, a three-time Lok Sabha MP from Dakshina Kannada who had served beyond his initial term.

Yediyurappa expressed confidence that Vijayendra would unify the party and lead them to win over 25 of Karnataka’s 28 Lok Sabha seats in the upcoming general elections. He dismissed claims of internal dissent and responded to Congress's allegations of 'dynasty politics' by affirming his son’s merit and the enthusiasm of party workers. Congress criticized the appointment, suggesting it reflects dynastic tendencies within BJP. Despite these allegations, Yediyurappa insisted the party remains united and focused on its electoral goals.

article_content: Moscow is remarkable for its enormous scale, with broad 10-lane avenues and striking architecture that reflect Russia’s position as the world’s largest country. Matthew Chance, a senior international correspondent at CNN who has lived in Moscow for six years, describes the city as vibrant and impressive. Russia covers almost twice the area of the United States, and Moscow’s population exceeds 10 million, according to the CIA World Factbook. The city is regularly counted among the most expensive globally, filled with luxury cars and high-end living, according to Chance. For sweeping city views, Sparrow Hills is a top choice—offering park walks and opportunities to buy Soviet-era souvenirs from vendors nearby. Contrary to the stereotype of being unattractive, Chance points out that Moscow contains many picturesque areas, shining especially after dark. For celebratory dinners, Galleria on Petrovka Ulitsa presents a showy option, while Tiflis on Ostozhenka Ulitsa offers a more intimate Georgian dining experience. Patriarch's Ponds, Chance’s favorite neighborhood, combines the charm of a village with distinctive shops, inviting cafes, the popular Klava bar, and the excellent Volkonsky bakery. The pond is ideal for summer strolls and turns into an ice rink in winter. To unwind, the Sanduny Banya provides an authentic Russian sauna experience—birch branch treatments, icy plunges, and then snacks like shrimp with hot tea and honey. If you’re limited on time, he suggests visiting Red Square and the iconic St. Basil’s Cathedral, then enjoying a session at a traditional banya. Tourists often stand out by not speaking Russian, but leading attractions—Lenin’s Tomb, ballet at the Bolshoi Theatre, and the Kremlin Armory—are still must-sees. A memorable meal for Chance was at Darbar, an Indian restaurant atop Hotel Sputnik, appreciated for its Indian staff and scenic city views. For an excursion out of town, he recommends either a friend’s countryside dacha or a quick trip on the bullet train to St. Petersburg. Visitors should try local specialties like vodka, caviar, blinis, and sour cream, while a fur hat with ear flaps makes a favored souvenir. Have you explored Moscow? Russland dekker nesten dobbelt så stort areal som USA, og Moskvas befolkning er over 10 millioner, ifølge CIA World Factbook. Byen regnes jevnlig blant de dyreste i verden, full av luksusbiler og eksklusiv livsstil, ifølge Chance. For panoramautsikt over byen er Spurvehøydene et toppvalg – med parkvandringer og muligheten til å kjøpe suvenirer fra sovjettiden fra boder i nærheten. I motsetning til stereotypien om at byen er lite pen, påpeker Chance at Moskva har mange vakre områder, spesielt når den lyser opp om kvelden. Glenda Gilson and her brother Damien, directors of the Dublin-based Gilson Motor Company Limited, are facing potential jail time for allegedly failing to submit complete financial statements during their company's liquidation. The liquidation, initiated by the Irish Revenue Commissioners, follows more than €140,000 in unpaid taxes amassed by the luxury car sales business. Both siblings have now provided their statements of affairs; however, the liquidator, Gary Lennon of Lennon Corporate Recovery, found both submissions incomplete.

Glenda, a non-executive director reportedly involved to assist Damien, had already submitted her statement while Damien did so only after a delay attributed to a misunderstanding. The High Court warned them that inadequate disclosure could result in imprisonment. Presiding judge, Ms Justice Mary Finlay Geoghegan, directed the liquidator to specify in writing any deficiencies in the statements by the next day, giving the Gilsons an opportunity to rectify issues ahead of the continued hearing on July 11, 2011.

Glenda Gilson og broren Damien, direktører i Dublin-baserte Gilson Motor Company Limited, risikerer fengsel for angivelig å ha unnlatt å levere fullstendige regnskaper under avviklingen av eget luksusbilselskap. Avviklingen ble satt i gang av det irske skattevesenet etter at selskapet hadde pådratt seg over 140 000 euro i ubetalte skatter. Begge søsknene har nå levert sine formueoppgaver, men bobestyrer Gary Lennon fra Lennon Corporate Recovery mener begge dokumentene er utilstrekkelige.

Glenda, som var ikke-utøvende direktør og ifølge rapporter kun involvert for å hjelpe Damien, hadde allerede levert sin erklæring, mens Damien først gjorde det etter en forsinkelse han forklarte som en misforståelse. Høyesterett advarte om at utilstrekkelige opplysninger kunne føre til fengselsstraff. Dommer Mary Finlay Geoghegan påla bobestyreren å spesifisere skriftlig eventuelle mangler innen dagen etter, slik at Gilson-søsknene får mulighet til å rette opp før neste rettsmøte 11. juli 2011.

article_content: Before I had children, I always saw myself as a mother to boys rather than girls. In truth, I intensely hoped for sons, even finding myself praying for them, despite not being religious. I envisioned that a home with boys would provide a refreshing contrast to my female-dominated family and social circle, which hasn’t seen a son born in three generations. Yet, fate had other plans: my three daughters now outnumber their 'beloved brother' three to one.  Of course, I am grateful to have four healthy, relatively stable children, but I still—illogically, perhaps—believe I would have thrived as a mother of sons. When expecting my first child, my list of boys’ names was extensive, while potential girls’ names were scarce. With my second pregnancy, I was determined to end my family’s streak of daughters, but once again, I welcomed another wonderful girl: Gracie.  My third pregnancy was different. Though my doctor wrongly advised an abortion for medical reasons, my partner and I chose not to follow that advice. During the frequent scans, my gynaecologist’s growing excitement hinted at news about the baby’s gender. Eventually, my much-hoped-for son arrived—he who once called himself 'Miss Argentina' and wore nighties, but who now tells me every night that he loves me more than a thousand kisses. We later completed our family with a fourth child, another girl.  Out of all my children, my relationship with my son is the most easygoing, which no doubt fuels my ongoing daydreams of being a 'mother to boys.' Boys, it seems to me, are less complicated to parent—at least before the teenage years.  Recently, I got to test my 'boys only' fantasy during a holiday in Cornwall. While others were busy with beach activities, I spent the day with my nearly eight-year-old son and his ten-year-old friend. The day was wonderfully simple: when I asked if they wanted to play crazy golf, they answered in unison, 'Yes.' With my daughters (aged ten and nearly twelve), the same question would have prompted a litany of clarifying questions and negotiations.  After a swift, fun golf game (where I unceremoniously came last), the boys wanted to bounce on trampolines, then run on the beach. Later, we had ice cream, and they were unfazed when accidentally served tubs instead of cones—whereas my daughters would likely have made a grand complaint about the 'tub-not-cone debacle.' Back at home, the boys played Mousetrap noisily while I prepared chicken nuggets for dinner, no negotiations required.  It was all strangely relaxing. With my daughters, days are always fun, but rarely straightforward. Perhaps my experience was just a fluke and unrelated to 'boydom,' but talking with other mums, I came to the admittedly unscientific conclusion that boys are a less complex parenting puzzle, at least until the turbulent teenage years.  However, I realise that raising sons may come with a different set of responsibilities. As a woman, perhaps it’s easier to guide girls into becoming good women; but how does one raise a good man?  Lorraine Candy is the editor of ELLE.
translated_content: Før jeg fikk barn, så jeg alltid for meg at jeg skulle være guttemamma og ikke jentemamma. Ærlig talt, jeg håpet intenst på gutter, og tok meg selv i å be om det – selv om jeg ikke er religiøs. Jeg så for meg at et hjem fullt av gutter ville vært en forfriskende forandring fra min kvinnedominerte familie og vennekrets, som ikke har hatt en sønn på tre generasjoner. Men skjebnen ville det annerledes: Mine tre døtre er nå i klart flertall over deres 'elskede bror', tre mot én.  Selvfølgelig er jeg takknemlig for å ha fire friske, forholdsvis stabile barn, men jeg tror fortsatt – ulogisk nok – at jeg ville trivdes bedre som guttemamma. Da jeg ventet mitt første barn, hadde jeg en lang liste med guttenavn, men knapt noen jentenavn. Under det andre svangerskapet håpet jeg igjen å bryte familiens jenterekke, men enda en fantastisk jente kom til verden: Gracie.  Tredje svangerskap var annerledes. Selv om legen min feilaktig rådet meg til abort av medisinske grunner, valgte partneren min og jeg å ikke følge rådet. Under de mange ultralydene, vokste gynekologens spenning rundt barnets kjønn for hver gang. Til slutt kom min etterlengtede gutt – han som før kalte seg 'Miss Argentina' og gikk i nattkjole, men som nå hver kveld sier at han elsker meg mer enn tusen kyss. Etter hvert kom vårt siste barn, også en jente.  Av alle barna mine har jeg det enklest med sønnen min, noe som utvilsomt gir næring til dagdrømmen om å være 'bare guttemamma'. For meg virker det som gutter er mindre kompliserte å oppdra – i hvert fall før tenåringsårene.  Nylig fikk jeg testet denne 'guttefantasien' på ferie i Cornwall. Mens de andre holdt på med strandaktiviteter, tilbrakte jeg dagen med min snart åtte år gamle sønn og hans tiårige kamerat. Alt var så enkelt: Da jeg spurte om de ville spille minigolf, svarte de i kor: 'Ja.' Hadde jeg derimot spurt døtrene mine (ti og snart tolv år), ville det endt med et vell av spørsmål og forhandlinger.  Etter en kjapp og morsom golfkamp (jeg tapte glatt), ville guttene hoppe på trampoline og deretter løpe på stranda. Litt senere spiste vi is, og de brydde seg ikke da de fikk beger i stedet for kjeks – der mine døtre sannsynligvis ville ha gjort et stort nummer ut av 'beger-not-kjeks-skandalen'. Da vi kom hjem, spilte guttene Mousetrap høylytt mens jeg laget kyllingnuggets uten å måtte forhandle om middagen.  Det var merkelig avslappende. Med døtrene mine er dagene alltid morsomme, men langt fra like ukompliserte. Kanskje var dette bare flaks, og ikke egentlig noe typisk for gutter. Men etter å ha diskutert med andre mødre kom jeg til den, riktignok uvitenskapelige, konklusjonen at gutter er et mindre komplisert foreldrepuslespill – i hvert fall frem til tenåringsalderen.  Samtidig innser jeg at det å oppdra gutter kommer med sitt eget ansvar. Som kvinne kan det kanskje føles lettere å veilede jenter til å bli gode kvinner – men hvordan oppdrar man egentlig en god mann?  Lorraine Candy er redaktør i ELLE.

article_content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday accused the Nitish Kumar-led Bihar government of deliberately inflating the numbers of Muslims and Yadavs in the state’s caste survey, describing this as part of 'appeasement politics' and claiming it neglected backward classes as a whole. Speaking at a rally in Patahi, Muzaffarpur, Shah argued that such policies could create significant problems in areas bordering Nepal and Bangladesh. He noted that the BJP was in coalition with Nitish Kumar when the survey was commissioned but claimed the party was unaware of Kumar’s alleged plans under pressure from RJD president Lalu Prasad. Shah asserted that the populations of Yadavs and Muslims were exaggerated in the survey and that injustice was done to OBCs and EBCs. He also criticized the Congress party for being historically hostile towards OBCs and highlighted BJP-led initiatives: increasing OBC representation in the Union Cabinet and granting constitutional status to the National Commission for OBCs—achievements he said previous governments, including one supported by Lalu Prasad, failed to deliver. He criticized the INDIA opposition alliance (including JD(U) and RJD) for opposing BJP policies such as abrogating Article 370 and building the Ram temple at Ayodhya, and questioned Nitish Kumar’s political stability. Shah repeated his appeal to voters to support the BJP and NDA in upcoming elections, referencing the NDA's decisive victory of 39 out of 40 seats in Bihar in 2019. Shah’s speech, marking his first visit to Bihar since the caste survey results were released on October 2, also included greetings for the upcoming Chhath festival. The survey showed OBCs and EBCs constitute more than 60% of Bihar’s population, with upper castes around 10%; the BJP has questioned its accuracy. Other news: The Indian government approved Sweden’s Saab for the first 100% foreign direct investment in the defense sector to establish a rocket facility. State Bank of India reported an 8% increase in quarterly net profit, attributed to steady loan demand and reduced loan loss provisions. Byju’s released financials indicating revenue growth to ₹3,569 crore in FY22 but continued substantial losses.

Under et folkemøte i Patahi, Muzaffarpur, hevdet Shah at slike tiltak kan skape betydelige problemer i områder som grenser til Nepal og Bangladesh. Han påpekte at BJP var i koalisjon med Nitish Kumar da undersøkelsen ble igangsatt, men hevdet partiet ikke var klar over Kumars påståtte planer under press fra RJD-leder Lalu Prasad. Shah påsto at antall Yadav-er og muslimer var overdrevet i undersøkelsen, og at det ble gjort urett mot OBC-er og EBC-er. Han kritiserte også Kongresspartiet for å være historisk fiendtlig mot OBC-er og fremhevet BJP-initiativer, blant annet økt OBC-representasjon i Unionens regjering og konstitusjonell status til nasjonalkommisjonen for OBC-er—prestasjoner han hevdet tidligere regjeringer, inkludert en støttet av Lalu Prasad, ikke klarte å få til. Han rettet også kritikk mot INDIA-opposisjonsalliansen (inkludert JD(U) og RJD) for å motsette seg BJP-politikk som opphevelsen av artikkel 370 og byggingen av Ram-tempelet i Ayodhya, og stilte spørsmål ved Nitish Kumars politiske stabilitet. Shah appellerte nok en gang til velgerne om å støtte BJP og NDA i de kommende valgene, med henvisning til NDA sin klare seier med 39 av 40 seter i Bihar i 2019. Shahs tale, som markerte hans første besøk til Bihar etter offentliggjøringen av kasteundersøkelsens resultater 2. oktober, inneholdt også hilsener til den kommende Chhath-festivalen. Undersøkelsen viste at OBC-er og EBC-er utgjør mer enn 60 % av Bihars befolkning, med de øvre kastene på rundt 10 %; BJP har satt spørsmålstegn ved undersøkelsens nøyaktighet. Andre nyheter: Indiske myndigheter har godkjent svenske Saab som det første selskapet til å motta 100 % utenlandske direkteinvesteringer i forsvarssektoren for å etablere en rakettfabrikk. State Bank of India meldte om en økning på 8 % i kvartalsresultatet, tilskrevet stabil etterspørsel etter lån og lavere tap på lån. Byju’s offentliggjorde resultater som viste inntektsvekst til ₹3,569 crore i 2022, men rapporterer fortsatt betydelige tap.

article_content: As televised theater, few moments could top it. As political forecasting, it was puzzling. And as partisan combat, it was strikingly bold. Karl Rove’s insistence that Barack Obama had not won Ohio—even after Fox News, his own network, called the state for Obama—reflected something greater. For a tense period, it captured how some in the media and political spheres refuse to accept reality, a pattern seen repeatedly this year. This wasn’t simply a mistaken call by a pundit. All commentators, myself included, have made bad predictions—if those were criminal, the media would be in jail. But Rove, a seasoned operative known as George W. Bush’s 'architect,' helped Bush win two presidential elections and is deeply familiar with polling. At Fox, Rove holds a unique position, moving from the Bush White House to prominent conservative commentator. He also has a Wall Street Journal column and co-founded American Crossroads and Crossroads Grassroots Political Strategies, political groups that spent approximately $175 million in this campaign, mainly supporting Mitt Romney or opposing Obama. Rove was not just a commentator; he was a political player, appearing on Fox frequently and sharing his analysis across numerous programs. Fox is not alone in hiring active partisans—CNN does as well—and news outlets have long blurred the boundary between journalism and politics. While such connections are typically disclosed, I personally would not employ anyone directly involved in political fundraising or party leadership as commentators, since it undermines impartiality. How can viewers expect anything but partisan perspectives? Rove surely values his reputation for political insight, making his break with Fox’s decision desk on election night all the more remarkable. It was dramatic: Fox News, CNN, and MSNBC were all calling Ohio—and the presidency—for Obama, but Rove disputed the call, warning about making projections with so few votes separating the candidates and significant ballots left to count. In the end, Rove was mistaken; Obama won Ohio and a second term. What stood out was Rove’s on-air challenge to his network’s own experts, appearing to reject the public’s verdict. This has been a persistent theme throughout the year. When Romney trailed in the polls, some conservatives accused the media of skewing surveys, leading to sites like unskewedpolls.com. After unemployment dropped in September, critics—including Jack Welch—baselessly accused the Obama administration of manipulating data. When The New York Times’ Nate Silver gave Obama a 90% chance of victory, some conservatives labeled him biased, but Silver was correct in every state. Donald Trump, meanwhile, spent the campaign promoting false birther claims, and on election night, tweeted that Obama’s win was a 'disgusting injustice.' He questioned both Obama’s birthplace and the legitimacy of his victory. I don’t suggest that Rove subscribes to conspiracy theories, though he did claim after the election that Obama won by 'suppressing the vote,' contradicting evidence that the president sought to increase turnout. For a fleeting moment on election night, viewers witnessed overt partisanship masquerading as journalism.
translated_content: Som TV-teater var det få øyeblikk som kunne overgå dette. Som politisk spådom var det forvirrende. Og som partisk kamp var det oppsiktsvekkende dristig. Karl Roves påstand om at Barack Obama ikke hadde vunnet Ohio – selv etter at Fox News, hans egen kanal, erklærte delstaten for Obama – reflekterte noe større. I en spent periode fanget det hvordan noen i medie- og politiske kretser nekter å akseptere virkeligheten, et mønster som har blitt sett gjentatte ganger dette året. Dette var ikke bare en feilansettelse fra en kommentator. Alle kommentatorer, inkludert meg selv, har gjort dårlige spådommer – hvis det var kriminelt, ville mediene vært fulle av folk. Men Rove, en erfaren strateg kjent som George W. Bushs 'arkitekt,' hjalp Bush med å vinne to presidentvalg og kjenner valgmålinger inngående. Hos Fox har Rove en unik posisjon, etter å ha gått fra Bush-administrasjonen til en fremtredende konservativ kommentator. Han har også en spalte i Wall Street Journal og var med på å stifte American Crossroads og Crossroads Grassroots Political Strategies, politiske grupper som brukte omtrent 175 millioner dollar i denne valgkampen, hovedsakelig for å støtte Mitt Romney eller motarbeide Obama. Rove var mer enn bare en kommentator; han var en politisk aktør og dukket ofte opp på Fox for å dele sin analyse i flere programmer. Fox er ikke alene om å engasjere aktive partimedlemmer – CNN gjør det også – og nyhetsorganisasjoner har lenge visket ut skillet mellom journalistikk og politikk. Selv om slike forbindelser vanligvis oppgis, ville jeg personlig ikke hyre noen som direkte samler inn penger til politiske partier eller har en ledende posisjon, som kommentator, fordi det går ut over upartiskheten. Hvordan kan seere forvente noe annet enn partiske synspunkter? Rove verdsetter utvilsomt sitt rykte for politisk innsikt, noe som gjør bruddet hans med Fox’ valgdesk på valgnatten desto mer oppsiktsvekkende. Det var dramatisk: Fox News, CNN og MSNBC erklærte alle Ohio – og dermed presidentvalget – for Obama, men Rove motsatte seg avgjørelsen og advarte mot å konkludere med så få stemmer som skilte kandidatene, og med betydelige antall igjen å telle. Til slutt tok Rove feil; Obama vant Ohio og en ny periode. Det som skilte seg ut var Roves utfordring av egne eksperter på direktesendt TV, hvor han fremsto som om han avviste folkets dom. Dette har vært et vedvarende tema gjennom hele året. Da Romney lå dårlig an på meningsmålingene, hevdet enkelte konservative at media manipulerte målingene, noe som førte til sider som unskewedpolls.com. Da arbeidsledigheten falt i september, anklaget kritikere – inkludert Jack Welch – grunnløst Obama-administrasjonen for å manipulere tallene. Da New York Times’ Nate Silver ga Obama 90 % sjanse for seier, stemplet noen konservative ham som partisk, men Silver traff blink i alle delstater. Donald Trump brukte valgkampen på å fremme falske påstander om Obamas fødested, og på valgnatten tvitret han at Obamas seier var 'avskyelig urettferdighet.' Han stilte spørsmål ved både Obamas fødested og valgseierens legitimitet. Jeg påstår ikke at Rove tror på slike konspirasjonsteorier, men han hevdet etter valget at Obama vant ved å 'undertrykke stemmegivningen,' i motsetning til bevis på at presidenten ville øke valgdeltakelsen. For et øyeblikk på valgnatten fikk seerne et klart glimt av partiskhet forkledd som journalistikk.

article_content: Designer sunglasses remain popular, with celebrities such as Kate Moss, Megan Fox, Cara Delevigne, and Ryan Gosling frequently seen wearing high-end shades. However, when it comes to eye protection, these expensive glasses may not provide additional benefits. An investigation by U.S. eye specialists has revealed that discount sunglasses are just as effective at blocking harmful UV rays as designer brands. Dr. Dennis Fong, a professor at the School of Optometry at the University of California, Berkeley, tested sunglasses costing less than £10 and found they blocked 100% of the sun’s harmful UVA and UVB rays, matching the performance of much pricier pairs. Opticians recommend wearing sunglasses when in strong sunlight for more than 10 minutes, particularly from mid-April through September, when UV ray levels are up to three times higher than in winter. UVB rays can be ten times stronger during summertime midday hours. Long-term UV exposure can cause significant damage to the eyes, including cataracts, macular degeneration, growths on the cornea, and other conditions. Cataracts, which cloud the lens of the eye, are a leading cause of blindness worldwide. UVB rays, the spectrum responsible for sunburn, are especially harmful to the eyes. Other potential consequences of sun exposure include pinguecula (yellowish deposits in the eye), photokeratitis (snow blindness), and skin cancer of the eyelid. As part of the investigation, Dr. Fong purchased designer sunglasses from brands such as Coach, Ray-Ban, and Smith, each costing over $100. He also acquired 11 inexpensive pairs, each around $10, from various retailers. Using a spectrophotometer to measure UV transmission, all sunglasses tested successfully blocked 100% of UVA and UVB rays, regardless of price. While both cheap and expensive sunglasses provided equal UV protection, higher-end models typically offer more durable frames, improved design, and greater comfort. The results of the investigation were featured on Good Morning America by ABC News. Eye experts additionally caution that lens color does not determine UV protection, as the protective coating is applied to the lens itself. An eye specialist at UC Berkeley confirmed that discount sunglasses, costing less than £10, are just as effective at blocking harmful UV rays as designer pairs costing over £50.

UVB-stråler kan være ti ganger sterkere midt på sommerdager. Langvarig UV-eksponering kan forårsake betydelige øyeskader, deriblant grå stær, makuladegenerasjon, utvekster på hornhinnen og andre tilstander. Grå stær, som gir uklarheter i øyets linse, er en ledende årsak til blindhet på verdensbasis. UVB-stråler, som også forårsaker solbrenthet, er spesielt skadelige for øynene. Andre mulige konsekvenser av soleksponering inkluderer pinguecula (gulaktige avleiringer i øyet), fotokeratitt (snøblindhet) og hudkreft på øyelokket. Resultatene fra undersøkelsen ble presentert på Good Morning America av ABC News. Øyeeksperter understreker også at fargen på glassene ikke avgjør UV-beskyttelsen, fordi det er et beskyttende belegg som påføres linsen. En øyespesialist ved UC Berkeley bekreftet at billige solbriller til under 100 kroner er like effektive som designerbriller til over 500 kroner når det gjelder å blokkere skadelige UV-stråler.

article_content: Being an early morning TV presenter and getting up for work at 3am often means getting dressed while still half asleep. If you have a sleeping husband and three small children you don't want to wake, it might even be in the dark. So it's little surprise that BBC Breakfast star Susanna Reid, 42, accidentally wore her Marks & Spencer dress backwards. On BBC Breakfast yesterday morning, Susanna appeared alongside her co-host Bill Turnbull, 57, who had managed to wear his suit correctly. The usually well-dressed mother-of-three didn't notice her fashion mistake until after her three-hour live appearance. When someone pointed out that her £39.50 shift dress was on backwards, Reid turned to Twitter to admit her error, asking viewers: 'Just realised my dress is on back-to-front. Why didn't you tell me?' Bill Turnbull jokingly replied: 'And spoil the fun?' Susanna Reid shared her wardrobe mishap online, while Bill Turnbull's humorous response added to the lighthearted moment. Reid isn't the first celebrity to experience a confusing outfit. Actresses such as Angelina Jolie, Sigourney Weaver, and Amanda Seyfried have appeared at red carpet events wearing gowns backwards. Their agents or stylists sometimes claim these choices were intentional. Even the Duchess of Cambridge has had minor wardrobe accidents, like wearing a coat belt upside down. In January, American actress Sigourney Weaver attended the SAG Awards in a Lanvin dress worn the wrong way round. According to Styleite, the front of the dress typically features a deep v-neck and a faux waist-belt detail, while the back is a plain high neckline. On the red carpet, Weaver seemed to wear the top part backwards. It was suggested designer Alber Elbaz may have customized the look for her, but the dress didn’t impress all fashion critics. In 2011, Demi Lovato wore a Roland Mouret dress backwards to the Latin Grammy Awards, giving the appearance of a plunging neckline intended for the back. Similarly, Amanda Seyfried attended the 2010 premiere of 'Mother And Child' in a BodyAmr dress worn back-to-front, and in 2009, Angelina Jolie purposely reversed her Max Azria dress at the SAG Awards to show off her tattooed back. Even the Duchess of Cambridge once wore the slimline belt of a £980 MaxMara wool coat upside down during a visit to Cambridge in November. Observant fans noticed the loops of the bow were underneath the belt. Such moments show that even the most stylish celebrities can fall victim to minor fashion mix-ups.

På den røde løperen så det ut som om Weaver hadde overdelen bak-frem. Det ble foreslått at designeren Alber Elbaz kanskje hadde tilpasset kjolen, men den imponerte ikke alle motekritikere. Til og med hertuginnen av Cambridge har hatt på seg beltet til en £980 MaxMara-ullkåpe opp-ned under et besøk i Cambridge i november. Oppmerksomme fans la merke til at løkkene til sløyfen var under beltet. Slike øyeblikk viser at selv de mest stilige kjendisene kan bli utsatt for små mote-tabber.

article_content: Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, surpassed Wall Street expectations in the third quarter, but is now experiencing advertising volatility in the fourth quarter due in part to the Israel-Hamas conflict. Snap also reported strong third-quarter results and similar concerns about uncertainty for the current quarter. Both companies emphasized the challenge of providing accurate financial guidance amid these global events. Meta’s CFO, Susan Li, said on a conference call with CEO Mark Zuckerberg that while there continues to be robust demand for advertising in key sectors, volatility has increased at the start of the fourth quarter. As a result, Meta broadened its guidance range for the quarter to reflect this heightened uncertainty. Li noted that although Meta does not have significant direct revenue exposure in Israel or the Middle East, ad spending has softened at the beginning of Q4, corresponding with the start of the conflict. She added, 'Our thoughts are with everyone impacted by the horrific violence in the Middle East. Our services can be vital for information, connection, and expression during difficult times. We are closely monitoring the situation and doing everything we can to ensure safety and security on our platforms.' For the September quarter, Meta’s revenue jumped 23% to $34.15 billion, driven by a rebound in digital advertising. Profit more than doubled to $11.6 billion, aided by aggressive cost-cutting measures, including significant layoffs. Meta’s workforce stood at 66,185 employees, down 24% from a year earlier. User growth remained strong: 3.14 billion people used at least one of Meta’s 'family of apps' daily—an increase of 7% year-over-year—with 2.09 billion daily active users (DAUs) on Facebook alone in September 2023, up 5% from last year. These results came just one day after Meta was sued by 41 states, which allege that Instagram and Facebook employ algorithms and strategies designed to keep minors engaged, potentially harming the mental health of children and teenagers. The lawsuit claims that Meta declined to implement key safeguards, such as more robust age verification options. The topic was not discussed during the earnings call.
translated_content: Meta, morselskapet til Facebook og Instagram, overgikk Wall Streets forventninger i tredje kvartal, men opplever nå større volatilitet i annonsemarkedet for fjerde kvartal, delvis på grunn av Israel-Hamas-konflikten. Snap rapporterte også sterke resultater for tredje kvartal og uttrykte lignende bekymringer for usikkerhet i inneværende kvartal. Begge selskapene understreket utfordringen med å gi presise økonomiske prognoser midt i disse globale hendelsene. Metas finansdirektør, Susan Li, sa på en telefonkonferanse sammen med CEO Mark Zuckerberg at det fortsatt er solid etterspørsel etter annonsering i viktige sektorer, men at volatiliteten har økt i starten av fjerde kvartal. Derfor utvidet Meta sitt forventningsintervall for kvartalet for å ta høyde for denne usikkerheten. Li påpekte at selv om Meta ikke har betydelig direkte inntekter fra Israel eller Midtøsten, har annonseforbruket gått ned i starten av fjerde kvartal, noe som sammenfaller med starten på konflikten. Hun la til: 'Våre tanker går til alle som er berørt av det forferdelige volden i Midtøsten. Våre tjenester kan være viktige for informasjon, kontakt og ytring i vanskelige tider. Vi følger situasjonen nøye og gjør alt vi kan for å holde folk trygge og våre tjenester sikre.' I septemberkvartalet steg Metas inntekter med 23 % til 34,15 milliarder dollar, drevet av en oppgang i digital annonsering. Overskuddet mer enn doblet seg til 11,6 milliarder dollar, hjulpet av betydelige kostnadskutt, inkludert store oppsigelser. Metas arbeidsstyrke var på 66 185 ansatte, en nedgang på 24 % fra året før. Brukerveksten holdt seg sterk: 3,14 milliarder mennesker brukte minst én av Metas 'familie av apper' daglig—en økning på 7 % fra året før—og med 2,09 milliarder daglige aktive brukere (DAU) på Facebook i september 2023, opp 5 % fra i fjor. Disse resultatene kom bare én dag etter at Meta ble saksøkt av 41 delstater, som hevder at Instagram og Facebook bruker algoritmer og strategier som holder mindreårige engasjert og potensielt skader barns og tenåringers psykiske helse. article_content: The insurance industry is launching a multi-million-dollar advertising, grassroots, and lobbying campaign to persuade Washington officials not to reduce funding for Medicare Advantage next year. A centerpiece of this campaign is a new television ad, first reported by CNN, set to air Thursday as policymakers begin to set payment rates for the upcoming year. Preliminary rates for Medicare Advantage—which delivers private insurance to seniors—will be announced next month, with final rates settled in April. This campaign is a coordinated effort by insurers to avert reductions in Medicare Advantage payments. The Affordable Care Act introduced substantial funding cuts to Medicare Advantage, totaling $200 billion, alongside a 6.5% decrease this year. Insurance officials say these cuts have already compelled insurers to scale back their doctor networks, warning that further reductions could drive up costs and restrict access for seniors. "If Medicare Advantage is cut again, seniors will find out in October that their costs are increasing, their benefits are being reduced, and their provider choices are shrinking," said Robert Zirkelbach, spokesperson for America's Health Insurance Plans. In the ad, seniors tell policymakers that they depend on Medicare Advantage and will make their voices heard. Evelyn Harrell says, "No more cuts to Medicare Advantage." Mary Kay Boerner adds, "You know, we vote." Insurers believe that the timing—open enrollment in October, just weeks before congressional elections—puts added pressure on lawmakers. They argue elected officials won't want to explain to 14 million seniors why their health care costs more or their benefits have diminished.

Et sentralt element i kampanjen er en ny TV-reklame, først omtalt av CNN, som sendes torsdag når politiske beslutningstakere starter prosessen med å fastsette betalingssatser for det kommende året. Foreløpige satser for Medicare Advantage – som gir privat forsikring til eldre – kunngjøres neste måned, mens endelige satser fastsettes i april. Kampanjen er et koordinert forsøk fra forsikringsselskapene på å unngå reduksjoner i utbetalingene til Medicare Advantage. Affordable Care Act har innført betydelige kutt i finansieringen av Medicare Advantage, totalt 200 milliarder dollar, samt en nedgang på 6,5 % i år. Forsikringsbransjen hevder at disse kuttene allerede har tvunget dem til å redusere sine legetilbud, og de advarer om at ytterligere reduksjoner kan øke kostnadene og begrense tilgangen for eldre. "Hvis Medicare Advantage blir kuttet igjen, vil eldre oppdage i oktober at kostnadene deres øker, fordelene blir færre, og valgmulighetene til leverandører reduseres," sier Robert Zirkelbach, talsperson for America's Health Insurance Plans. article_content: Singer-songwriter Barry Manilow says he avoided discussing his sexuality for years because it could have ended his career. Manilow, who publicly came out as gay in 2017, told CNN's Chris Wallace that the public was not ready for anyone to come out in the 1970s. 'Now being gay is no big deal,' he added. 'Back in the 70s, it would have killed a career.' The Brooklyn-born singer has been in a relationship with his manager, Garry Kief, for 39 years. They married privately in 2014. Asked by Wallace whether he felt pressured to hide his identity, Manilow said he 'never thought about it.' He characterized his decision to come out in People magazine six years ago as a 'non-event.' 'I think everybody knew that Garry and I were a couple all those years,' he said. He also shared that his fans' response to the announcement was a 'beautiful experience.' 'I didn't know what was going to happen,' Manilow told Reuters, 'but I should have known better because my fans, and frankly the public, care about my happiness and I've always known that.' Manilow, whose real name is Barry Pincus, is one of the best-selling musicians of all time, known for orchestrated hits like 'Mandy,' 'Looks Like We Made It,' and 'Copacabana.' A natural performer, he remains active in his eighth decade, with a new Broadway musical and a recently announced Christmas TV special. He’s currently in the fourteenth year of a Las Vegas residency, with concerts scheduled through December 2024. Manilow's career began to rise in the mid-1970s, and he credits Kief with saving his life during those intense years. 'As my career exploded, it was just crazy. Going back to an empty hotel room night after night can be difficult, but meeting Garry changed that.' 'It was pretty lonely until I met Garry. Then it was fun.' Before his relationship with Kief, Manilow married his childhood sweetheart, Susan Deixler, in 1964. The marriage lasted one year and was annulled in 1966. Manilow said he 'really did love' Deixler, but the marriage ended more due to lack of commitment than his sexuality. 'We had a nice marriage, but I was always out making music and couldn't be a proper husband.' Reflecting on his career, Manilow said his experience writing jingles benefited his songwriting. 'You've got to get a hook in 15 seconds for a commercial, and the same goes for a pop song.' He also revealed that he came up with the concept for 'Copacabana' while recovering at the Copacabana Hotel in Rio de Janeiro in 1970. When asked about having a 'nervous breakdown,' Manilow said he was 'just kidding,' but did acknowledge that fame affected his mental health. 'Before Mandy and the big hits, I was happy in the background. Performing brought challenges, but it wasn’t a nervous breakdown; it was a real adjustment for me.'
