article_content: Winter is approaching, and for ski enthusiasts, that means it's time to hit the powdery slopes. However, the cost of skiing can be a concern for many. Fortunately, there are ways to make the most of your ski trip while keeping expenses in check. From versatile ski passes to affordable mountains and practical money-saving strategies, here's how you can ski more affordably this season. Top Ski Passes Multi-resort ski passes like Epic, Ikon, Mountain Collective, and Indy offer access to multiple mountains with one purchase. Each pass offers unique benefits and access to different resorts. Deciding which is right for you depends on your preferences, budget, and travel plans. The Epic Pass, managed by Vail Resorts, provides access to more than 80 resorts worldwide, including the Vail Resorts network (Vail, Breckenridge, Park City, Whistler Blackcomb, Stowe, and more). Epic has partner resorts in Europe and Japan as well. The full Epic Pass is $969 per adult (age 13+) and $494 per child (ages 5-12), offering unlimited access to 41 resorts and limited access (e.g., 7 days at Telluride). The Epic Local Pass is $719 per adult (age 19+), $585 per teen (13-18), and $377 per child (5-12). The Epic Day Pass starts at $110 per adult and $58 per child, customizable from one to seven days. All passes include 20% savings on food, lodging, rentals, Buddy Tickets, and discounted 'Ski With A Friend' Tickets. Passes are cheapest in spring and rise in price closer to the season. Prices increase after November 19—buy early for the best value. The Ikon Pass, from Alterra Mountain Company, gives access to 58 mountain destinations worldwide, including Winter Park (CO), Mammoth Mountain (CA), Stratton (VT), and others. The full Ikon Pass is $1,309 per adult (23+), $1,009 per young adult (13-22), $429 per child (5-12), and $149 for ages 4 and under—offering unlimited access at 16 mountains and up to 7 days at 41 others, with no blackout dates. The Ikon Base Pass ($979 per adult, $729 per young adult, $359 per child, $99 for 4 and under) grants access to 14 mountains and up to five days at 36 destinations, with some blackout dates. The Ikon Session Pass starts at $319 per adult, $259 per young adult, and $199 for ages 12 and under for two to four days. Passes are available until sold out; early purchase yields the best deal. The Mountain Collective Pass, created by Aspen Skiing Company, provides access to 24 resorts (e.g., Aspen Snowmass, Sugarbush, Snowbird, Alta, Jackson Hole). The pass costs $650 per adult (19+), $530 per teen (13-18), $210 per child (12 and under) and includes two days at each partner resort with no blackout dates, plus 50% off additional days at participating resorts. The Indy Pass gives two days each at over 180 independent ski areas in the US, Canada, Japan, and Europe, plus a 25% discount on the third day. There is a waitlist for this season; the base pass is $399 per adult and $199 per child, with some blackout dates. Money-Saving Ski Tips Buy your pass early for the lowest prices. Look for additional promotions and special offers by booking ahead. Bundle your pass with lodging for possible package discounts. Skiing midweek—avoiding weekends and holidays—leads to better prices and fewer crowds. Renting gear instead of buying, especially for occasional skiers, is cost-effective—it's usually cheaper to rent equipment from town than at the resort. If you live near a ski area, check for local season pass options which may be cheaper than daily tickets. Students and military members should inquire about discounts; many resorts provide reduced rates for these groups. Save on dining by packing your own snacks and meals. Consider skiing during the early or late season for discounted rates, keeping in mind that snow conditions may vary but can still provide a great experience. Affordable Ski Resorts Some affordable options include: Snowbasin Resort (Utah, Epic Pass)—well-kept slopes and good facilities; Homewood Mountain Resort (California, Ikon Pass)—great Lake Tahoe views and varied terrain; Taos Ski Valley (New Mexico, Mountain Collective)—challenging slopes and a unique cultural atmosphere; Mad River Glen (Vermont)—classic ski experience, independent; Bridger Bowl (Montana)—spacious terrain and no major crowds, independent. By planning ahead, using passes and deals, and making savvy choices, you can enjoy an affordable and memorable ski season.

article_content: Leeds United president Massimo Cellino returned to the UK in a defiant mood on Tuesday, telling the Football League it had 'made a big mistake' by disqualifying him from owning the club. Cellino, who had been in Bahrain for talks with former owner Gulf Finance House—which retains a 25 percent stake in Leeds—received the Football League’s announcement on Monday that he had failed its 'owners and directors' test due to a conviction for tax evasion in Italy. The League instructed Cellino to step down after obtaining further evidence of dishonesty from the Italian judge who convicted him in March. Cellino, 58, will be eligible to return to his position on March 18 next year, when the conviction is considered 'spent' under UK law. He has 14 days to appeal the decision. Speaking to ITV, Cellino said: 'I don't want to spend a lot of money on lawyers. This club in the last five years has spent more money on lawyers than on players.' When asked if he intended to appeal, he confirmed: 'Sure. I'm going to meet my lawyers. They (Football League) have made a big mistake. They're just throwing money away.' Cellino took control of Leeds in April when his family company, Eleanora Sport Limited, acquired 75 percent of the club's shares from GFH. He recently announced a new £20 million investment in the club, as well as a £5 million contribution from GFH following negotiations in Bahrain. The club issued a statement confirming receipt of the Football League’s notification of Cellino’s disqualification as a director until March 18, 2015, and said it is seeking legal advice. The statement added that removing Cellino and then reinstating him three months later would be destabilizing for the club, supporters, and sponsors. Cellino further commented: 'I solved a major problem in Bahrain, important for the survival of this club. The club is now financially strong and we will present the facts. We will fix the club and the league will realize its mistake.' The Football League initially attempted to block Cellino’s takeover following the tax conviction in April, but he appealed successfully. Judge Tim Kerr QC ruled at the time that Cellino's conduct was not considered dishonest, but noted that a different court assessment could change that. Cellino faces a second tax evasion charge in Sardinia related to another yacht. The latest case was adjourned in October, with no new date yet set. The League has asked an independent commission to consider whether Cellino and/or Leeds United breached its rules by not fully disclosing information from the Sardinian court. There is no time limit on the commission's findings. Eleanora Sport may implement a new management structure at Elland Road to demonstrate Cellino has no control during his disqualification. The Football League Board reviewed the Italian Court's judgment on Cellino, ultimately agreeing that he is subject to a disqualifying condition, except for Chief Executive Shaun Harvey, who abstained due to a prior association with Leeds. Cellino has the right to appeal within 14 days. Details of the Italian court judgment remain confidential, and a separate disciplinary commission will consider any potential breaches regarding the disclosure of information. Editor’s note: Shaun Harvey was Chief Executive and Director of Leeds United between 2004 and 2013. Cellino has dismissed two managers since becoming owner.
translated_content: Leeds United-president Massimo Cellino returnerte til Storbritannia i en trassig stemning tirsdag, og han fortalte Football League at de hadde 'gjort en stor feil' ved å diskvalifisere ham fra å eie klubben. Cellino hadde vært i Bahrain for samtaler med tidligere eier Gulf Finance House – som fortsatt eier 25 prosent av Leeds – da han mottok Football Leagues kunngjøring mandag om at han hadde strøket på 'owners and directors'-testen på grunn av en dom for skatteunndragelse i Italia. Ligasystemet instruerte Cellino om å trekke seg etter å ha mottatt ytterligere bevis på uredelighet fra den italienske dommeren som dømte ham i mars. Cellino, 58, vil være kvalifisert til å gå tilbake til sin posisjon 18. mars neste år, når dommen anses som 'oppgjort' etter britisk lov. Han har 14 dager på seg til å anke avgjørelsen. Til ITV sa Cellino: 'Jeg vil ikke bruke mye penger på advokater. Denne klubben har de siste fem årene brukt mer penger på advokater enn på spillere.' Da han ble spurt om han ville anke, bekreftet han: 'Selvsagt. Jeg skal møte advokatene mine. De (Football League) har gjort en stor feil. De kaster bare penger bort.' Cellino overtok Leeds i april, da hans familieselskap, Eleanora Sport Limited, kjøpte 75 prosent av klubbens aksjer fra GFH. Nylig kunngjorde han en ny investering på 20 millioner pund i klubben, samt et bidrag på 5 millioner pund fra GFH etter forhandlinger i Bahrain. Klubben ga ut en uttalelse som bekrefter mottakelsen av Football Leagues varsel om at Cellino er diskvalifisert som direktør frem til 18. mars 2015, og at de søker juridisk rådgivning. Uttalelsen la til at det å fjerne Cellino før han blir gjeninnsatt tre måneder senere, vil være destabiliserende for klubben, supporterne og sponsorene. Cellino uttalte videre: 'Jeg løste et stort problem i Bahrain, viktig for klubbens overlevelse. Klubben er nå økonomisk sterk, og vi vil legge frem fakta. Vi skal fikse klubben og ligaen vil innse at de gjør en feil.' Football League forsøkte først å hindre Cellinos overtakelse etter dommen for skatteunndragelse i april, men han anket med hell. Dommer Tim Kerr QC konkluderte den gang med at Cellinos handlinger ikke var uredelige, men bemerket at en annen rettsavgjørelse kunne endre vurderingen. Cellino står overfor en ny sak om skatteunndragelse i Sardinia knyttet til en annen yacht. Den nyeste saken ble utsatt i oktober, og ny dato er ikke satt. Ligaen har bedt en uavhengig kommisjon vurdere om Cellino og/eller Leeds United har brutt reglene ved å ikke opplyse fullt ut om informasjon fra Sardinia-domstolen. Det er ingen tidsfrist på kommisjonens avgjørelse. Eleanora Sport kan implementere en ny ledelsesstruktur på Elland Road for å vise at Cellino ikke har kontroll under diskvalifiseringsperioden. Styret i Football League gjennomgikk den italienske domstolens kjennelse om Cellino, og konkluderte med at han omfattes av en diskvalifiserende betingelse, med unntak av daglig leder Shaun Harvey, som avsto fra behandling på grunn av tidligere tilknytning til Leeds. Cellino har rett til å anke innen 14 dager. Detaljer om den italienske dommen er konfidensielle, og en egen disiplinærkommisjon vil vurdere eventuelle brudd vedrørende informasjonshåndtering. Redaktørens notat: Shaun Harvey var daglig leder og direktør i Leeds United mellom 2004 og 2013. Cellino har sparket to managere siden han ble eier.

article_content: Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot has expressed strong confidence that his government will be re-elected in the upcoming assembly election scheduled for November 25. Gehlot stated that his future political role will be determined by the Congress High Command, emphasizing that he will accept whatever responsibilities are assigned to him.  Speaking about the election, Gehlot remarked, 'People have made up their mind to return our government. We are aiming for 156 seats, and I believe the tradition of changing the government every five years will be broken this time. The state's residents are satisfied with our work, and it is clear the government will be repeated.'  Gehlot drew comparisons with Kerala, stating that just as the state's longstanding pattern of alternating governments ended during the pandemic, Rajasthan is also poised for change. He highlighted that his government received international praise for its COVID-19 response, notably through the 'Bhilwara model,' and for ensuring no one went hungry during the crisis by collaborating with religious leaders, NGOs, and activists.  He accused the central government of misusing agencies such as the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and Income Tax (IT) department to destabilize non-BJP governments, claiming these bodies are being used to pressure legislators and engineer political change instead of focusing on economic offenses.  Gehlot pointed to key social schemes introduced by his government including a social security law for gig workers, health insurance coverage of up to Rs 50 lakh per family, and extensive consultations with platform workers during the Bharat Jodo Yatra.  Criticizing Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Gehlot said the PM’s campaign language lacks the decorum befitting his office, calling for more respectful discourse with voters.  The Rajasthan assembly election will see voting take place for 199 of 200 seats (due to a postponed poll in Karanpur after the death of Congress candidate Gurmeet Singh Koonar). Votes will be counted on December 3. In the 2018 assembly election, Congress won 99 seats and BJP 73, with Gehlot becoming Chief Minister with support from BSP MLAs and Independents.  Additional news highlights include the Income Tax Department uncovering approximately ₹10,000 crore in tax evasion via social media sellers, and an allegation from Nawaz Modi that her estranged husband, industrialist Gautam Singhania, assaulted her and their daughter.

article_content: Roger Federer has enlisted his childhood hero, Stefan Edberg, as part of his coaching team for the upcoming tennis season. The 17-time Grand Slam champion announced on Facebook that Edberg, a Swedish tennis legend, will join the team beginning with the Australian Open in January 2014. "I'm happy to share that, starting in Melbourne, Stefan Edberg will join Severin Luthi on my coaching team," Federer said. "Severin, who has been with me for the past seven years, will continue to coach most weeks, and Stefan has agreed to work with us for at least 10 weeks. Stefan was my childhood hero, and I'm genuinely looking forward to learning from him." Following a tough 2013 season, Federer parted ways with his former coach, Paul Annacone, in October. Severin Luthi, the Swiss Davis Cup captain, remains in Federer's corner and expressed enthusiasm about collaborating with Edberg. "Like Roger, I have great respect for Stefan, and I believe he will add a lot to our team as Roger continues his quest for titles in 2014," Luthi said. Edberg has already spent a few days working with Federer in Dubai earlier this month. His addition follows the recent trend of top tennis players seeking guidance from former champions. Andy Murray hired Ivan Lendl before the 2012 season, and Maria Sharapova briefly teamed up with Jimmy Connors. Other notable partnerships include Novak Djokovic hiring Boris Becker, Kei Nishikori working with Michael Chang, and Richard Gasquet enlisting Sergi Bruguera. Becker was seen coaching Djokovic during the exhibition tournament in Abu Dhabi, where Djokovic reached the final after defeating Jo-Wilfried Tsonga. He is set to face David Ferrer, who managed an upset over world number one Rafael Nadal. Djokovic, who ended 2013 with a 24-match winning streak, stated he will not play further warm-up events before defending his Australian Open title, expressing confidence that Becker’s experience could elevate his game, both technically and mentally. Meanwhile, Andy Murray, returning from injury, finished fifth at the Abu Dhabi exhibition after defeating Stanislas Wawrinka.

article_content: David Letterman revealed to his audience on Thursday that he was the target of an attempted extortion and acknowledged having sexual relationships with several female staff members, according to a statement from his production company. During the recording of the 'Late Show,' Letterman shared that he testified before a grand jury earlier that day, something he had never done before. Three weeks prior, he received a package from an individual who claimed to have evidence of his affairs and demanded $2 million to prevent the information from being made public. He reported the incident to the Manhattan District Attorney’s office, which launched an investigation and made an arrest earlier on Thursday. In his testimony, Letterman confirmed he had relationships with staff members, noting that it could be embarrassing if exposed but emphasizing his desire to protect those involved, especially his family. Details regarding when the encounters occurred were not disclosed. Letterman married his long-time partner, Regina Lasko, in March. The couple, together since 1986, share a six-year-old son named Harry. Letterman has been the host of the 'Late Show with David Letterman' on CBS since 1993, after leaving NBC’s 'Late Night with David Letterman,' which aired for 11 years. 'Late Show' broadcasts at 11:30 p.m., while 'Late Night' aired an hour later.

article_content: This story originally appeared on Grist and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration. Although the Roman Empire fell over 1,500 years ago, its hold on popular imagination remains strong, as shown by a recent trend on TikTok. Women have been recording the men in their lives, asking a simple question: How often do you think about the Roman Empire? 'I guess, technically, like every day,' one boyfriend replied, leaving his girlfriend astonished. He wasn't the only one, as a surge of posts on Twitter, Instagram Reels, and news articles revealed. Some men, while driving on highways, say they think about the vast network of roads built by the Romans, some still in use today. Others ponder the Roman aqueduct system, constructed with concrete capable of hardening underwater. Many reasons explain the fascination with the rise and fall of ancient empires, beyond just gender dynamics. This interest often centers on a crucial question: How could something so vast and advanced fail? And, more urgently: Could something similar happen to us? With wildfires intensifying, political violence increasing, and public trust in government hitting record lows, it's not hard to imagine America facing serious challenges. Theories about societal breakdown linked to climate change have gained popularity in recent years, fueled by Jared Diamond’s 2005 book Collapse: How Societies Choose to Fail or Succeed. For example, the Roman Empire began to unravel during a period of volcanic eruptions that caused cooling and triggered the first pandemic of bubonic plague. The fall of the ancient Maya in Central America is associated with a major drought, while Angkor Wat’s decline in present-day Cambodia has been connected to periods of severe drought and monsoon flooding. If relatively small climate fluctuations contributed to the collapse of these grand civilizations, how can we expect to withstand the much more extreme shifts occurring today? Focusing only on catastrophe can lead to a distorted view of history, overlooking societies that faced environmental disasters yet endured. A 2021 review found 77% of studies examining the relationship between climate and society emphasized catastrophe, while only 10% focused on resilience. Recently, historians, anthropologists, and archaeologists have tried to address this gap. A new study analyzes 150 crises from different eras and regions, using a comprehensive data set covering over 5,000 years of human history, dating back to the Neolithic period. The research finds that environmental forces frequently play a critical role in societal collapse, but they are not solely responsible. Researchers from the Complexity Science Hub in Vienna, Austria, using mathematical models to study complex systems, identified examples of societies that survived famines, cold snaps, and other environmental stresses. Some Mesoamerican cities, such as the Zapotec settlements of Mitla and Yagul in present-day Oaxaca, not only survived but thrived during the same drought conditions believed to contribute to the Maya’s fall in the 8th century. The Maya themselves, prior to that point, survived five earlier droughts and continued to flourish. The new research, published last month in a peer-reviewed biological sciences journal from The Royal Society, suggests resilience is a capacity societies can build or lose over time. The authors conclude that a stable society can withstand even dramatic climate shocks, while a vulnerable one may collapse after a relatively minor disturbance.

Selv om Romerriket falt for over 1 500 år siden, har det fortsatt et sterkt grep om folks fantasi, noe en nylig trend på TikTok viser. Kvinner har filmet mennene i livene sine og stilt et enkelt spørsmål: Hvor ofte tenker du på Romerriket? 'Jeg tror egentlig, sånn teknisk sett, hver dag', svarte en kjæreste til stor forbauselse for kjæresten sin. Han var ikke alene, noe en bølge av innlegg på Twitter, Instagram Reels og nyhetsartikler tydeliggjorde. Noen menn forteller at de tenker på det store veinettet romerne bygde, som fortsatt er i bruk i dag, mens de kjører på motorveien. Andre reflekterer over romerske akvedukter, bygget med betong som kunne stivne under vann. Mange årsaker ligger bak fascinasjonen for gamle imperiers oppgang og fall, utover bare kjønnsdynamikk. Denne interessen dreier seg ofte om et viktig spørsmål: Hvordan kunne noe så stort og avansert feile? Og, mer presserende: Kan noe lignende skje med oss? Med økende skogbranner, mer politisk vold og laveste tall på folks tillit til myndighetene, er det lett å se for seg at USA kan møte store utfordringer. Teorier om samfunns-kollaps knyttet til klimaendringer har blitt populære de siste årene, ikke minst på grunn av Jared Diamonds bok fra 2005, Collapse: How Societies Choose to Fail or Succeed. For eksempel begynte Romerriket å vakle under en periode med vulkanutbrudd, noe som skapte avkjøling og førte til den første bølge av svartedauden. Maya-sivilisasjonens fall i Mellom-Amerika er knyttet til en alvorlig tørke, mens Angkor Wats nedgang i dagens Kambodsja har blitt koblet til kraftige perioder med tørke og monsunnflom. Hvis relativt små klimaendringer bidro til å knekke disse store sivilisasjonene, hvordan kan vi da forvente å overleve mye mer ekstreme forandringer i dag? Å bare fokusere på katastrofer gir et skjevt bilde av historien og overser samfunn som har stått imot miljøkatastrofer og overlevd. En gjennomgang fra 2021 viser at 77 % av studiene som undersøkte forbindelsen mellom klima og samfunn la vekt på katastrofer, mens bare 10 % tok for seg motstandsdyktighet. Historikere, antropologer og arkeologer har nylig forsøkt å tette dette gapet. En ny studie analyserer 150 kriser fra ulike tidsepoker og regioner, med et omfattende datasett som dekker over 5 000 år av menneskets historie, helt tilbake til steinalderen. Forskningen viser at miljøkrefter ofte spiller en avgjørende rolle i samfunnskollaps, men at de aldri står alene. Forskere fra Complexity Science Hub i Wien, Østerrike, som bruker matematiske modeller for å studere komplekse systemer, har funnet eksempler på samfunn som overlevde sultkatastrofer, kuldeperioder og andre miljøutfordringer. Noen mesoamerikanske byer, som Zapotekernes bosetninger Mitla og Yagul i dagens Oaxaca, ikke bare overlevde, men blomstret under de samme tørkeforholdene man mener bidro til Mayarikets fall på 700-tallet. Mayaene selv overlevde for øvrig fem tidligere tørkeperioder og fortsatte å vokse. Den nye forskningen, som ble publisert i fjor i et fagfellevurdert biologisk tidsskrift fra The Royal Society, antyder at motstandsdyktighet er en egenskap samfunn kan bygge opp – eller miste – over tid. Forfatterne konkluderer med at et stabilt samfunn kan takle selv dramatiske klimaendringer, mens et sårbart samfunn kan kollapse etter en mindre forstyrrelse.

article_content: A new video game controller called Delta Six, designed to closely resemble a real firearm, is set to launch early next year. The device, targeted at adult gamers, aims to provide players of first-person shooting (FPS) games with a more immersive experience than ever before. Some critics have raised concerns that such realistic accessories may encourage violent behavior, particularly among young people, though this is a matter of ongoing debate. Delta Six features the controls of a standard gamepad housed in a shell modeled after military-grade assault weapons. It includes a built-in accelerometer that works without calibration, allowing players to aim like using a real gun, with no need for external sensors. Pressure switches enable precision aiming by holding the controller to the user's cheek, while simulated recoil and reloading functions add to the realism. The controller comes with accessories to transform it from a full-length sniper rifle to a compact submachine gun, depending on the player's preference. Delta Six was developed by David Kotkin, known for his Avenger joypad modification. He claims the Delta Six allows players to feel more immersed and in control than ever before, stating, 'The only way to get more real is to enlist.' According to preliminary tests, Kotkin's company says the Delta Six is easier and faster to use for FPS games compared to standard controllers. The device is expected to retail at $89 (£55) and is recommended for adults, not for players under 21. Delta Six will be released early next year.

article_content: The United States is lowering the number of National Guard troops at the Southwest border and changing their role, as announced by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Pentagon. Beginning in January and completing by March, the plan will reduce ground troops from 1,200 to 300. Those remaining will shift to aerial support roles instead of ground patrols. According to officials, the modification is possible due to an increased Border Patrol workforce, implementation of new technology, and a decline in illegal border apprehensions. DHS data indicates that in the last fiscal year, apprehensions of undocumented immigrants were 340,252—a drop of 53% since 2008—while the Border Patrol's ranks have doubled to more than 21,000 agents since 2004. DHS and Defense representatives describe this as a strategic evolution towards better border security, emphasizing improvements like advanced aerial surveillance, quicker air-based responses, and upgraded reconnaissance tools. Despite these changes, some members of Congress, such as Republican Representatives Ted Poe and Lamar Smith, object to the troop reductions. Poe notes that only 44% of the border has operational control and suggests bipartisan action to stop the troop cuts. Smith argues that the administration's move undermines its own border security goals. On the other hand, Democratic Representative Silvestre Reyes supports the downsizing, citing better cost efficiency and enhanced border security measures. The Defense Department's budget for the border mission is expected to fall from $120 million to $60 million, and final specifics about expanded aerial surveillance are still being developed. Some lawmakers plan to continue to fight the reduction initiative.

article_content:
In 2014, the ramen burger dominated food trends, but just one month into 2015, New York has found its new must-try sandwich. M. Wells Dinette, a French-Canadian restaurant at MoMA's PS1 in Long Island City, has quickly made waves with its $13 spaghetti sandwich, selling up to 100 daily since it debuted on the menu a week ago. Instead of a patty, the sandwich features spaghetti tossed in a tomato-garlic sauce, mixed with pecorino cheese, coated in egg, and baked in a blini pan to form a cohesive patty. 

Chef Aidan O'Neal explained to the New York Post: 'The result is crispy on the outside and very juicy on the inside.' It's served on a toasted onion roll with garlic butter and topped with a layer of chopped Caesar salad and red pepper flakes. 

While delicious, it's far from a low-calorie option. A restaurant staff member shared that they cram as much as possible between the buns: about an appetizer-sized portion of pasta (roughly 420 calories, per Calorieking.com) and salad (204 calories), the bun (150 calories), pecorino (20 calories), a generous serving of garlic butter (102 calories), and homemade potato chips on the side (160 calories), totaling just over 1,000 calories. 

The spaghetti sandwich, conceived by owner Hugue Dufour, first appeared on the menu four years ago despite initial skepticism from the kitchen. Mr. O'Neal recalled, 'We cooks all kind of scoffed at the idea, but he was right; it's very, very good.' After being removed last year in favor of more seasonal dishes, the sandwich returned by popular demand. 

Demand has been intense, according to Mr. O'Neal: 'It's been insane. We'll get an order to fire up seven at a time for one table, then another, and another.'

For research purposes, the Femail team visited to sample the sandwich. Wary of the carbs, they split one sandwich between two, but were quickly won over by the appealing combination of textures and flavors. 

Charlie Lankston, Femail's U.S. Assistant Editor, said, 'It was so much tastier than I was expecting and not nearly as "carby" as I thought. The tomato sauce was delicious, and the tangy Caesar dressing really balanced the flavors.' 

Daters beware—this is not a neat sandwich. 'Maybe save it for the third date,' Charlie suggested. 'It was incredibly messy, but worth the tomato stains—and I'd definitely eat it again.'

article_content: When actress Scarlett Johansson discovered her face and voice had been used without her consent to promote an AI app online, she took legal action against the app's developer, Lisa AI. While that video was removed, many deepfake videos circulate online for weeks, such as a recent unauthorized ad using the likeness of internet personality MrBeast to promote $2 iPhones. Deepfake technology has become sophisticated enough that it can be difficult to distinguish between real and AI-generated content. Recent surveys by Northeastern University, Voicebot.ai, and Pindrop show that about half of respondents could not tell the difference. This is a growing issue, especially for celebrities. But new tools may soon help the public detect and defend against deepfakes—and also make it harder for AI systems to generate convincing fakes. Ning Zhang, assistant professor of computer science and engineering at Washington University in St. Louis, is leading research on a new tool called AntiFake. According to Zhang, 'Generative AI has become such an enabling technology that we think will change the world. However, when it's being misused, we need ways to defend against it.' AntiFake, inspired by the University of Chicago's Glaze (which protects visual artists from AI scraping), scrambles audio signals so AI systems can't easily replicate them. The tool is new and will be presented at a major security conference in Denmark soon. To use AntiFake, people can upload their voice track to the platform before publishing a video. AntiFake distorts the audio in a way that is unnoticeable to human listeners but confuses AI systems, making it difficult for them to create realistic voice clones. Users retain full rights to their original audio tracks. However, AntiFake cannot protect voices that are already widely available online, as AI models might already have enough data to clone them. When released, AntiFake is expected to offer a proactive defense against audio deepfakes. Meanwhile, other detection solutions exist, such as digital watermarks (Google's SynthID, Meta's Stable Signature) and forensic analysis by companies like Pindrop and Veridas. Deepfake detection methods also have limitations. As Siwei Lyu, a computer science professor at the University at Buffalo, notes, detection only works after content is posted and may not prevent initial harm. Rupal Patel, a professor at Northeastern University and an executive at Veritone, highlights that while safeguards are important, generative AI can also do good—like helping those who lost their voices to illness. For example, actor Val Kilmer now uses a synthetic voice after losing his own due to throat cancer. Patel and other experts call for balance, since high-quality datasets are needed for beneficial AI applications, but user consent remains crucial. Legal measures are under discussion. In October, U.S. lawmakers proposed the NO FAKES Act of 2023, aiming to make creators of unauthorized deepfakes legally responsible. Attorney Yael Weitz points out that this could create unified federal protection, since only about half of U.S. states currently have 'right of publicity' laws—and protections vary widely. A nationwide law could take years to implement. This article was edited by Jennifer Vanasco and audio produced by Isabella Gomez Sarmiento.

article_content: New survey data released Monday by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York shows that US consumers expect inflation to keep easing, believe the labor market will stay strong, and anticipate maintaining higher spending levels compared to pre-pandemic times. The October Survey of Consumer Expectations offered a more positive outlook than the previous month's report, when consumers were as worried about missing minimum debt payments as they were in the early stages of the Covid-19 pandemic. In October, the average perceived probability of missing a minimum debt payment dropped to 11.99%, matching June's figure and remaining within pre-pandemic ranges. Consumers’ short-term (one-year) and long-term (five-year) inflation expectations both declined by 0.1 percentage points from the previous month, settling at 3.6% and 2.7%, respectively. However, median inflation expectations for the three-year horizon held steady at 3%, which is a high for the year. The Federal Reserve pays close attention to consumer inflation expectations because they can influence future inflation: if people expect prices to rise, they may spend more and seek higher wages, prompting businesses to raise prices. Recently, Fed officials have expressed concern about worsening expectations. On Friday, the University of Michigan's consumer survey indicated declining sentiment about the current economic situation and a slight increase in long-term inflation expectations. Although inflation is cooling, price increases have not fully ended. Regarding earnings, expectations for wage growth decreased 0.2 percentage points to 2.83%, the lower end of the series since September 2021. The perceived probability of losing a job in the next year edged up to 12.7%, but consumers are also somewhat more optimistic about their chances of finding another job, with that probability rising to 56.6%. Median expected household income growth increased by 0.1 percentage point to 3.1%, compared to 2.7% in February 2020. Spending expectations, at 5.25%, have fallen from a high of 9% in May 2022 but still exceed pre-pandemic levels of 3.1%. Overall, more respondents reported their households were better off than a year ago. For the year ahead, expectations are mixed, with similar shares believing they will be either better or worse off financially.

I oktober falt den gjennomsnittlige oppfattede sannsynligheten for å miste en minste gjeldsbetaling til 11,99 %, likt som i juni og innenfor nivåene før pandemien. Forbrukernes inflasjonsforventninger på ett og fem år sank begge med 0,1 prosentpoeng fra forrige måned, til henholdsvis 3,6 % og 2,7 %. Median inflasjonsforventning for treårshorisonten holdt seg imidlertid stabil på 3 %, noe som er årets høyeste. Nylig har Fed-tjenestemenn uttrykt bekymring for at forventningene kan forverres. For det kommende året er forventningene mer blandede, med omtrent like mange som tror de vil få det bedre som dårligere økonomisk.

article_content: The colourful flash of a red squirrel in the trees is a spectacle that few Britons have witnessed. After more than a century of decline, experts say the plight of the native red squirrel in Britain may finally be improving. According to a recent RSPB survey, fewer than one in 20 people in Britain have ever seen this distinctive animal. Research by Red Squirrel Northern England shows that red squirrels have recently been spotted in parts of the Yorkshire Dales, the North Pennines, and Lancashire for the first time in decades. This resurgence is largely attributed to extensive conservation efforts, particularly the control of invasive grey squirrels. Grey squirrels, introduced to Britain from America in 1876, carry a pox virus that is fatal to red squirrels. As a result, grey squirrel populations grew to 2.5 million, while the number of red squirrels fell to 120,000, mainly in Scotland. Only about 15,000 red squirrels remained in England, primarily in the Lake District and Northumberland, with a few isolated populations on the Isle of Wight and Brownsea Island in Dorset. Recent conservation work has helped boost red squirrel populations, which increased by 7% last year. Prince Charles recently ordered a cull of grey squirrels on his Duchy of Cornwall lands. The latest findings indicate that the number of red squirrels in the north has remained stable while expanding their territory. New sightings this year include Upper Swaledale in Yorkshire, Teesdale in County Durham, and Ormskirk in Lancashire. Experts note that efforts to control and remove grey squirrels are showing results. Red squirrel colonies are now stable in Cumbria and Northumberland, according to Red Squirrel Northern England. Nick Mason, project manager at Red Squirrels Northern England, stated: 'In several areas, red squirrels appear to be reclaiming territory long lost. Time will tell whether these new populations will persist, but they are all near areas with high-quality conservation work. This is really exciting!' A recent Liverpool University study found that some red squirrels in northern England may be developing immunity to the squirrel pox virus. However, experts believe the main reason for the rising numbers is continued control of grey squirrels. Dr. David Bullock, head of nature conservation at the National Trust, remarked: 'It looks like we might be turning a corner with red squirrels. There is cautious optimism, but definitely optimism. Personally, I have never been more positive about the future of red squirrels. This is due to a lot of hard work. However, we cannot become complacent; managing grey squirrels remains essential, and there are still large parts of Britain without red squirrels.' He added: 'Removing grey squirrels seems to be key. When you remove grey squirrels, red squirrels tend to return—it’s that simple.' Prince Charles recently ordered a cull of grey squirrels on his Duchy of Cornwall lands, and the government is encouraging others to do the same. The Forestry Commission agrees that controlling grey squirrels is essential for red squirrels to thrive. Earlier this month, it introduced a new policy offering grants of £100 per hectare to landowners who reduce grey squirrel populations. Landowners must also have a plan to control grey squirrels to qualify for other woodland funding. While there was consideration to make culling grey squirrels mandatory, this was ruled out after public consultation. Instead, the new policy emphasizes incentivizing landowners to manage grey squirrels, noting that landowners and managers play a critical role in the success of these efforts.

After losing to Rafael Nadal in the U.S. Open final, Novak Djokovic is determined to help Serbia reach its first Davis Cup final. The 22-year-old world number two told the ATP Tour website he's disappointed, but his attention has shifted entirely to the Davis Cup semifinal against the Czech Republic in Belgrade. 

'I can't deny I'm disappointed, but I'm not about to dwell on it,' said Djokovic. 'I gave everything I had to beat Nadal, and now my focus is on the Davis Cup.' 

Djokovic will face Radek Stepanek in the opening singles match, followed by Janko Tipsarevic facing world number seven Tomas Berdych in the second singles rubber. 

Serbia reached the semifinals after defeating the United States and Croatia. Meanwhile, the Czech Republic aims for their second straight final appearance. 

The other semifinal in Lyon features France against Argentina. France will be represented by Gael Monfils in the absence of the injured Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, after defeating defending champions Spain. Monfils told the official Davis Cup website, 'For an emotional player like me, the Davis Cup is an incredible experience.' 

Argentina, runners-up in 2006 and 2008, advance to the semifinals following away victories over Sweden and Russia, hoping to secure another spot in the final.

article_content: A significant cyber-attack was launched against Spamhaus, an anti-spam organization based in Geneva and London, following a dispute with the hosting company Cyberbunker, which operates from a former NATO bunker in the Netherlands. Spamhaus, which maintains a blacklist of servers involved in sending spam, recently blacklisted Cyberbunker. In response, Spamhaus alleges that Cyberbunker orchestrated a distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack that flooded Spamhaus’s servers with vast amounts of traffic. The attack—described by security experts as among the largest ever seen—affected internet infrastructure on a global scale, disrupting access to major sites such as Netflix and causing delays in website loading for millions of users. The DDoS attack targeted the Domain Name System (DNS), a crucial layer that translates website names into numerical addresses, thereby amplifying its impact across the internet. Some banking customers, particularly those using Natwest, RBS, and Ulster Bank, reported difficulties accessing mobile banking services, though these issues have not been officially linked to the cyber-attack. Separately, Egyptian authorities detained three divers suspected of tampering with undersea internet cables near Alexandria, potentially affecting Egypt's internet connectivity. It remains unclear whether this incident is connected to the broader disruptions. Cybersecurity experts such as Professor Alan Woodward and Matthew Prince have compared the scale of the attack to a ‘nuclear bomb’ for web infrastructure. Businesses and individuals experienced delays and outages, illustrating the rising threat of large-scale cyber-attacks. Sven Olaf Kamphuis, speaking on behalf of Cyberbunker, has criticized Spamhaus for what he calls an abuse of power in deciding which organizations are allowed on the internet. DDoS attacks have become increasingly powerful in recent years, posing significant risks to organizations reliant on internet accessibility.
translated_content: Et betydelig dataangrep ble rettet mot Spamhaus, en anti-spam-organisasjon med base i Genève og London, etter en konflikt med hostingfirmaet Cyberbunker, som opererer fra en tidligere NATO-bunker i Nederland. Spamhaus, som opprettholder en svarteliste over servere involvert i utsending av spam, satte nylig Cyberbunker på listen. Som svar hevder Spamhaus at Cyberbunker sto bak et distribuert tjenestenektangrep (DDoS) som oversvømmet Spamhaus’ servere med enorme mengder trafikk. Angrepet – beskrevet av sikkerhetseksperter som et av de største noensinne – påvirket internett-infrastrukturen globalt, forstyrret tilgangen til store nettsteder som Netflix og førte til forsinkelser i lasting av nettsider for millioner av brukere. DDoS-angrepet var rettet mot Domain Name System (DNS), et avgjørende lag som oversetter nettstedsnavn til numeriske adresser, og forsterket dermed effekten på internett. Noen bankkunder, spesielt de som bruker Natwest, RBS og Ulster Bank, rapporterte vanskeligheter med å få tilgang til mobilbanktjenester, men det er ikke offisielt bekreftet at dette er knyttet til dataangrepet. Samtidig pågrep egyptiske myndigheter tre dykkere mistenkt for å ha tuklet med undersjøiske internettkabler nær Alexandria, noe som potensielt påvirket Egypts internettforbindelse. Det er fortsatt uklart om denne hendelsen har sammenheng med de bredere forstyrrelsene. Cybersikkerhetseksperter som professor Alan Woodward og Matthew Prince har sammenlignet angrepets omfang med en ‘atombombe’ for nettinfrastrukturen. Både bedrifter og privatpersoner opplevde forsinkelser og utfall, noe som illustrerer den økende trusselen fra store dataangrep. Sven Olaf Kamphuis, som uttaler seg på vegne av Cyberbunker, har kritisert Spamhaus for det han kaller maktmisbruk ved å bestemme hvilke organisasjoner som får tilgang til internett. DDoS-angrep har blitt stadig kraftigere de siste årene og utgjør betydelige risikoer for virksomheter som er avhengige av internett-tilgang.

article_content: Sometimes, fortune can be found in the most unlikely places—garage sales, attics, or even a farmer’s field. Here are six real-life stories of people who unexpectedly discovered valuable treasures. 1. Lost Hammer, Legendary Hoard: In 1992, a farmer in Suffolk, England, lost his hammer and asked friend Eric Lawes to help search with a metal detector. Instead, Lawes uncovered the Hoxne Hoard—over 24 bronze coins, 565 gold and 14,191 silver coins, plus jewelry and statues from the Roman Empire. Under British law, the hoard was declared a Treasure Trove, making it government property, but the farmer and Lawes shared a reward of £1.75 million (about $2.8 million). Today, the hoard is on display at the British Museum, though the hammer’s fate remains unknown. 2. Arkansas’s Diamond Finds: In 1924, W.O. Bassum unearthed a 40.23-carat diamond near Murfreesboro, Arkansas—a site now known as Crater of Diamonds State Park. The park has a 'finders keepers' policy, so Bassum’s 'Uncle Sam Diamond' remains North America’s largest diamond discovery. Others have followed, including 'The Star of Murfreesboro' and the perfectly rated Strawn-Wagner Diamond. On average, two diamonds are found daily at the park, keeping the dream of striking it rich alive. 3. Declaration of (Financial) Independence: Michael Sparks bought a print of the Declaration of Independence at a thrift store for $2.48, later realizing it was one of only 200 official copies from 1820—his was the 36th discovered. After authentication, Sparks sold his find at auction for $477,650. 4. Masterpiece Behind the Wall: An Indiana tool-and-die company worker purchased furniture and an old flower painting for $30. Years later, he learned it was an original by American artist Martin Johnson Heade. The painting, 'Magnolias on Gold Velvet Cloth,' was sold to the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, for $1.2 million. 5. A Pendant Worth Millions?: After years of metal-detecting, Mary Hannaby found a gold pendant featuring an intricate crucifixion scene. Experts valued it at up to £2.5 million due to its rarity but, at auction, bids peaked at just £38,000—well below expectations. 6. The Pollock Mystery: Retired truck driver Teri Horton bought a large, abstract painting from a thrift store for $5. A local art teacher suggested it could be a lost Jackson Pollock. Although forensic evidence suggests a link, experts dispute its authenticity due to lack of provenance. Horton’s struggle became the subject of the documentary 'Who the *$&% is Jackson Pollock?' These stories remind us that exceptional finds can be hidden in everyday places, though turning discovery into fortune isn’t always guaranteed.

Mistet hammer, funnet skatt: I 1992 mistet en bonde i Suffolk, England, hammeren sin og ba vennen Eric Lawes lete med metalldetektor. I stedet fant Lawes «Hoxne Hoard»—over 24 bronsemynter, 565 gull- og 14 191 sølvmynter, samt smykker og statuer fra Romerriket. article_content: A 40-year-old construction worker from California, Alazar Ortiz, lost his right hand and three fingers on his left hand in a fireworks accident over the Fourth of July weekend. The incident happened around 10 p.m. on Friday at his mother’s home near Cassel Park in San Jose, while his family watched nearby. According to relatives, a 'professional-grade explosive' used to trigger a large fireworks display malfunctioned and exploded. Doctors amputated Ortiz's right hand and three fingers on his left hand due to the injuries. Family members reported that Ortiz had bought the illegal fireworks for $50 from a market store in San Jose. The police are currently investigating the shop. Ortiz’s nephew, Luis Ortiz, told NBC Bay Area, 'We’re trying to get those fireworks off the streets, especially from that store. For $50, he lost both his hands.' Ortiz’s family is heartbroken but grateful he survived. Ortiz, who works in construction, will not be able to return to his job following the accident. He also suffered burns to his face and ears. There is currently no information on when he will be released from the hospital. The explosion occurred on Leeward Drive.

Ifølge pårørende var det et 'profesjonelt sprengstoff' brukt til å utløse et stort fyrverkeri som sviktet og eksploderte. Politiet etterforsker nå butikken. Ortiz' nevø, Luis Ortiz, fortalte NBC Bay Area: 'Vi prøver å få dette fyrverkeriet bort fra gatene, spesielt fra den butikken. Det finnes foreløpig ingen opplysninger om når han blir skrevet ut fra sykehuset. Eksplosjonen skjedde i Leeward Drive.

article_content: Authorities have identified a body that washed up on a Florida beach as that of a missing cruise ship worker. According to a news release from Clearwater Police, 27-year-old Cliford B. Minej was found on Friday morning. The body was discovered around 7:15 a.m. by a person walking along the 1500 block of Gulf Boulevard on Sand Key. Minej, who was from Thane, India, worked aboard the Holland America Line cruise ship 'Ryndam,' which docked in Tampa last Sunday. Police believe Minej jumped or fell from the ship near Egmont Key on Sunday before it arrived at port. The U.S. Coast Guard had searched Tampa Bay-area waters, but did not find him prior to the discovery on the beach. Clearwater is approximately 20 miles from Egmont Key. The Pinellas County Medical Examiner's Office determined the death to be accidental. Holland America Line released a statement to The Tampa Bay Times expressing deep sadness at the loss and offering condolences to Minej’s family.

Kroppen ble oppdaget rundt klokken 07:15 av en person som gikk langs 1500-blokken av Gulf Boulevard på Sand Key. Minej, som var fra Thane i India, arbeidet om bord på Holland America Line-cruiseskipet 'Ryndam', som la til kai i Tampa forrige søndag. Politiet mener at Minej hoppet eller falt fra skipet nær Egmont Key søndag før det ankom havnen. Den amerikanske kystvakten hadde søkt i Tampa Bay-området, men fant ham ikke før kroppen dukket opp på stranden. Clearwater ligger omtrent 32 kilometer fra Egmont Key. Pinellas County rettsmedisiner har konkludert med at dødsfallet var et uhell. Holland America Line ga en uttalelse til The Tampa Bay Times der de uttrykker dyp sorg over tapet og sender kondolanser til Minejs familie.

article_content: Joe Koblenzer, a 73-year-old Vietnam veteran who spent over three years working at a Cracker Barrel in Venice, Florida, was terminated after giving a homeless man a corn muffin and some condiment packets. Joe, known for his friendly demeanor, had previously received write-ups for minor policy violations, such as providing a coffee to a customer and taking a fountain drink while on shift. According to Cracker Barrel, Joe received several warnings about giving away food, behavior which violates company policy. On the fifth such incident, Joe was dismissed as per company rules. In their statement, Cracker Barrel acknowledged Joe's military service but emphasized the necessity of adhering to policy. Although Joe admits he broke the rule, he feels the decision was severe, considering his service background and strong connection with guests. The incident has triggered substantial debate online, with many showing support for Joe and criticizing the restaurant’s decision, while others argue that enforcing rules is necessary for all employees. Now, Joe is seeking new opportunities to supplement his Social Security and remains proud of his recognition as a dedicated host at Cracker Barrel.

Ifølge Cracker Barrel mottok Joe flere advarsler om å gi bort mat, noe som bryter med selskapets retningslinjer. Da det skjedde for femte gang, mistet han jobben i tråd med reglementet. Selv om Joe innrømmer at han brøt reglene, føler han at avgjørelsen var streng, spesielt med tanke på hans bakgrunn og gode forhold til gjestene. article_content: A Beechcraft Baron 58 was forced to make an emergency landing at Toowoomba airport in southern Queensland after its front landing wheel failed to deploy. The incident occurred on Wednesday morning as the plane returned to Darling Downs city from Hervey Bay on Queensland's Fraser Coast. Pilot Mark Crampton and his co-pilot attempted three times to deploy the nose wheel, both automatically and manually, but it would not lock in place. Although they were unharmed, the pair were shaken by the experience. Shortly after takeoff, Mr. Crampton heard a loud bang and a clunk as the nose gear was retracted, raising concerns for the crew. Ground observers confirmed the nose wheel had not properly released, making an emergency landing necessary. The plane touched down nose-first, skidding along the runway at approximately 200 mph before coming to a stop. Both pilots exited the plane immediately due to concerns about the risk of fire. Mr. Crampton credited their training for managing the emergency, describing the sound of the nose dragging as 'pretty scary.' He emphasized the experience had not deterred him from flying.

Pilot Mark Crampton og hans andrepilot forsøkte tre ganger å felle ut nesehjulet, både automatisk og manuelt, men det låste seg ikke på plass. Selv om de slapp uskadd fra hendelsen, var begge preget av opplevelsen. Kort tid etter avgang hørte Crampton et høyt smell og dunk da nesehjulet skulle trekkes inn, noe som gjorde besetningen bekymret. Bakkepersonell bekreftet senere at nesehjulet ikke var skikkelig ute, og derfor ble nødlanding nødvendig. Flyet landet med nesen først og skled bortover rullebanen i omtrent 320 km/t før det stanset. Crampton gir opplæringen æren for at de håndterte nødsituasjonen, og beskriver lyden av nesa som dro langs rullebanen som 'ganske skremmende.' Han understreker at hendelsen ikke har skremt ham fra å fly videre.

article_content:
Ally McCoist has submitted his resignation as Rangers manager after becoming increasingly disillusioned with the club’s internal struggles and ongoing cost-cutting. The club’s recent 2-0 loss to Queen of the South highlighted this difficult time for the Ibrox team. Reports suggest McCoist’s decision was prompted by the dismissal of several long-time employees, with youth academy leader Jimmy Sinclair potentially next.

Although McCoist has given notice, he plans to continue his duties for the full 12-month notice period unless an agreement for early departure or gardening leave is reached. The situation is complicated by the club's financial instability—Rangers are in need of fresh funds and are unable to pay out McCoist’s contract in full. While he previously agreed to a significant pay cut, his severance is still calculated from his original salary, and would have been even greater had he been fired instead of resigning.

The decision came to light just hours before the Queen of the South match. McCoist has refrained from confirming the details publicly but has thanked fans and apologized for the team’s poor performance, saying he remains committed to managing Rangers for now. He acknowledged the club’s turbulent years and stressed his continued focus on the job.

Leadership changes may be on the horizon, with a search underway for new executives and finance directors; former Newcastle managing director Derek Llambias, an ally of Mike Ashley, is currently involved in club operations. The team has seen multiple staff redundancies as part of a wider review. Sources indicate McCoist has been considering leaving for some time, worn down by the financial uncertainty and layoffs.

Former teammate Stuart McCall expressed sadness over the news and praised McCoist’s steadfastness during a tough period for Rangers. The club still faces significant scrutiny and is seeking vital new investment as its annual general meeting approaches.

McCoist har gjort det klart at han har til hensikt å fortsette i jobben gjennom hele oppsigelsesperioden på tolv måneder, med mindre en tidligere avgang eller permisjon avtales. Klubbens økonomiske trøbbel gjør situasjonen vanskelig – Rangers mangler penger og har ikke råd til å betale ut hele kontrakten til McCoist. Selv etter å ha gått med på en stor lønnsreduksjon tidligere, beregnes sluttpakken hans etter den opprinnelige lønnen, og den ville vært enda større dersom han hadde blitt avskjediget fremfor å si opp selv.

article_content: Bengaluru and neighboring areas are expected to see moderate to light rain this weekend, due to a cyclonic circulation off the Kerala coast. According to officials, this rainy spell may last until the end of November. In related news, Chennai experienced cloudy weather, a mild breeze, and below-normal daytime temperatures following the impact of two cyclonic circulations—one over Comorin and another over the southwest Bay of Bengal. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast moderate rainfall over the next two days and issued yellow alerts for several districts. The rain is expected to move from east to west, affecting various parts of the state. For Mumbai and its neighboring districts—Thane and Palghar—the IMD has also issued yellow alerts for November 25-26, anticipating unseasonal rainfall, thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds. This rainfall, caused by a trough along the Bay of Bengal coast, could help improve air quality in the region. Earlier, several parts of Mumbai reported heavy rainfall.

I relaterte nyheter har Chennai hatt overskyet vær, mild bris og dagtemperaturer under normalen etter påvirkning fra to sykloniske sirkulasjoner—en over Comorin og en annen over sørvest i Bengalbukta. Det indiske meteorologiske instituttet (IMD) har varslet moderat nedbør de neste to dagene og sendt ut gult farevarsel for flere distrikter. Regnet ventes å bevege seg fra øst mot vest og ramme ulike deler av delstaten. For Mumbai og tilstøtende distrikter—Thane og Palghar—har IMD også sendt ut gult farevarsel for 25.–26. november, med forventning om uvanlig regn, tordenvær, lyn og kraftig vind. Dette regnværet, forårsaket av en lavtrykkssone langs Bengalbukta, kan bidra til bedre luftkvalitet i området. Tidligere har flere deler av Mumbai rapportert kraftig nedbør.

article_content: NEW DELHI: India being a net importer of steel is a matter of concern, Tata Steel CEO & MD T V Narendran said on Tuesday. The government has assured intervention if imports continue to rise, Narendran said at the ISA Steel Conclave in the capital. "It's a bit concerning because global steel prices remain soft, mainly due to China. You heard Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal mention that if imports increase, the government will explore ways to support us," Narendran said when asked about India becoming a net steel importer in October. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal assured the domestic industry that India will not accept unfair taxes and will strive for a fair deal for producers and exporters. He said India has already raised its concerns about the carbon tax with the European Union (EU) and the World Trade Organization (WTO). The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), also known as the carbon tax, will take effect from January 1, 2026. However, from October 1 this year, companies in seven carbon-intensive sectors, including steel, cement, fertilizer, aluminum, and hydrocarbon products, must share carbon emission data with the EU. "I assure you we are extremely concerned about CBAM. We are taking it up with the WTO very seriously. We will work to secure a fair deal for Indian producers and exporters, and no one is complacent about CBAM," Goyal said at a steel industry event. According to SteelMint India, India's steel imports were 0.46 million tonnes (MT) in October 2023, compared to exports of 0.24 MT. Responding to a question about Tata Steel Netherlands' decarbonization plans, Narendran said, "We have already submitted a proposal to the Dutch government which will be discussed further." After securing funding in the UK, Tata Steel is now seeking financial assistance from the Netherlands government to pursue its decarbonization strategy. In the Netherlands, Tata Steel operates a 7 million tonnes per year plant in IJmuiden. The company aims to produce carbon-neutral steel in Europe by 2050. Narendran did not disclose the estimated amount of funding being sought from the Netherlands government, stating, "We prefer not to share that now; let's wait for the discussions to happen."
translated_content: NEW DELHI: India er en nettoimportør av stål, noe som er bekymringsfullt, sa administrerende direktør og konsernsjef i Tata Steel, T V Narendran, tirsdag. Regjeringen har forsikret at de vil gripe inn dersom importen fortsetter å øke, uttalte Narendran på ISA Steel Conclave i hovedstaden. "Det er litt bekymringsfullt fordi de globale stålprisene fortsatt er lave, hovedsakelig på grunn av Kina. Du hørte handelsminister Piyush Goyal nevne at dersom importen øker, vil regjeringen se på muligheter for å støtte oss," sa Narendran da han ble spurt om India ble en nettoimportør av stål i oktober. Handels- og industriminister Piyush Goyal forsikret den innenlandske industrien om at India ikke vil akseptere urettferdige avgifter og vil kjempe for en rettferdig avtale for produsenter og eksportører. Han sa at India allerede har fremhevet sine bekymringer om karbonavgiften overfor EU og Verdens handelsorganisasjon (WTO). Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), også kjent som karbonavgiften, vil tre i kraft fra 1. januar 2026. Imidlertid må selskaper innen syv karbonintensive sektorer, inkludert stål, sement, gjødsel, aluminium og hydrokarbonprodukter, dele utslippsdata med EU fra 1. oktober i år. "Jeg kan forsikre dere om at vi er svært bekymret for CBAM. Vi tar dette opp med WTO på alvor. Vi vil arbeide for å sikre en rettferdig avtale for indiske produsenter og eksportører, og ingen er tilfredse med CBAM," sa Goyal på et arrangement for stålindustrien. Ifølge SteelMint India importerte India 0,46 millioner tonn (MT) stål i oktober 2023, sammenlignet med eksport av 0,24 MT. Som svar på et spørsmål om Tata Steel Nederlans planer for avkarbonisering, sa Narendran: "Vi har allerede sendt et forslag til den nederlandske regjeringen som vil bli diskutert videre." Etter å ha sikret finansiering i Storbritannia, søker Tata Steel nå økonomisk støtte fra den nederlandske regjeringen for å forfølge sin avkarboniseringsstrategi. I Nederland driver Tata Steel et anlegg med en kapasitet på 7 millioner tonn per år i IJmuiden. Selskapet har som mål å produsere karbonnøytralt stål i Europa innen 2050. Narendran ønsket ikke å oppgi hvor mye støtte de søker fra den nederlandske regjeringen og uttalte: "Det vil vi ikke dele nå, la oss vente til samtalene er ferdige."

article_content: In Kirkby, Merseyside, a town facing economic challenges, Poundcafe has opened to the public, serving a full English breakfast for just £1. On its first day, roughly 300 locals came to try the cafe's four-item breakfast, allowing selections from eggs, bacon, sausage, hash browns, baked beans, or tomatoes. Poundcafe is operated by Poundbakery, a company that has established 60 locations in the northwest in two years. Customers can expand their breakfast with extra items for 25p each. Drinks and desserts, such as cakes and gingerbread men, are priced at either 50p or £1. Community members like Vicky Robinson, 19, and Natalie Bennett, 31, praised the new spot for its affordability and community value. Vicky highlighted having an accessible place to socialize, and Natalie said she’d return after enjoying a sausage bap and tea. Both saw the Poundcafe as beneficial for Kirkby. The launch ties in with broader regeneration campaigns in the UK, such as the recent initiative in Stoke-on-Trent, where rundown homes in Cobridge were sold for £1 each to qualifying locals, attracting hundreds of applicants. Kirkby, about 10 miles from Liverpool, has high unemployment; a recent Sheffield Hallam University study estimated that 16.1% of working-age people in the area are unemployed, while official numbers put it lower. Management at Poundcafe, including Marketing Manager Keeley Palin and Regional Manager Cathy Fulton, expressed excitement at the busy launch and hope that the cafe will become a welcoming and affordable gathering place. Similar affordable ventures in deprived areas, like Muhammad Nazir’s £1 fish stall in East London, show the popularity of these community-focused concepts.

article_content: According to new findings from the Pew Internet and American Life Project, 13% of American adults who use the internet also use Twitter, and more than half (54%) of these users access the platform on their mobile phones. The research highlights notable differences in Twitter adoption among different groups: 25% of Black adult internet users and 19% of Hispanic adults use Twitter, compared to just 9% of white adults. Additionally, urban and suburban residents are more likely to be Twitter users (15%), while only 7% of rural internet users are on the platform. Younger adults, particularly those aged 18–29, as well as men, tend to use Twitter more frequently. Education plays a role too—16% of college-educated adults use Twitter, as opposed to only 8% of those with just a high school diploma. Income, on the other hand, doesn’t appear to significantly influence Twitter use. Mobile accessibility has been central to Twitter since its inception. The familiar 140-character tweet limit was originally set to fit SMS text message constraints, meaning users could tweet from nearly any mobile phone. Today, Twitter supports multiple mobile entry points—including SMS, mobile browsers (even simple ones), dedicated smartphone and tablet apps, and email notifications. Reports from comScore and Nielsen show a surge in social media activity via mobile devices. Currently, social media is the fastest-growing mobile content area, with over half of smartphone users and more than a third of feature phone users accessing social networks through mobile apps. These trends indicate that mobile devices are quickly becoming the main way people use social media services like Twitter, prompting both creators and audiences to embrace a mobile-first approach.

Forskningen trekker frem betydelige forskjeller i Twitters popularitet blant ulike grupper: 25 % av svarte voksne internettbrukere og 19 % av latinamerikanske voksne er på Twitter, sammenlignet med bare 9 % av hvite voksne. Dessuten bruker flere i by- og forstadsområder Twitter (15 %), mens bare 7 % av internettbrukere på landsbygda benytter plattformen. Yngre voksne, særlig de mellom 18 og 29 år, samt menn, bruker Twitter mest. Utdanning har også betydning—16 % av voksne med høyere utdanning bruker Twitter, mot kun 8 % med kun videregående. Inntekt har derimot liten betydning for hvem som bruker Twitter. Mobiltilgang har vært essensielt for Twitter fra begynnelsen. Grensen på 140 tegn per tweet var opprinnelig satt for å passe SMS-meldinger, slik at nesten alle mobiltelefoner kunne brukes. Nå støttes flere mobile tilganger—inkludert SMS, enkle og avanserte mobilnettlesere, dedikerte apper for smarttelefon og nettbrett, og e-postvarsler. Rapporter fra comScore og Nielsen viser at bruk av sosiale medier på mobil øker kraftig. Sosiale medier er nå det raskest voksende innholdsområdet for mobilbrukere, og over halvparten av smarttelefonbrukere og mer enn en tredjedel av brukere av enkle mobiltelefoner er innom sosiale nettverk via apper. Samlet peker disse trendene på at mobiltelefoner raskt blir den viktigste måten å bruke sosiale medier på, noe som gjør at både innholdsskapere og brukere i økende grad tenker 'mobile first.'

A woman who had recently adopted a cat developed months of recurrent diarrhea, which doctors believe may have been caused by a bacterial infection transmitted from her new pet. According to a recent case report, both the woman and her cat tested positive for Clostridioides difficile (C. diff), a bacterium that causes gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhea and colitis. Fortunately, both recovered after receiving appropriate treatment. This case may be the first documented instance of potential cat-to-human transmission of C. diff.

C. diff is a common cause of gastrointestinal illness in the United States, with nearly half a million reported infections annually, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The bacterium is challenging to eliminate because it frequently recurs after initial treatment, particularly among vulnerable populations such as hospitalized and elderly patients. In 2017, there were approximately 223,900 C. diff cases among hospitalized patients and 12,800 associated deaths in the U.S.

A major risk factor for C. diff infection is disruption of the gut microbiome, often following use of broad-spectrum antibiotics. The patient, a previously healthy 31-year-old woman, developed severe diarrhea shortly after completing antibiotics for a urinary tract infection. She was diagnosed with C. diff and treated with another round of antibiotics, which seemed effective initially. However, her symptoms returned after two months, and subsequent antibiotic therapy provided less relief.

During a follow-up, the woman questioned whether her recently adopted cat, found as a stray before her illness began, might be related to her recurrent infection. Testing confirmed that her cat was asymptomatically carrying C. diff. Both the woman and her cat underwent treatment, and her symptoms resolved only after both were treated.

Doctors highlighted the timing of the cat's adoption, the woman's illness, and symptom resolution following treatment of both, suggesting a possible case of zoonotic (animal-to-human) transmission. However, the authors note that their evidence is circumstantial; it is also possible the woman initially contracted the infection elsewhere and then transmitted it to her cat, who subsequently reinfected her during further antibiotic treatments. Alternatively, the cat's infection might be unrelated.

Researchers stress the importance of considering pets as potential reservoirs for recurrent C. diff infection, encouraging additional study to determine if such transmissions are more common than previously recognized. Thorough patient histories and awareness of possible zoonotic transmission could help identify new sources of community-acquired C. diff, the authors conclude.

En kvinne som nylig hadde adoptert en katt, utviklet måneder med tilbakevendende diaré. Legene mener dette kan ha vært forårsaket av en bakteriell infeksjon overført fra hennes nye kjæledyr. Ifølge en nyere kasusrapport testet både kvinnen og katten positivt for Clostridioides difficile (C. diff), en bakterie som gir mageproblemer som diaré og kolitt. Heldigvis ble begge friske etter riktig behandling. Dette kan være det første dokumenterte tilfellet av mulig smitte fra katt til menneske av C. diff.

C. diff er en vanlig årsak til mageproblemer i USA, med nesten en halv million rapporterte tilfeller årlig, ifølge Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Bakterien er vanskelig å bli kvitt fordi infeksjonen ofte kommer tilbake etter behandling, spesielt blant sårbare grupper som sykehuspasienter og eldre. I 2017 var det omtrent 223 900 C. diff-tilfeller blant sykehuspasienter og 12 800 relaterte dødsfall i USA.

En viktig risikofaktor for C. diff-infeksjon er forstyrrelser i tarmens mikrobiom, ofte etter bruk av bredspektrede antibiotika. Pasienten, en tidligere frisk 31 år gammel kvinne, fikk alvorlig diaré kort tid etter avsluttet antibiotikabehandling for urinveisinfeksjon. Hun ble diagnostisert med C. diff og fikk en ny antibiotikakur, som først så ut til å fungere. Symptomer kom imidlertid tilbake etter to måneder, og videre antibiotikabehandling hadde mindre effekt.

Under en oppfølging spurte kvinnen om den nylig adopterte katten, som ble funnet som hjemløs før sykdomsutbruddet, kunne ha bidratt til infeksjonen. Prøver viste at katten, selv uten symptomer, bar på C. diff. Begge fikk behandling, og kvinnens symptomer forsvant etter at både hun og katten var blitt behandlet.

Legene påpekte tidsmessig sammenheng mellom kattens adopsjon, kvinnens sykdom og symptomfrihet etter behandling av begge, noe som kan tyde på mulig dyre-til-menneske-smitte (zoonose). Forfatterne understreker imidlertid at funnet kun bygger på omstendelige bevis. Det er også mulig at kvinnen først ble smittet et annet sted og deretter smittet katten, som så kan ha smittet henne tilbake under videre antibiotikabehandling. Alternativt kan kattens infeksjon være tilfeldig og ikke ha noen sammenheng.

Forskerne understreker viktigheten av å vurdere kjæledyr som mulige smittekilder ved gjentatte C. diff-infeksjoner og oppfordrer til videre forskning for å finne ut om dette er mer vanlig enn tidligere antatt. Nøye pasienthistorikk og bevissthet om zoonotisk smitte kan bidra til å avdekke nye kilder til samfunnservervet C. diff, konkluderer forfatterne.

article_content: The UK Department of Health has signaled its intention to halt NHS staff pay increases, prompting threats of industrial action from unions. Instead of implementing a 1% pay rise previously planned for staff, the department suggests redirecting the funds towards modernizing pay structures. In its latest submission to the pay review body, the Department of Health described the NHS as being under exceptional financial pressure, with increased demand and expectations to improve care for an ageing and growing population. The submission notes that, even after years of budget increases, the NHS must deliver greater value for taxpayers. Union leaders have criticized this proposal, arguing that even considering a pay freeze would damage staff morale. Rehana Azam of the GMB union pointed out that NHS staff are already frustrated by service and job cuts, which they feel put patient safety in jeopardy. She warned that further pay reductions, combined with government tax cuts elsewhere, could be the tipping point that triggers industrial action. Peter Carter, the general secretary of the Royal College of Nursing, stated that it is particularly demotivating for frontline staff to face another pay freeze after years of effective wage decreases, particularly when senior managers have received larger increases. Carter emphasized that the modest 1% pay rise is necessary, and disagreed with the government's implication that NHS staff receive pay increases simply for time served, clarifying that increments are based on gained experience and skills. Phil Gray, chief executive of the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy, also condemned the proposal, arguing it undermines partnership with NHS staff who have already endured a real-terms pay cut of up to 12% in recent years. The Department of Health defends its stance by stating that higher pay could reduce the number of staff NHS can employ, possibly affecting patient safety and service standards. As an alternative, it recommends reforms linking pay more closely to individual performance and productivity. Chancellor George Osborne announced in his spending review that public sector pay rises would be limited to an average of 1% for 2015/16. He also stated plans to remove automatic pay progression in the civil service and other sectors, describing current systems as outmoded and unfair. In its communication to pay review bodies, the Department of Health reiterated its view that modernizing pay frameworks is a priority. Reforms should focus on enhancing patient care by establishing a fairer connection between pay, performance, and productivity. These reforms are intended to ensure NHS contracts support improvements in efficiency and service quality and are financially sustainable, without granting automatic increases based only on years of employment. The government’s overarching aim is to put patient needs first by ensuring NHS staff are rewarded for their contributions, whilst updating pay systems to address current financial and operational pressures.
translated_content: Det britiske helsedepartementet har signalisert at de ønsker å stanse lønnsøkninger for NHS-ansatte, noe som har ført til streiketrusler fra fagforeninger. I stedet for å gi en planlagt lønnsøkning på 1 %, foreslår departementet å bruke midlene på å modernisere lønnsstrukturene. I sin siste innstilling til lønnsutvalget beskriver helsedepartementet NHS som under stort økonomisk press, med økende etterspørsel og behov for å forbedre omsorgen for en aldrende og voksende befolkning. De påpeker at til tross for flere år med budsjettøkning, må NHS levere større verdi for skattebetalerne. Fagforeningsledere har kritisert forslaget og mener at selv tanken på lønnsfrys undergraver moralen til de ansatte. Rehana Azam fra GMB påpekte at NHS-ansatte allerede er frustrerte over kutt i tjenester og stillinger, noe de mener kan gå ut over pasientsikkerheten. Hun advarte om at ytterligere lønnskutt sammen med skattekutt for andre kan føre til krav om streik. Peter Carter, generalsekretær i Royal College of Nursing, uttalte at enda en lønnsfrys etter år med reelle lønnskutt er spesielt demotiverende for ansatte på gulvet, særlig når ledere har fått større økninger. Carter understreket at en beskjeden lønnsvekst på 1 % er nødvendig, og var uenig i regjeringens antydning om at lønnsøkning gis kun basert på ansiennitet. Han presiserte at lønnsopprykk gis basert på erfaring og økt kompetanse. Phil Gray, leder i Chartered Society of Physiotherapy, fordømte også forslaget og mente det svekker samarbeidet med NHS-ansatte, som allerede har opplevd lønnskutt på opptil 12 % de siste årene. Helsedepartementet hevder på sin side at høyere lønn kan bety færre ansatte NHS har råd til å ansette, noe som kan påvirke pasientsikkerheten og kvaliteten på tjenestene. Som alternativ foreslår de å knytte lønn tettere opp til prestasjon og produktivitet. Finansminister George Osborne meldte i budsjettgjennomgangen at lønnsøkninger i offentlig sektor i 2015/16 skal begrenses til i snitt 1 %. Han varslet også plan om å fjerne automatiske lønnsopprykk i staten og andre sektorer, og beskrev dagens system som foreldet og urettferdig. I dialog med lønnsutvalgene slo helsedepartementet fast at modernisering av lønnssystemene bør ha høyeste prioritet. Reformene skal bidra til å forbedre pasienttilbudet ved å koble lønn tettere til innsats og resultater. Målet med disse reformene er at NHS-kontrakter skal fremme effektivitet og kvalitet, og være økonomisk bærekraftige – uten at lønnsoppgang gis automatisk etter arbeidsår. Regjeringens hovedmål er å sette pasienten først, ved å belønne NHS-ansatte for innsatsen sin, og modernisere lønnssystemet slik at det holder tritt med økonomiske og organisatoriske utfordringer i helsevesenet.
