Cricketikonet Sachin Tendulkar gratulerte det australske laget med deres imponerende prestasjon og delte oppmuntrende ord med det indiske laget. Tendulkar bemerket at Australia spilte best på den avgjørende dagen, men roste også Indias innsats gjennom hele turneringen. Han uttrykte medfølelse med skuffelsen både hos spillerne og supporterne, og påpekte at tilbakeslag er en del av sporten. Han anerkjente lagets helhjertede innsats. Tidligere India-åpner Virender Sehwag sendte også sine gratulasjoner til Australia, og fremhevet spesielt Travis Heads comeback etter skade for å spille en avgjørende rolle i finalen. Sehwag roste Australias valg om å beholde Head på laget og hyllet de minneverdige øyeblikkene India ga fansen i løpet av VM, selv om det ikke holdt hele veien. Jay Shah, sekretær i Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), skrøt av det indiske lagets utholdenhet og vilje, og uttalte at deres VM-reise var en inspirasjon for hele nasjonen. Han trakk frem lagets ubeseirede rekke frem til finalen og den enorme støtten fra indiske fans. Shah takket hver spiller for deres innsats, og understreket at lagets lidenskap og utholdenhet gjorde landet stolt. I finalen fikk India 240 løp på 50 overs. Australia, som kom dårlig ut med 47/3, tok til slutt seieren med seks wicket etter en fantastisk 137 fra Travis Head og solide 58 fra Marnus Labuschagne.

article_content: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has highlighted the critical need for Nigeria to expand the use of electric vehicles to help curb air pollution and support a cleaner transportation system. Inspecting new solar-powered EV charging stations in Abuja, Shettima noted that these advancements align with preparations for the upcoming COP28 United Nations climate summit in Dubai. Shettima stated that adopting e-mobility directly supports Nigeria's Energy Transition Plan (ETP), which focuses on reducing greenhouse gas emissions from the transportation sector—currently responsible for 28.4% of the country's total emissions. The ETP, supported by groups like Sustainable Energy for All and the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet, advocates for upgrading to low-emission transport options. To achieve this, the Nigerian government is encouraging increased domestic production of electric vehicles, building more charging stations, and inviting greater participation from private companies. He emphasized that these steps reflect Nigeria’s willingness to embrace sustainable energy solutions, demonstrating a leadership role for Africa in energy transition. Shettima also stressed how closer cooperation between the public and private sectors is vital for improving national infrastructure, which underpins President Bola Tinubu’s 'Renewed Hope Agenda.' At a recent launch event for books by Nigerian lawyers Yusuf Ali and M. T. Adekilekun, he praised President Tinubu’s proven expertise with public-private partnerships, referencing Tinubu’s prior achievements in Lagos State as examples of transformative leadership for Nigeria’s future.
translated_content: Visepresident Kashim Shettima har fremhevet hvor viktig det er for Nigeria å øke bruken av elektriske kjøretøy for å redusere luftforurensning og bidra til et renere transportsystem. Under inspeksjonen av nye solcelledrevne ladestasjoner for elbiler i Abuja påpekte Shettima at disse tiltakene inngår i forberedelsene til det kommende COP28 FN-klimatoppmøtet i Dubai. Shettima uttalte at satsingen på elbiler støtter Nigerias Energy Transition Plan (ETP), som har som mål å redusere klimagassutslipp fra transportsektoren—nå ansvarlig for 28,4 % av landets totale utslipp. ETP, støttet av aktører som Sustainable Energy for All og Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet, fremmer overgang til lavutslippsløsninger i transport. For å oppnå dette jobber Nigerias regjering for økt produksjon av elbiler i landet, utbygging av ladeinfrastruktur og større deltakelse fra privat sektor. Han fremhevet at disse tiltakene reflekterer Nigerias vilje til å satse på bærekraftige energiløsninger og vise lederskap i Afrikas energiomstilling. Shettima understreket også hvor viktig det er med tettere samarbeid mellom offentlig og privat sektor for å styrke nasjonal infrastruktur, som er kjernen i president Bola Tinubus 'Renewed Hope Agenda.' Ved en boklansering i Abuja for forfatterne og advokatene Yusuf Ali og M. T. Adekilekun, berømmet han president Tinubus solide erfaring med offentlig–privat partnerskap, og viste til hans resultater i Lagos State som eksempler på lederskap som kan forme Nigerias framtid.

article_content: Players from the Pittsburgh Penguins and Anaheim Ducks honored former Penguin Adam Johnson on Monday after he died during a game in England. The Penguins are making neck guards mandatory for players at the minor-league level and plan to urge NHL players to wear them as well. Johnson, a 29-year-old forward, died Saturday while playing for the Nottingham Panthers in England. According to the team, a 'freak accident' occurred when another player's skate cut his neck. Adam Johnson played three years with the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins in the AHL and appeared in more than a dozen NHL games for the Pittsburgh Penguins. The Penguins are requiring neck protection for players in their lower-level affiliates, the AHL and the ECHL, and are strongly encouraging NHL players to use neck guards. Coach Mike Sullivan said the organization is discussing additional protective equipment, especially for vulnerable areas like the neck and wrists, and hopes the NHL will explore new safety options. NHL mandates on gear require approval from the NHL Players' Association, and the league did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Interest in cut-resistant neck guards has surged since Johnson's death. Warroad Hockey, a company co-founded by Washington Capitals forward T.J. Oshie, reported selling out of neck and wrist protectors due to increased demand. Both Oshie and Johnson are from Minnesota. Warroad introduced its neck gear just a month before the accident. Oshie told Minneapolis TV station KARE that 'one death is one too many,' referencing Teddy Balkind, a 16-year-old who died last year in Connecticut after a neck injury during a high school game. The NHL has a history of serious neck injuries, including incidents involving Clint Malarchuk (Buffalo Sabres, 1989), Richard Zednik (Florida Panthers, 2008), and Adam Burish (Chicago Blackhawks, 2009). Despite increased awareness, many believe adoption of neck guards at the NHL level will be slow, citing resistance to change, mobility concerns, and supply issues. Oshie himself has not worn his company's neck guard in games but plans to try it at practice. The English Ice Hockey Association (EIHA) announced that neck guards will become mandatory for all players starting January 1, 2024. Until then, it strongly recommends their use, though the EIHA does not govern the Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL), where Johnson played. The delay is attributed to anticipated supply shortages. USA Hockey recommends all players wear neck guards but notes there is limited data on their effectiveness in preventing neck lacerations. Research has shown that 27% of players who sustained a neck laceration were wearing a guard at the time. While catastrophic injuries can occur, most neck cuts are not life-threatening. A 2015 academic study tested 14 different neck protectors and found a wide range of effectiveness against skate cuts.

Having a mentor can significantly boost your career. Whether you want to advance professionally, develop new skills, or simply seek guidance, finding a mentor is invaluable—especially for college students or recent graduates. Yet, many people are unsure how to approach potential mentors or are reluctant to seek help. In today’s competitive job market, every advantage matters. Research from Gallup and Amazon indicates that those with mentors are more likely to have fulfilling, credible, and well-compensated careers.

What Does a Mentor Do?
A mentor is someone who offers advice and guidance on multiple aspects of your career. An ideal mentor can help you with networking, job searches, career decisions, and strategies for building relationships and credibility. It’s common to approach different people for various types of advice—for example, a friend’s parent may provide job leads, while a former boss or professor can coach you on workplace interactions.

Mentorship benefits individuals regardless of their field. Whether you’re entering STEM, education, or any other sector, connecting with someone who is ahead in the field can provide invaluable perspective. For example, an engineer can share how they got started, and a principal can advise a new teacher about what makes a great educator.

How to Find a Mentor
Consider your network as concentric circles—the closest people to you at the center, and acquaintances, or even strangers, on the outside. Begin by reaching out to people you know, and ask for introductions if needed. Activities like job shadowing (59% have benefited), internships (43%), and even meeting visiting experts at your school (30%) are proven ways to connect with mentors.

The most crucial step is making the ask. Many are hesitant, but most potential mentors are glad to help and often feel honored by the request. While a one-time meeting—such as coffee—can be useful, ongoing interactions are more valuable for building rapport and consistent support. When reaching out, explain why you’re interested in their guidance and what you hope to gain.

Maximizing the Mentorship
To get the most from your mentor, take the initiative: set up meetings, come prepared with updates and questions, and be intentional. Ask not only about your mentor’s successes, but also about challenges and lessons learned. According to the Gallup-Amazon poll, mentees especially value mentors who share real-life examples (48%), practical warnings (43%), and guidance about career paths (49%).

Who Makes a Great Mentor?
Seek mentors whom you trust, respect, and feel comfortable discussing your goals with. The best mentors balance knowledge (77%), humility (66%), encouragement (65%), belonging (61%), empathy (49%), and realistic career success (68%). Many people—90% by race, 77% by gender—find mentors with whom they share similar backgrounds or identities.

Expressing Gratitude
Always thank your mentor for their time and support. Expressing appreciation not only strengthens the relationship but also encourages their continued investment in your growth.

Conclusion
Reaching out for mentorship can provide enormous advantages. Interestingly, being vulnerable in seeking help can actually increase your confidence. The benefits are not only in the advice received but also in developing a strong, trusting relationship with someone experienced in your chosen field.

article_content: Although the Ryder Cup is still a year away, psychological tactics have already begun. At a press conference at Gleneagles in Scotland, the venue for next year’s biennial golf contest, U.S. captain Tom Watson playfully challenged his European counterpart, Paul McGinley. Watson suggested changing the team selection process by removing the captain’s discretionary picks. Currently, most players qualify through prize money earned on their respective tours, with captains selecting a few additional golfers. 'In my first three Ryder Cups everyone had to qualify,' said Watson, an eight-time major winner. 'Maybe that's the way it should go back to. I reduced my picks from four to three this year, and even considered two. Maybe we should go back to no picks at all. What do you think?' Watson asked McGinley in front of the assembled journalists. The question was light-hearted but strategic, as many believe that removing captain's picks would favor the U.S., since numerous European players now play on the American tour. McGinley responded, 'That would be tricky for us with so many of our players on the U.S. tour. Question deferred.' The exchange showcased the respect and sportsmanship both captains wish to bring to golf’s most prestigious team event. 'We know this is a partisan event—we’re on away turf and Europe is the favorite. But Paul and I agree that the tournament’s conduct is crucial,' Watson said. 'There’s always an edge, but how we handle it is important.' He added: 'Respect is essential. When you lose, you respect the winners. When you win, you respect the losers.' Neither captain wants to be labeled the favorite, but the statistics favor Europe. They have won five of the last six Ryder Cups, including the 2012 'Miracle in Medinah,' where the U.S. led 10-6 but Europe ultimately won 14.5–13.5 on the final day. 'The bookmakers say we’re favorites,' McGinley admitted. 'But the difference is small. We’ll have to play incredibly well. The U.S. team under Tom Watson will be very strong. It’s a heavyweight contest.' Watson, meanwhile, acknowledged the challenge: 'We’ve lost seven out of the last nine Ryder Cups. We’re playing away from home, and traditionally the home team has the advantage.' Watson’s history as captain and success in the UK may play a role. He led the U.S. to their last away victory at the Belfry in England in 1993 and has claimed five British Open titles. 'I’m very grateful for the chance to be captain in Scotland, a place special to my career. It’s hard to believe it was nearly 20 years ago that I experienced the thrill of being a captain in 1993.'

A recent Pew Research Center study has highlighted Europeans' views on each other, set against the backdrop of the continent’s economic difficulties. Residents in eight EU countries—Britain, the Czech Republic, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Poland, and Spain—shared opinions on trust, compassion, and arrogance among their neighbors.

Germany generally emerged as the most trustworthy nation, except for Greeks, who trust their own people most and see Germans as least trustworthy, most arrogant, and least compassionate. These attitudes mirror broader resentment towards Germany’s role in enforcing austerity policies during the euro crisis.

Six of the eight nations considered Germany the least compassionate, but the British were selected in this category by the French and Germans. The British, for their part, thought the French were least trustworthy and Germans least compassionate. The French, Germans, and Czechs ranked Greeks as least trustworthy, while Italians had the lowest trust in their own country, likely influenced by frustration over corruption.

On the arrogance scale, the French see themselves as both most and least arrogant, while the British and Germans choose France and other countries largely name Germany. Yet, a majority in each nation liked to think of themselves as least arrogant and most compassionate, indicating national self-favoritism.

In southern Europe, especially Spain, Italy, and Greece, deep pessimism prevails: over 70% of respondents in Spain and Greece, and many Italians, call the economic situation very bad. Unemployment dominates concerns, with over 90% in those countries seeing it as a serious issue. By contrast, German respondents are less concerned. This north-south division is reflected in attitudes toward the wider EU, with countries like Spain, Italy, and Greece growing more disillusioned and feeling increasingly disconnected from Brussels and Berlin. French attitudes, too, are becoming more critical, moving closer to the perspective of southern Europe than to Germany’s more optimistic outlook.

Against this tense political and social landscape, the Eurovision Song Contest stands as both entertainment and a symbol of European rivalry. With 39 countries participating and more than 100 million viewers, the 2013 contest is hosted in Malmo, Sweden. Eurovision is famous for its extravagant performances and playful nationalism, but voting is often suspected to follow regional alliances rather than pure musical talent. While the contest may provide temporary escapism, it also serves as a stage for Europe’s ongoing negotiation of national identities and relations.

article_content: Satellite images taken during the Cold War have revealed nearly 400 previously unknown Roman forts in Iraq and Syria, according to archaeologists. The research, published in Antiquity, an academic archaeology journal, is leading historians and archaeologists to rethink their understanding of Rome’s eastern frontier from 1,900 years ago. Antoine Poidebard, a French Jesuit priest who pioneered aerial archaeology in the 1920s, previously mapped 116 Roman forts along a 1,000 km (approximately 620-mile) border, suggesting they formed a defensive line against Arab and Persian invaders due to their spacing. However, the new research has identified an additional 396 forts, indicating the region may have been more of a hub for global trade rather than solely a defensive barrier. The findings suggest the forts were likely used to support the movement of people, goods, and military assets between east and west, according to lead author Jesse Casana, a professor of anthropology at Dartmouth College. Casana's team is now asking whether this historical border was 'a wall or a road.' Previously, these forts were thought to form a north-south defensive border, but the newly discovered sites reveal an east-west line connecting the Tigris River to the Mediterranean, Casana explained. The research utilized declassified spy satellite images from the CORONA and HEXAGON programs. CORONA, launched in the late 1950s, was designed to capture images of the Earth’s surface for intelligence purposes and became a significant source of information about Soviet military activities, according to the CIA. The HEXAGON program, which operated from 1971 to 1986, involved the largest U.S. intelligence satellites and returned photographic film to Earth, capturing 877 million square miles of the planet’s surface, according to the National Museum of the United States Air Force. Analysts used these images to identify potential threats. Casana noted that the next steps should include expanding this type of research to other regions and utilizing additional types of imagery.

Den nye forskningen har imidlertid identifisert ytterligere 396 fort, noe som tilsier at regionen kanskje var et knutepunkt for global handel, ikke bare et forsvarsverk. Funnene antyder at fortene sannsynligvis ble brukt til å støtte bevegelse av mennesker, varer og militære enheter mellom øst og vest, ifølge hovedforfatter Jesse Casana, professor i antropologi ved Dartmouth College. In July, 17-year-old Rifqa Bary left her Columbus, Ohio home asserting that her family threatened her after she converted from Islam to Christianity. She sought safety in Orlando, Florida, with Pastor Blake Lorenz of the Global Revolution Church, and was placed into foster care while legal proceedings took place.

At a recent hearing, Judge Daniel Dawson ruled that Rifqa and her parents, Mohamed and Aysha Bary, must enter mediation within 30 days to try to resolve their dispute. The Barys, unable to attend in person, participated by phone with their lawyer representing them, adamantly denied ever threatening Rifqa or objecting to her practicing Christianity, although they expressed a preference that she stayed within the Muslim faith.

Rifqa alleges in a sworn affidavit that her father faced pressure from the family’s mosque to address her conversion, and she claims he told her, "If you have Jesus in your heart, you are dead to me! I will kill you!" Her parents, for their part, reported her missing to local police and argue that the situation has been exaggerated by misinformation.

The court-appointed guardian emphasized that the case centers on family strife rather than religious conflict. Judge Dawson also sealed a law enforcement report and issued a gag order on attorneys. The case has drawn impassioned responses from both Muslim and Christian advocates, with disputes occurring outside the courtroom.

Another hearing is planned for September 29 if mediation does not bring a resolution.

Under en nylig høring bestemte dommer Daniel Dawson at Rifqa og foreldrene Mohamed og Aysha Bary skal gjennomføre mekling innen 30 dager for å prøve å løse konflikten. Foreldrene, som ikke kunne møte fysisk, deltok via telefon, med advokat til stede. De benekter bestemt å ha truet Rifqa eller motarbeidet hennes valg om å praktisere kristendom, selv om de helst skulle sett at hun forble muslim.

Rifqa hevder i en edsvoren erklæring at faren hennes ble presset av moskeen familien tilhører til å «ta affære», og hun påstår at han sa: «Hvis du har Jesus i hjertet, er du død for meg! Jeg dreper deg!» Foreldrene meldte henne savnet til politiet og mener at saken har blitt overdrevet på grunn av feilinformasjon.

article_content: An early morning townhouse fire on Monday claimed the life of 8-year-old Jayden Isme, while his brother, 9-year-old Justin Isme, made a daring escape by jumping from a second-story bedroom window. According to police, Jayden died at the scene due to the intensity of the fire, which forced firefighters to withdraw for their own safety. After escaping, Justin ran to a neighbor’s home to call 911. He sustained minor injuries and is expected to recover. The boys’ father, Wisler Toto Isme, was seen speaking with authorities shortly after the blaze. Lauderhill Police spokesperson Lt. Michael Butkus confirmed that the children were left home alone. 'There is definitely a possibility of criminal charges, but we will wait until the investigation is complete,' said Butkus. Neighbors described Jayden and Justin as energetic, inseparable, and passionate about sports. Michael Florent, a neighbor, said, 'When you saw one, you saw the other.' Another resident, Sally Williams, expressed her sorrow after witnessing Justin escaping the fire, believing his brother was right behind him. Justin tried to save Jayden but was unable to get him out. He was treated at Plantation General Hospital. Due to the severity of the fire, authorities could not retrieve Jayden’s body for several hours. The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Lt. Butkus stated, 'There’s nothing indicating any malicious activity. It appears to have been a tragic accident.'

Ifølge politiet døde Jayden på stedet på grunn av den intense brannen, som tvang brannmannskapene til å trekke seg tilbake for sin egen sikkerhet. Etter å ha kommet seg ut, løp Justin til en nabo for å ringe 911. Han fikk lettere skader og forventes å bli helt frisk. Guttenes far, Wisler Toto Isme, ble observert mens han snakket med myndighetene kort tid etter brannen. Talsmann for Lauderhill-politiet, løytnant Michael Butkus, bekreftet at barna var hjemme alene. 'Det er definitivt en mulighet for strafferettslige anklager, men vi vil vente til etterforskningen er ferdig,' sa Butkus. Naboer beskrev Jayden og Justin som energiske, uatskillelige og sportsinteresserte. Naboen Michael Florent sa: 'Når du så den ene, så du alltid den andre.' En annen beboer, Sally Williams, uttrykte sin sorg etter å ha sett Justin flykte fra brannen og trodde broren hans var rett bak ham. Justin forsøkte å redde Jayden, men klarte det ikke. Han ble behandlet på Plantation General Hospital. På grunn av brannens styrke kunne myndighetene ikke hente ut Jayden før etter flere timer. Brannårsaken etterforskes fortsatt. article_content: Humans have long relied on natural substances to enhance flavors, boost energy, manage pain, or shift perspectives. From caffeine in our morning coffee to the fiery kick of chili peppers, and from ancient painkillers like morphine to modern interest in psychedelics such as psilocybin, these chemicals are woven into our daily lives. Today, researchers are taking a closer look at their potential, especially for treating mental health conditions. But why do plants, fungi, microbes, and even animals produce such powerful compounds? Most of these chemicals originated as tools for survival and defense, not for human benefit. As someone who studies the evolutionary battles between plants and their attackers, I see these substances as part of nature’s ongoing arms race. For example, bacteria produce botulinum toxin to defend against threats—a substance now used as Botox. Bread mold invented penicillin to outcompete other microbes; humans made it an antibiotic. Plants use caffeine or Taxol (from yew trees) to ward off pests, but we use them as a daily stimulant or a cancer drug. Venom from cone snails, designed for paralyzing fish, is now a potent painkiller. While these seem perfect for human needs, they were originally evolutionary weapons or shields. My own family illustrates their double edge: my father died from alcohol dependency, a result of consuming ethanol—a yeast-made toxin created to outcompete microbial rivals. This example shows how nature’s chemistry can save or destroy. Animals join the chemistry battle, too. Monarch butterfly caterpillars eat milkweed, absorbing toxins that protect the adult butterflies from predators. Through genetic research, we've learned how they've adapted to resist these poisons. Even the foxglove plant’s toxins—dangerous in nature—became some of our earliest heart medications. Interest in psychedelics is rising again, both in science and society. Compounds like psilocybin, DMT, 5-Meo-DMT, mescaline, and ergot alkaloids show promise against hard-to-treat mental health issues. Indigenous communities have long used these substances for ceremony and healing, but the modern West is just now catching up through clinical studies. While early results are hopeful, careful research remains vital. Crucially, these chemicals evolved for reasons unrelated to humans. They're often so bitter that animals steer clear, acting as natural deterrents. In some grasses and fungi, such substances protect the plant or mushroom from herbivores or microbes. For instance, damage turns some mushrooms blue due to defensive chemical reactions that likely deter or disrupt would-be eaters. Nature’s arsenal is full of remedies and hazards. Medicines like Taxol work by blocking cell growth — helpful against cancer but harmful to hair follicles. The belief that natural means safe is misleading; these compounds are a legacy of nature’s struggles. Diligent research into their origins and effects is the only way to harness their benefits while avoiding unwanted harm. As our society renews its relationship with these chemicals, we must remember their power comes from the fight for survival—a fact both humbling and sobering.
translated_content: Mennesker har lenge vært avhengige av naturlige stoffer for å forbedre smak, gi energi, lindre smerte eller endre perspektiv. Fra koffein i morgenkaffen til den sterke smaken fra chilipepper, og fra gamle smertestillende midler som morfin til dagens interesse for psykedelika som psilocybin, er disse kjemikaliene en del av hverdagen vår. I dag undersøker forskere potensialet deres, spesielt for behandling av psykiske lidelser. Men hvorfor produserer planter, sopp, mikrober og til og med dyr så kraftige forbindelser? De fleste av disse kjemikaliene oppstod som verktøy for overlevelse og forsvar, ikke for mennesker. Som forsker på den evolusjonære kampen mellom planter og angripere, ser jeg disse stoffene som en del av naturens pågående våpenkappløp. For eksempel produserer bakterier botulinumtoksin for å beskytte seg mot trusler—et stoff vi nå kjenner som Botox. Brødmugg oppdaget penicillin for å overvinne andre mikrober; mennesker gjorde det til et antibiotikum. Planter bruker koffein eller Taxol (fra barlind) for å holde skadedyr unna, men vi bruker dem som stimulerende middel eller kreftmedisin. Gift fra kjeglesnegler, laget for å lamme fisk, har blitt et effektivt smertestillende middel. Selv om disse stoffene virker tilpasset menneskers behov, var de i utgangspunktet evolusjonære våpen eller skjold. Min familie illustrerer denne dobbeltsidigheten: Min far døde av alkoholavhengighet, som følge av etanol—et stoff produsert av gjær for å bekjempe mikrober. Dette viser hvordan naturens kjemi kan både redde og skade. Dyr deltar også i dette kjemikappløpet. Monarksommerfugl-larver spiser melkefrø, tar opp giftstoffer og blir som voksne beskyttet mot rovdyr. Gjennom genetisk forskning har vi lært hvordan de har utviklet toleranse for disse giftene. Selv giftige stoffer fra revebjelle, som er farlige i naturen, har blitt brukt som tidlige medisiner mot hjerteproblemer. Interessen for psykedelika øker både i forskning og samfunn. Stoffer som psilocybin, DMT, 5-Meo-DMT, meskalin og ergotalkaloider viser lovende resultater mot tunge psykiske lidelser. Urfolk har lenge brukt disse stoffene i seremonier og til helbredelse, men nå tar vestlige samfunn dem opp via kliniske studier. Selv om tidlige funn er positive, er grundig forskning avgjørende. Det er viktig å forstå at disse stoffene utviklet seg uavhengig av menneskers behov. De er ofte så bitre at dyr styrer unna, en naturlig beskyttelse. Noen gressarter og sopper bruker slike forbindelser som beskyttelse mot beitedyr eller mikrober. Noen sopper blir blå når de skades, trolig for å avskrekke angripere. Naturens arsenal gir både medisin og fare. Medisiner som Taxol stopper celledeling—bra mot kreft, men kan også føre til hårtap. Å tenke at naturlig betyr trygt, er en misforståelse—disse stoffene er en arv fra naturens kamp. Bare grundig forskning på opprinnelse og effekt kan hjelpe oss å dra nytte av fordelene og unngå skade. Når samfunnet nå fornyer forholdet til slike stoffer, må vi huske at deres kraft stammer fra kampen for å overleve—et faktum som bør gi både ydmykhet og ettertanke.

article_content: Laolu Akande, a former presidential aide, described the ongoing nationwide strike by labour unions as a distraction and called on President Bola Tinubu to intervene. Akande emphasized that Nigeria is facing more pressing challenges, including widespread hardship among citizens and a fiscal crisis affecting the Federal Government. Speaking on Channels Television’s 'Politics Today' on Tuesday, Akande urged the President to address the multiple national problems, which he said are being made worse by the strike initiated by the National Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress (TUC). Akande stated: 'Mr. President has said that the buck stops at his desk, so we need to urge him, Mr. President, fix this! We don’t need this distraction. The people are suffering; the last thing they need is a nationwide strike. I believe this can be resolved quickly, and I do not see this as an insurmountable issue.' When asked if the strike was politically motivated, he responded: 'That is why we have elected political leaders—to solve political problems. Labour does have responsibilities, but is it right to bring the entire nation to a standstill over a local issue in Imo State? Wouldn’t it have been better to localize this matter?' Akande further stated that resolving the issue should be possible with dialogue: 'For the government, from the President down, this is something that could be settled with a single phone call. Reaching out to labour leaders should expedite a solution. We don’t need more delays; the President needs to address and resolve this swiftly.' He strongly condemned the alleged inhumane treatment of NLC President Joe Ajaero in Imo State, calling it criminal. Akande praised Inspector-General of Police Olukayode Egbetokun for promising a quick investigation into the assault. Akande added: 'What happened to Mr. Joe Ajaero in Imo State is criminal. Assaulting anyone is a crime. We must be clear that such actions are unacceptable.' On the best approach for labour leaders, Akande suggested: 'From what I have gathered, this is essentially a local issue. Even Governor Hope Uzodinma of Imo State described it as a local political matter. There are allegations that Mr. Ajaero is partial to the Labour Party, so it might be better to address this issue within Imo rather than make it a national one.'

I tirsdagens TV-program 'Politics Today' på Channels Television, oppfordret Akande presidenten til å håndtere de mange nasjonale problemene, som han mener blir forverret av streiken fra National Labour Congress (NLC) og Trade Union Congress (TUC). Akande sa: 'Presidenten har sagt at ansvaret til slutt hviler på ham, så vi må oppfordre: President, ordn opp! Vi trenger ikke denne avsporingen. Folk lider; det siste de trenger er en landsomfattende streik. Jeg tror dette kan løses raskt, og jeg ser ikke dette som et uløselig problem.' På spørsmål om streiken er politisk motivert, svarte han: 'Derfor har vi folkevalgte ledere – for å løse politiske problemer. Fagforeningene har ansvar, men er det riktig å lamme hele landet for en lokal sak i Imo State? Hadde det ikke vært bedre å løse det lokalt?' Akande understreket videre at dette kunne vært løst i dialog: 'For regjeringen, fra presidenten og nedover, kunne dette vært avklart med en enkelt telefonsamtale. Å kontakte fagforeningslederne burde få fart på en løsning. Vi trenger ingen flere forsinkelser – presidenten må ta tak i dette og løse det raskt.' Han fordømte sterkt den angivelig umenneskelige behandlingen av NLC-president Joe Ajaero i Imo State og beskrev den som kriminell. Å angripe noen er en forbrytelse. Vi må være tydelige på at slike handlinger ikke er akseptable.' Det er påstander om at Ajaero er partisk overfor Labour Party, så det kunne vært bedre å håndtere dette i Imo i stedet for å gjøre det til en nasjonal sak.'

article_content: Google has introduced the 'Chromebook Plus' certification to guide consumers toward high-quality Chromebooks, eliminating the need for technical know-how. Modeled after Intel’s Evo certification for Windows PCs, this new label identifies Chromebooks that meet tough performance standards. While battery life is not emphasized—since all Chromebooks are expected to offer at least 10 hours according to Google's tests—eligible devices must pass other strict benchmarks. In addition to superior hardware, Chromebook Plus devices offer AI-enhanced features, including Google Photos' magic eraser, improved video conferencing, AI-generated wallpapers, and a built-in writing assistant. Purchasers also get three months of free access to Photoshop on the Web and GeForce Now's priority tier. Brands such as Lenovo, HP, and Acer are early adopters of the certification. Shoppers in the U.S. can order Chromebook Plus laptops from October 8, 2023, through retailers like Best Buy, Amazon, Walmart, and Target. Availability in Canada and Europe starts October 9.

Inspirert av Intels Evo-sertifisering for Windows-PC-er, markerer denne etiketten Chromebooks som møter strenge ytelseskrav. Batteritid er ikke fremhevet—alle Chromebooks skal likevel ha minst 10 timers batterilevetid ifølge Googles tester—men enhetene må oppfylle andre høye standarder. Utover bedre maskinvare har Chromebook Plus-modellene AI-drevne funksjoner som magisk viskelær i Google Photos, forbedret videokonferanse, AI-valgte bakgrunnsbilder og en integrert skriveassistent. Kjøpere får også tre måneder gratis tilgang til Photoshop på nettet og GeForce Now-prioritet. Lenovo, HP og Acer er blant de første til å ta i bruk sertifiseringen. Amerikanske kunder kan bestille Chromebook Plus-bærbare fra 8. oktober 2023 hos Best Buy, Amazon, Walmart og Target, mens tilgjengeligheten starter 9. oktober i Canada og Europa.

article_content: Paris, France – The future of social networking, the real-time web, and a range of new apps and devices were major topics at the annual Le Web conference, which opened Wednesday. Twitter's remarkable rise and future roadmap dominated the first sessions, which brought together bloggers and industry leaders in a converted morgue on the city's northeastern edge. Executives from Twitter, Facebook, and MySpace presented technical innovations to attract more users. Following Twitter founder Jack Dorsey’s unveiling of Square, a device that allows credit card payments via mobile phones, Twitter platform director Ryan Sarver announced that more than 50,000 apps now utilize the company’s stream of blog updates. Sarver also introduced Twitter’s “firehose” feature, providing developers with unrestricted access to its data stream—a first for the platform, which has not yet announced significant revenue sources, even as others profit from its data. Ethan Beard, a developer at Facebook, promoted the site’s 500,000 apps and the traffic-boosting power of Facebook Connect, which now boasts 60 million users. Meanwhile, Mike Jones, Chief Operating Officer at MySpace, announced the addition of real-time status updates—similar to Twitter and Facebook—to its platform, and greater developer access, backed by a $50,000 innovation prize. Jones did not address rumors of a possible MySpace and Facebook partnership. The executives declined to discuss site revenues or ongoing speculation about IPOs. YouTube co-founder Chad Hurley, whose company is owned by Google, also withheld revenue figures but noted that some creators had earned over $1 million since advertising was introduced to the platform. Hurley said, 'We didn’t introduce advertising right away because we didn’t want to change why people uploaded videos. We aimed to build a video community.' He added, 'Over time, we realized advertising could provide secure revenue without changing who we are, and it has worked well.' Hurley emphasized there is no formula for viral success. 'You could punch me in the face and get a lot of views,' he joked. 'Shocking content often gets attention, but there’s no magic recipe. The key is that everyone can participate.' Offstage, much discussion centered on the competition between Facebook and Twitter, and the trend of opening data to app developers. Attendees also debated the unpredictable nature of internet success. Katrin Weber of Deutsche Telekom observed, 'It’s interesting how everyone is announcing awards and conferences now, but what’s next? Who will ultimately win? People are looking for the formula for success—why do some apps and platforms make it while others don’t?' Social media marketing agent Vero Pepperrell commented, 'I’m glad Twitter recognizes how much of an ecosystem it has with its developers—they’re moving in the right direction.' Blogger Gabriel Jorby said that Square, Dorsey’s credit card device, signals a trend toward combining online and physical experiences. 'If you want to provide a service, you need something that connects to the real world. You can’t just rely on an online app; it has to be something tangible. That’s the future—it’s not just about what’s on screen.' Over 2,000 participants from 46 countries were expected at Le Web, making it one of Europe’s largest tech gatherings.
translated_content: Paris, Frankrike – Fremtiden for sosiale nettverk, sanntidswebben og en rekke nye apper og enheter var hovedtemaene på den årlige Le Web-konferansen, som åpnet onsdag. Twitters bemerkelsesverdige vekst og fremtidsplaner preget de første sesjonene, hvor bloggere og bransjeledere samlet seg i et ombygd likhus i den nordøstlige delen av byen. Ledere fra Twitter, Facebook og MySpace presenterte tekniske nyvinninger for å tiltrekke seg flere brukere. Etter at Twitter-grunnlegger Jack Dorsey lanserte Square, en enhet som lar deg ta betalt med kredittkort via mobiltelefon, kunngjorde Twitters plattformdirektør Ryan Sarver at over 50 000 apper nå bruker selskapets strøm av bloggoppdateringer. Sarver introduserte også Twitters «firehose»-funksjon, som gir utviklere ubegrenset tilgang til datastrømmen—en nyhet for plattformen, som ennå ikke har kunngjort vesentlige inntektskilder, selv om andre tjener penger på dataene. Ethan Beard, utvikler hos Facebook, fremhevet nettstedets 500 000 apper og trafikkøkningen fra Facebook Connect, som nå har 60 millioner brukere. Samtidig kunngjorde Mike Jones, Chief Operating Officer i MySpace, at plattformen får statusoppdateringer i sanntid—likt som hos Twitter og Facebook—og større tilgang for utviklere, støttet av en innovasjonspris på 50 000 dollar. Jones kommenterte ikke ryktene om et mulig samarbeid mellom MySpace og Facebook. Lederne ønsket ikke å diskutere inntekter fra nettstedene eller rykter om børsnoteringer. YouTube-medgründer Chad Hurley, hvis selskap eies av Google, ville heller ikke dele inntektstall, men fortalte at noen innholdsprodusenter har tjent over én million dollar siden annonsering ble innført. Hurley sa: «Vi innførte ikke annonsering med en gang fordi vi ikke ville endre hvorfor folk la ut videoer. Vi ville bygge et videofellesskap.» Han la til: «Etter hvert forsto vi at annonsering kunne gi sikre inntekter uten å endre hvem vi er, og det har fungert bra.» Hurley understreket at det ikke finnes noen oppskrift på virale suksesser. «Du kunne slått meg i ansiktet nå, og fått mange visninger,» spøkte han. «Noe sjokkerende får ofte oppmerksomhet, men det finnes ingen magisk oppskrift. Det viktigste er at alle kan delta.» Utenfor scenen dreide mye av diskusjonen seg om konkurransen mellom Facebook og Twitter, samt trenden med å åpne data for apputviklere. Deltakerne diskuterte også hvor uforutsigbar suksess på internett kan være. Katrin Weber fra Deutsche Telekom bemerket: «Det er interessant at alle nå annonserer priser og konferanser, men hva skjer videre? Hvem vil til slutt vinne? Folk leter etter suksessformelen—hvorfor lykkes noen apper og plattformer, mens andre mislykkes?» SoMe-rådgiver Vero Pepperrell kommenterte: «Jeg er glad for at Twitter anerkjenner hvilket økosystem de har med utviklerne sine—de gjør noe riktig.» Blogger Gabriel Jorby mener Square, Dorseys kredittkort-enhet, signaliserer en trend mot å kombinere nett- og fysiske opplevelser. «Hvis du vil tilby en tjeneste, må du ha noe som kobler til den virkelige verden. Du kan ikke bare stole på en nettapp; det må være noe håndfast. Det er fremtiden—ikke bare det som skjer på skjermen.» Over 2 000 deltakere fra 46 land var ventet på Le Web, noe som gjør det til et av Europas største teknologimøter.

article_content: Jack Straw, the former UK foreign secretary, is facing legal action from Abdel Hakim Belhadj, a Libyan military commander, over allegations that he personally authorized Belhadj's illegal rendition to Libya in 2004. Lawyers for Belhadj have confirmed that legal documents have been served on Straw, who was a Labour MP at the time. Belhadj claims he and his wife, Fatima, were detained while transiting through an airport en route to Britain, where they sought asylum, and were subsequently returned to Libya, then under the rule of Muammar Gaddafi. Belhadj alleges he and his wife were imprisoned and tortured upon their return. The case seeks to examine Straw's role in the rendition and to claim damages for the alleged trauma caused. Belhadj’s lawyers, Leigh Day & Co, have asked Straw to provide documents they believe may be relevant, including those mentioned in a Sunday Times article, as well as personal notes, diaries, and memoirs from March 2004 onward. Sami Al Saadi, another Libyan dissident who claims to have undergone a similar experience, is also pursuing legal action against Straw. Belhadj, notably a prominent figure in the uprising that toppled Gaddafi in 2011, is already suing the Foreign Office and MI6. He alleges torture by Gaddafi's regime after being rendered to Libya via the British territory of Diego Garcia. The Metropolitan Police are investigating these claims. British ministers have insisted there was no complicity in rendition or torture. A recent Sunday Times report suggested that Straw had been confronted by MI6 about his alleged involvement. Sapna Malik, a partner at Leigh Day & Co, emphasized the need for accountability through the chain of command and called for Straw to clarify his role. Cori Crider, legal director at Reprieve, stated that it now appears clearer who authorized Britain’s involvement in the rendition, urging Straw and the government to be transparent and to apologize to the victims and their families. Crider also criticized the government’s continued refusal to confirm or deny their role, emphasizing the need for full public examination. A government spokesperson from Downing Street noted that the administration is examining the legal action closely but declined to comment on specifics, reiterating the UK's clear position against torture and its commitment to ensuring fair legal proceedings in such cases.

Advokatene til Belhadj har bekreftet at juridiske dokumenter har blitt overlevert til Straw, som var Labour-parlamentsmedlem på den tiden. Belhadj hevder at han og kona Fatima ble pågrepet mens de mellomlandet på vei til Storbritannia, der de søkte asyl, og deretter sendt tilbake til Libya, som da var under Muammar Gaddafis styre. Belhadj påstår at både han og kona ble fengslet og torturert etter hjemkomsten. Saken har som mål å granske Straws rolle i utleveringen og kreve erstatning for den påståtte traumatiske behandlingen. Belhadjs advokater, Leigh Day & Co, har bedt Straw om å legge frem dokumenter de mener er relevante, inkludert de som er nevnt i en artikkel i Sunday Times, samt personlige notater, dagbøker og memoarer fra mars 2004 og senere. Sami Al Saadi, en annen libysk dissident som sier han har opplevd det samme, fremmer også sak mot Straw. article_content: When Hyacinth Alia became Governor of Benue State, his administration discovered the treasury was empty. The previous government had claimed the state’s debt was N187bn, but a thorough review revealed a debt burden closer to N359bn, spanning both state and local government liabilities, including outstanding salaries and contractor payments. Finance Commissioner Michael Oglegba outlined that the current government is committed to honestly presenting the state's financial challenges. High debt levels threaten the state’s creditworthiness and discourage potential investors. To prevent worsening the situation, Governor Alia’s team has halted all new borrowing and refrained from purchasing official vehicles or incurring non-essential costs. Despite financial constraints, the government continues to pay salaries and gratuities and is working to enhance welfare for medical staff, including prompt payment of hazard allowances. The state wage bill has been a major concern. The previous administration listed monthly salary obligations at N7–8bn, while actual revenues hovered around N6bn. This mismatch left little room for capital investment. A payroll audit revealed many 'ghost workers'—people receiving state salaries without actually working or being present. Removing these fraudulent entries has already saved N1.2bn, with further corrections ongoing. The administration is reviewing previous loans to trace how the borrowing was utilized. Some loans were tied to specific projects, but full financial transparency is still a work in progress. The government is conducting this review with the focus on governance, not politics. To secure public funds, all state accounts were temporarily frozen for auditing. An investigation revealed the presence of over 600 accounts, far exceeding the 25 initially disclosed. A special committee has been recovering government vehicles and assets taken out of service in breach of regulations. This aims to ensure all state property is properly accounted for. Through these reforms, the administration strives to rebuild trust and achieve transparent, accountable management of Benue State’s finances.
translated_content: Da Hyacinth Alia tiltrådte som guvernør i Benue-delstaten, oppdaget administrasjonen at statskassen var tom. Den forrige regjeringen hevdet at gjelden var på 187 milliarder naira, men nærmere undersøkelser viste at gjelden snarere var rundt 359 milliarder naira, fordelt på både stat og lokale myndigheter, inkludert utestående lønn og kontraktsforpliktelser. Finanskommissær Michael Oglegba forklarte at dagens regjering er opptatt av å være ærlige om statens økonomiske utfordringer. Høy gjeld kan skade statens kredittverdighet og skremme bort investorer. For å unngå å forverre situasjonen, har guvernør Alias team sluttet å ta opp nye lån og unngår å bruke penger på nye tjenestebiler og andre unødvendige utgifter. Til tross for økonomiske utfordringer betaler staten fortsatt lønninger og pensjoner, og arbeider for å bedre velferden til helsepersonell, inkludert rask utbetaling av risikotillegg. Statens lønnsutgifter har vært en stor utfordring. Forrige administrasjon rapporterte månedlige lønnskostnader på 7–8 milliarder naira, mens inntektene var rundt 6 milliarder. Dette ga lite rom for investeringer i utviklingsprosjekter. En gjennomgang av lønningslistene avslørte mange «spøkelsesarbeidere»—personer som mottok lønn uten å faktisk jobbe. Å fjerne disse har allerede spart staten 1,2 milliarder naira, og opprydningen pågår fortsatt. Regjeringen gransker nå tidligere lån for å spore hvordan pengene ble brukt. Noen lån var knyttet til spesifikke prosjekter, men full oversikt og åpenhet er fortsatt under arbeid. Fokus er god forvaltning og ikke politikk. Alle statlige bankkonti ble midlertidig frosset for revisjon. Det ble avdekket over 600 konti, langt flere enn de 25 som først ble oppgitt. En særskilt komité jobber med å hente inn statlige biler og eiendeler som har vært tatt ut av bruk i strid med reglene. Dette skal sikre at statens ressurser er under kontroll. Med disse reformene ønsker administrasjonen å bygge opp tillit og sikre åpen og ansvarlig økonomistyring i Benue.

article_content: The UK Government is considering expanding a fuel duty discount for motorists living in rural areas. Currently, a 5p per litre reduction is available for drivers in the Scottish islands and the Isles of Scilly. Now, plans are underway to extend this scheme to remote parts of mainland Britain, such as Devon, Cornwall, Herefordshire, North Yorkshire, and Wales, to help combat higher fuel prices that arise from increased transportation costs to these regions. However, AA President Edmund King has warned that introducing this subsidy on the mainland could create a 'postcode lottery.' He explained that, while island communities have no choice but to use their local petrol stations, designating certain zones on the mainland may unfairly impact stations just outside the supported areas, making the scheme 'very difficult' to implement. Under the proposed plan, remote area fuel retailers could benefit from a cut in duty from 53p to 48p per litre. The savings are intended to be passed on to customers, supporting rural economies. To be eligible for the rebate, rural petrol stations must charge above 139p per litre for petrol or 145.5p per litre for diesel. Despite support for the initiative, some rural drivers in areas like Suffolk, Norfolk, and Pembrokeshire have expressed concern that their regions may not qualify. King noted that price differences of 5p per litre already exist in some places, and he called for greater pricing transparency, including the publication of wholesale fuel prices, as is done in other countries. As the subsidy is classified as state aid, government ministers must seek approval from the European Commission, demonstrating that the scheme does not breach competition laws. While similar discounts have been approved for various European islands, extending the scheme to parts of mainland Britain adds complexity. At present, the rebate applies to petrol stations in the Scottish Inner and Outer Hebrides, Northern Isles, Islands of the Clyde, and the Isles of Scilly, allowing for a relief of 5p per litre. Over the next five weeks, the government intends to collect pump prices from 1,500 retailers in 36 remote areas. This data will support their case to the Commission for expanding the programme. Chief Secretary to the Treasury, Danny Alexander, emphasized the importance of the rebate in helping communities where driving is a necessity, not a choice. He urged local areas that may meet the criteria to provide information to strengthen the government's application. Although the scheme’s expansion is expected to cost millions of pounds and may prove challenging to gain approval, Alexander stressed his commitment to seeing it through.
translated_content: Den britiske regjeringen vurderer å utvide avgiftsreduksjonen på drivstoff for bilister som bor i distriktene. For øyeblikket får sjåfører på de skotske øyene og Scillyøyene 5 pence billigere drivstoff per liter. Planen er nå å utvide ordningen til avsidesliggende deler av fastlands-Britannia, som Devon, Cornwall, Herefordshire, North Yorkshire og Wales, for å motvirke de høyere drivstoffprisene som skyldes økte transportkostnader til disse områdene. AA-president Edmund King har imidlertid advart om at innføring av denne subsidien på fastlandet kan føre til et «postnummerlotteri». Han forklarte at øysamfunn ikke har andre alternativer enn sine lokale bensinstasjoner, men at utvelgelse av enkelte soner på fastlandet kan ramme stasjoner rett utenfor støtteområdene, noe som gjør ordningen «svært vanskelig» å gjennomføre. I det foreslåtte opplegget kan drivstoffselgere i avsidesliggende områder få redusert avgiften fra 53 pence til 48 pence per liter. Besparelsene er ment å komme kundene til gode og støtte distriktenes økonomi. For å kvalifisere seg til refusjonen må bensinstasjonene ta mer enn 139 pence per liter bensin eller 145,5 pence for diesel. Til tross for støtte for tiltaket, har noen sjåfører i distrikter som Suffolk, Norfolk og Pembrokeshire uttrykt bekymring for at deres områder ikke vil kvalifisere. King bemerket at prisforskjeller på 5 pence per liter allerede eksisterer flere steder, og han etterlyste større prisåpenhet – inkludert offentliggjøring av engrospriser, slik som i andre land. Fordi subsidien defineres som statsstøtte, må regjeringen få godkjenning av EU-kommisjonen og vise at ordningen ikke bryter med konkurranselovene. Lignende rabatter er allerede godkjent for ulike europeiske øyer, men utvidelse til deler av fastlands-Britannia gjør det mer komplisert. For tiden gjelder rabatten for bensinstasjoner på de skotske indre og ytre Hebridene, Nordøyene, øyene i Clyde samt Scillyøyene, og gir 5 pence avslag per liter. De neste fem ukene skal regjeringen samle inn drivstoffpriser fra 1 500 forhandlere i 36 avsidesliggende områder for å styrke søknaden til EU-kommisjonen. Finansminister Danny Alexander understreket hvor viktig ordningen er for lokalsamfunn der bilkjøring er en nødvendighet, ikke et valg. Han oppfordret relevante områder til å bidra med informasjon som kan styrke regjeringens sak. Selv om utvidelsen av ordningen kan koste flere millioner pund og blir utfordrende å få godkjent, understreket Alexander sitt sterke engasjement for å få det til.

article_content: Connections is a new puzzle game from The New York Times that invites you to organize 16 words into four hidden groups, discovering how each set is connected. Every day brings a new puzzle at midnight, and the level of challenge may change daily. Much like Wordle, the game tracks your streak and lets you share results with friends, turning puzzle solving into a social event. At the start, you’ll face a grid of 16 words. Your mission: sort them into four groups of four by figuring out what links them. These categories can involve anything from video game franchises and series sequels to colors or restaurant chains. Some words might appear to fit several themes, but there’s only one right solution. To help spot relationships, you can shuffle and rearrange the words in the grid. The four groups are color-coded by difficulty: yellow (easiest), green, blue, and purple (most challenging). Pick your four, hit Submit—if you’re correct, those words disappear, and the link is revealed. Each incorrect attempt counts as a mistake, and you’re allowed up to four errors before the game ends. If things get tough, you can check hints or even see the answers. There’s a new Connections puzzle every day, so if you miss today’s, you’ll have another chance tomorrow.

Hver dag lanseres en ny oppgave ved midnatt, og vanskelighetsgraden kan variere. Akkurat som i Wordle kan du følge med på seiersrekka di og dele resultater med venner, så det blir morsomt å konkurrere sammen. Når du starter, får du et rutenett med 16 ord. Målet ditt er å sortere dem i fire grupper på fire ved å finne ut hva som binder dem sammen. Gruppene kan handle om alt fra videospillserier og bokoppfølgere til fargenyanser eller kjederestauranter. Noen ord ser kanskje ut til å passe flere steder, men det finnes bare én riktig løsning. For å oppdage sammenhenger kan du stokke om på ordene i rutenettet. Gruppene er fargekodet etter vanskelighetsgrad: gul (lettest), grønn, blå og lilla (vanskeligst). Velg fire ord, trykk på «Send inn» – hvis du har rett, forsvinner de fra brettet, og temaet avsløres. Hver feil gir en bommert, og du kan gjøre opptil fire feil før spillet avsluttes. Blir det vanskelig, finnes det hint og svar du kan bruke. Det kommer en ny Connections-utfordring hver dag, så går du glipp av dagens, får du en ny sjanse i morgen.

article_content: FREDERICKSBURG, Va. — Spotsylvania County, Virginia, known as the 'crossroads of the Civil War,' is experiencing modern conflict at school board meetings, reflecting national cultural and political divides. Heated debates and political maneuvering have replaced previous civility, especially as local elections approach. Although school board seats in Virginia are officially nonpartisan, political parties and associated groups are heavily involved in current contests. Each side seeks to shape public education, while national observers consider the results a sign of broader voter sentiment moving into 2024. Conservative groups advocate for greater parental control over education, seeking to change curriculum and policies related to library materials, equity initiatives, and support for transgender students. Opposing parents emphasize the importance of meeting diverse student needs. Public meetings have often devolved into shouting matches and disputes, prompting legal complaints and increased security measures, such as private security at board meetings. Tensions remain high, with both sides unwilling to compromise on their vision for education. Political polarization is impacting not only Spotsylvania but other Virginia counties, making school board races pivotal as debates over parental rights and educational direction intensify. Changes on the Spotsylvania school board have led to shifts in leadership, policy decisions like book removals, and the resignation of teachers and staff, many of whom cite concerns about new policies and priorities. Despite deep divisions, some candidates and community members are calling for civility and productive dialogue. Recent forums show attempts at constructive discussion, though disagreements remain. The struggles in Spotsylvania exemplify broader national challenges in public education, as partisan politics increasingly shape the governance and climate of local schools.

Opphetede debatter og politiske manøvreringer har erstattet tidligere sivilitet, spesielt når lokalvalg nærmer seg. Selv om skolestyrer i Virginia offisielt er partipolitisk uavhengige, er politiske partier og tilknyttede grupper tungt involvert i de nåværende kampene. Begge sider ønsker å forme offentlig utdanning, mens nasjonale observatører ser resultatene som en indikator på bredere velgerstemning foran 2024. Konservative grupper ønsker større foreldreinnflytelse over utdanningen og prøver å endre læreplaner og retningslinjer for bibliotekets innhold, likestillingsinitiativer og støtte til transkjønnede elever. Motstandere understreker viktigheten av å møte behovene til et mangfoldig elevgrunnlag. Offentlige møter har ofte utartet til krangling og tvister, noe som har ført til juridiske klager og økt sikkerhet – blant annet med privat vakthold på styremøter. Stemningen er anspent, og ingen av sidene vil inngå kompromisser om sitt syn på skolepolitikken. Den politiske polariseringen påvirker ikke bare Spotsylvania, men også andre fylker i Virginia, der skolestyrekamper har blitt avgjørende ettersom debatten om foreldrerettigheter og skolens retning tilspisser seg. Endringer i sammensetningen av skolestyret i Spotsylvania har ført til skifter i lederskap, politikk som fjerning av bøker, og oppsigelser eller utgang blant lærere og ansatte – mange med bekymring for de nye prioriteringene. Til tross for dype splittelser oppfordrer noen kandidater og samfunnsmedlemmer til sivilitet og konstruktiv dialog. Nylige fora viser forsøk på konstruktiv diskusjon, selv om uenighetene fortsetter. Uroen i Spotsylvania illustrerer bredere nasjonale utfordringer i offentlig utdanning, der partipolitikk i økende grad påvirker styringen og klimaet i lokale skoler.

article_content: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has recently conducted several major drug busts throughout Nigeria, resulting in significant seizures and arrests. One notable arrest was Sherif Egbo, a 40-year-old Spain-based businessman who was detained at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja on October 14 while attempting to fly to Paris. Authorities found he had swallowed 93 packets of heroin, totaling 2.222 kilograms, which he later expelled under observation. Egbo admitted to working in a Madrid poultry business and to involvement in drug trafficking. On October 16, NDLEA agents at Lagos's Murtala Mohammed International Airport stopped a shipment of 10 cartons containing 500,000 tablets of tramadol (225mg, branded tapentadol) that was sent from India via Qatar Airways, reportedly en route to Liberia. The seizure resulted from intelligence cooperation with Liberian officials. In another case, Ngene Chinecherem was arrested at Lagos airport while trying to smuggle 11.1 kilograms of skunk and 600 grams of tramadol hidden in foodstuffs to Oman. These drugs were confiscated. NDLEA teams assigned to courier services stopped the export of 1 kilogram of methamphetamine disguised in body cream containers to New Zealand and 2.5 kilograms of cocaine and phenacetin concealed inside a carton destined for Saudi Arabia. Additional seizures on October 18 included 112 grams of Dimethyl Sulfone hidden in a motor shaft and 583 grams of cocaine and phenacetin inside a body cream bottle, also set for Saudi Arabia. Road operations saw the discovery of an abandoned Mercedes Benz truck on the Owerri-Onitsha expressway containing 168 bags (1,854 kilograms) of skunk. Interdiction efforts in Edo state yielded 1,381.3 kilograms more, with suspects apprehended and vehicles carrying cannabis recovered. In Kano, Aminu Suleiman—a previously convicted drug offender—was arrested along with two others and 106 kilograms of cannabis were seized. Four additional individuals were caught in the same region with 75.3 kilograms of skunk. Elsewhere, Zone J Command officers collected 478 kilograms of cannabis from a forest in Ikere Ekiti, while Ondo state operatives recovered 928 kilograms in several rural locations. Borno authorities apprehended Sani Mohammed with 182 kilograms of cannabis on the Maiduguri–Damaturu road. These coordinated NDLEA operations between October 14 and 21 underscore continued nationwide action against drug smuggling.

Et spesielt oppsiktsvekkende arrestasjon var Sherif Egbo, en 40 år gammel forretningsmann bosatt i Spania, som ble stoppet på Nnamdi Azikiwe internasjonale lufthavn i Abuja 14. oktober da han forsøkte å fly til Paris. article_content: Bayern Munich continued their relentless march at the top of the Bundesliga with a commanding 5-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt on Sunday, extending their unbeaten league run to a record 44 games. The win restored Bayern’s 13-point advantage, all but ensuring their grip on this season’s title, with the team amassing 53 points from just 19 matches. A packed Allianz Arena crowd of 71,000 was treated to another display of attacking brilliance. Mario Goetz volleyed home the opener, followed by goals from Franck Ribery before halftime, Arjen Robben after the break, then defender Dante, and finally Mario Mandzukic to wrap up the emphatic scoreline. The team, led by Pep Guardiola, look set to shift focus to the Champions League, where they face English side Arsenal in the last 16 later this month. For Arsenal, Sunday brought positive news as they returned to the top of the English Premier League through a 2-0 home win against Crystal Palace. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain marked his comeback from injury by scoring both goals in the second half at the Emirates Stadium, keeping Arsenal two points ahead of Manchester City, who face Chelsea on Monday. Liverpool, meanwhile, missed the chance to close the gap in the title chase after drawing 1-1 at West Bromwich Albion. Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger praised Oxlade-Chamberlain’s performance, especially with new loan signing Kim Kallstrom sidelined by a back injury until March, ruling him out for key fixtures including the Bayern clash. Bayern’s dominance was further underlined by midfielder Thiago Alcantara setting a new Bundesliga record with 185 touches of the ball during the match, reflecting their overwhelming control of possession. Club president and legendary former player Franz Beckenbauer stated Bayern asserted their authority from the outset and could have scored more before halftime. Elsewhere in Germany, Bayer Leverkusen beat Stuttgart to stay within 10 points of Bayern, while Borussia Dortmund sit further adrift after a vital win on Friday. In Italy’s Serie A, Juventus widened their league lead to nine points thanks to a 3-1 victory over Inter Milan, with goals from Stephan Lichsteiner, Giorgio Chiellini, and Arturo Vidal. Roma’s match against Parma was halted after just nine minutes due to adverse weather conditions, giving Juventus a chance to pull further ahead.

article_content: Bahrain has revoked the citizenship of 31 Shiite activists, marking the latest action in the government’s ongoing crackdown on opposition amid unrest in the Persian Gulf kingdom. State-run Bahrain TV announced the measure on Tuesday evening, quoting a statement from the Interior Ministry. The broadcast named all 31 activists, including Jawad Fairouz, a former member of parliament from the Shiite opposition group Al-Wefaq, and his brother Jalal. Other prominent opposition figures affected include Said al-Shihabi, head of the Freemen of Bahrain movement, and Ali Hassan Mushaima, son of the leader of the Al-Haq group. Three Shiite clerics—Hussein Mirza, Khaled Mansour Sanad, and Alawi Sharaf—were also included. According to the Interior Ministry, Bahrain’s Citizenship Act allows the country to revoke the citizenship of anyone deemed a threat to national security. Those impacted have the right to challenge the decision in court. Two notable local organizations, the Bahrain Youth Society for Human Rights and the Bahrain Center for Human Rights, criticized the action, saying it showed a systematic targeting of political activists, former parliamentarians, clerics, and others. They noted a lack of substantial evidence for the revocations. Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch also condemned the move. Philip Luther, Middle East and North Africa Director at Amnesty International, said the authorities’ justification was vague and may be based on the activists’ political views. He noted that making individuals stateless violates international law, urging Bahraini authorities to reverse their decision. Joe Stork, deputy Middle East director at Human Rights Watch, said the government’s action appears to disregard basic rights and argued that political dissent should not be equated with threats to national security. Last month, Bahraini authorities also banned public protests, citing the need to control violence—a move Amnesty International called a breach of free speech. Violent clashes between security forces and opposition protesters have occurred frequently since protests started in February 2011, inspired by uprisings in Tunisia and Egypt. Bahrain is ruled by the Sunni Muslim Khalifa family, while roughly two-thirds of its population are Shiite. The country holds strategic importance for the United States and hosts the U.S. Navy’s 5th Fleet. CNN’s Mohammed Jamjoom contributed to this report.

Statlig Bahrain TV annonserte tiltaket tirsdag kveld, og siterte en uttalelse fra innenriksdepartementet. Sendingen oppga navnene på alle 31 aktivistene, inkludert Jawad Fairouz, tidligere parlamentsmedlem fra det sjiamuslimske opposisjonspartiet Al-Wefaq, og hans bror Jalal. Andre fremtredende opposisjonsfigurer som ble rammet, inkluderer Said al-Shihabi, leder for Freemen of Bahrain-bevegelsen, og Ali Hassan Mushaima, sønn av lederen for Al-Haq-gruppen. Tre sjiamuslimske geistlige—Hussein Mirza, Khaled Mansour Sanad og Alawi Sharaf—ble også inkludert. Ifølge innenriksdepartementet gir Bahrains statsborgerskapslovgivning landet rett til å frata statsborgerskapet til alle som anses som en trussel mot nasjonal sikkerhet. De som er berørt, har rett til å utfordre avgjørelsen i retten. To sentrale lokale organisasjoner, Bahrain Youth Society for Human Rights og Bahrain Center for Human Rights, kritiserte tiltaket og mente dette viser systematisk målretting av politiske aktivister, tidligere parlamentarikere, geistlige og andre. De påpekte mangel på solid bevis for avgjørelsene. Amnesty International og Human Rights Watch fordømte også tiltaket. Philip Luther, regiondirektør for Midtøsten og Nord-Afrika i Amnesty International, uttalte at myndighetenes begrunnelse var uklar og kan være basert på aktivistenes politiske synspunkter. Han påpekte at å gjøre personer statsløse bryter internasjonal lov, og ba Bahrains myndigheter om å omgjøre avgjørelsen. Joe Stork, assisterende regiondirektør for Midtøsten i Human Rights Watch, sa at myndighetenes handling ser ut til å ignorere grunnleggende rettigheter og argumenterte for at politisk dissens ikke bør sidestilles med trusler mot nasjonal sikkerhet. Forrige måned forbød Bahrains myndigheter også offentlige protester, med henvisning til behovet for å kontrollere vold. Amnesty International mente dette var et brudd på ytringsfriheten. Voldelige sammenstøt mellom sikkerhetsstyrker og opposisjonelle demonstranter har forekommet hyppig siden protestene startet i februar 2011, inspirert av opprørene i Tunisia og Egypt. Bahrain styres av den sunnimuslimske Khalifa-familien, mens omtrent to tredjedeler av befolkningen er sjiamuslimer. Landet er strategisk viktig for USA og huser den amerikanske marinens femte flåte. CNNs Mohammed Jamjoom bidro til denne rapporten.
